What sets a New York City sale apart

The city is five boroughs and five counties, so the recording office and the paperwork depend on where the house stands. Manhattan is New York County, Brooklyn is Kings County, Queens and the Bronx share names with their counties, and Staten Island is Richmond County.

The Department of Finance sorts every property into one of four tax classes by use. A house of up to three units falls in Class 1, and co-ops and most condominiums go in Class 2. The city also runs its own transfer tax on top of the state's. This page concentrates on houses rather than co-op shares.

Who owns homes in the city

Fewer than a third of households own. Owners are 32.8 percent of the 3,334,088 households, a typical owned home is valued at $777,600 and a typical rent is $1,821. Population is 8,584,629, down 2.5 percent from 2020, and workers spend 40.3 minutes getting to their jobs.

In a renter-heavy city, houses are a modest slice of the market, and the boroughs behave differently. Staten Island is the most suburban. The Bronx is the only borough on the mainland. Queens is the largest by area, Brooklyn has the most residents, and Manhattan is the smallest and densest. If your house sits near a subway stop or commuter rail line, lead the listing with that.

Property tax classes and due dates

Each tax year runs July 1 through June 30, and a bill reflects the property's tax class and assessed value. A property assessed at $250,000 or less is billed four times a year, and one above that is billed twice.

New York City tax classes and rates for tax year 2026
Tax classWhat it coversRate for tax year 2026
Class 1Most residential property of up to three units19.843%
Class 2Other primarily residential property, such as co-ops and condos12.439%
Class 3Property with gas, telephone or electric company equipment11.108%
Class 4All other property, such as offices and warehouses10.848%

Quarterly bills come due on the first of July, October, January and April, each with a grace period to the 15th. Twice-a-year bills fall on July 1 and January 1. Paying the whole year by the July due date earns a 0.50 percent discount, and interest on late balances compounds daily. If a bill is still open when you sell, ask your closing attorney how it will be handled at closing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your New York house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Appealing your assessment

The NYC Tax Commission, an independent agency, takes the appeal. A Class 1 owner must file by March 15, while Classes 2, 3 and 4 face March 1, and late filings are denied. The Commission can lower an assessment, change the tax class and adjust exemptions.

Finance runs a separate track: a Request for Review to correct a description or clerical slip, due March 15 for Class 1 and April 1 for other classes. It does not replace an appeal, so file both when both apply.

Owners of high-value homes that are not their primary residence face a newer surcharge. It is 0.8 percent of market value on one, two and three-family houses worth $5 million or more, climbing to 1.05 and 1.3 percent at higher values. A house used as a primary residence by the owner, a tenant or a relative is exempt.

Taxes and costs at closing

A sale here stacks several taxes. On the seller's side sits the state base tax of $2 per $500 of price, plus a city real property transfer tax that is usually paid along with the other closing costs. For residential conveyances at $3 million or more, the state tacks on a further $1.25 per $500, also on the seller.

The buyer's side has the mansion tax at 1 percent from $1 million up, plus a supplemental tax between 0.25 and 2.9 percent once a residential price reaches $2 million. The city return, Form NYC-RPT, is created online in ACRIS, the Automated City Register Information System. Both parties sign it, and a late return adds 5 percent of the tax per month, capped at 25 percent.

Your attorney can quote the exact city figure, which varies with the kind of transfer and the price. A seller living outside New York State must work out the gain and pay any estimated income tax unless an exemption on Form TP-584-NYC applies.

Certificate of occupancy

The certificate states the legal use of a building, and nobody may lawfully occupy a structure until the Department of Buildings issues either a final certificate or a temporary one (TCO). A final certificate never expires, but the Department will not issue one while the property has open applications or open violations.

To obtain a final certificate, the Department requires:

  • Final construction, plumbing, elevator and electrical inspection sign-offs
  • A final building survey and an Owner's Cost Affidavit
  • No open applications and no open violations

Buildings put up before 1938 may not need one. A Letter of No Objection from the borough office can document their legal use. Search your address in DOB NOW to see whether a certificate is on file.

Buyers are urged to close on a final certificate, since an expired and unrenewed TCO can make a house hard to insure, sell or refinance. If you finished a basement or built an extension without closing out the job, a cash buyer taking the house as-is will price that in, so resolve or disclose it before accepting an offer.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy New York houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps for a quick house sale

Begin by finding out which tax class and county apply, then look up your certificate of occupancy in DOB NOW. Request a payoff letter from your lender and ask your attorney which transfer tax forms your sale needs. Compare offers on what you keep after the state tax, the city tax and any open balance. A cash buyer can take a house with open items and close without an appraisal. That helps when a missing certificate or an old violation would otherwise stall a mortgage.

Allow time for the paperwork that is specific to this city. The city transfer tax return is built online in ACRIS and signed by both sides, and a late return adds 5 percent of the tax per month, so ask your attorney to file it on the closing date. If you live outside New York State, check whether you owe estimated income tax on the gain. Keep the final closing statement, the recorded deed and the tax forms together for your records.

Frequently asked questions

On what dates do New York City property tax bills come due?

July 1 and January 1 for twice-a-year payers. Quarterly payers also owe on October 1 and April 1, with a grace period running to the 15th.

What is the 2026 tax rate for a one-family house in the city?

The Class 1 rate is 19.843 percent. Class 1 covers most residential property of up to three units, so a one-family house falls in it.

How long do I have to appeal my house assessment?

Until March 15 for Class 1, filed with the NYC Tax Commission. Owners of Class 2, 3 and 4 property must file by March 1.

Who bears the state transfer tax in a city sale?

The seller pays the base $2 per $500 unless the contract says otherwise. The buyer pays the mansion tax when the price is $1 million or more.

Is a certificate of occupancy required to sell?

Not always. A house built before 1938 may lack one, and a Letter of No Objection from the Department of Buildings can show its legal use. For anything newer or altered, expect the buyer's attorney to ask.

Selling in Hempstead?

Three ways to sell a Hempstead house

You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or sell straight to a buyer who accepts the house with its flaws. The house's condition and your deadline should decide it.

About four in five Hempstead homes are owner-occupied, so your house competes with many similar ones on nearby blocks. If the roof, boiler and kitchen are sound, a listing aimed at a mortgage buyer tends to win the highest price. A house that needs heavy work, carries an estate problem or has a tenant who won't leave may lose that advantage to repair bills and waiting.

  • Agent listing: a commission, weeks of showings and a buyer whose lender must approve the loan, in return for the biggest pool of bidders.
  • Owner-run sale: your attorney drafts the contract while you handle photos, pricing and open houses.
  • Direct as-is purchase: little preparation, few contingencies and a date you help set, offset by a discounted price.

Ask each bidder to put the number, the date and the proof of money on paper, then subtract every cost to see what actually reaches you.

Which communities are in the Town of Hempstead

Hempstead takes up the southwest of Nassau County on Long Island, and no other town in New York State has more people. Its western boundary meets Queens. It contains 22 incorporated villages and 38 hamlets. Villages include Freeport, Garden City, Rockville Centre, Valley Stream, Lynbrook and the Village of Hempstead itself, while hamlets include Levittown, Baldwin, Oceanside, Uniondale, East Meadow and Wantagh. The village or hamlet is the first thing a buyer asks about, and the mailing address may say only Hempstead or a neighboring name, so spell it out.

Commuting runs on rail and parkways. The Long Island Rail Road crosses the town on a Main Line and Hempstead, West Hempstead, Babylon, Far Rockaway and Long Beach branches, and Nassau Inter-County Express buses fill in between stations. The Southern State, Meadowbrook and Wantagh parkways carry car traffic. If the house is a short walk from a station, lead with that in the listing.

Housing figures for Hempstead owners

Nearly 796,000 people live in the town, in about 250,600 households of roughly three people each. The estimate for 2025 is 795,734 residents and 250,622 households. Owners live in 82.2% of homes. The median owner-occupied home is worth $640,800, median monthly owner cost with a mortgage is $3,657, median rent is $2,101, median household income is $141,243, and the average trip to work takes 36.6 minutes.

With owner costs that high, taxes weigh heavily on buyers. If your own bill runs lower than similar listings nearby, say so early.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Hempstead house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Property tax due dates

The Town of Hempstead Receiver of Taxes collects general and school taxes in four steps through the year. The same office collects for Nassau County, the town, 99 special districts and 33 school districts.

Hempstead tax installments and penalty-free windows
InstallmentDueNo penalty through
First-half general taxJanuary 1February 10
Second-half school taxApril 1May 10 (at the Receiver's office through May 31)
Second-half general taxJuly 1August 10 (at the office through August 31)
First-half school taxOctober 1November 10

The next general-tax installment becomes due on January 1, 2027. The Receiver of Taxes is at 200 N Franklin Street, First Floor, Hempstead, NY 11550, open weekdays from 9 am until 4:45 pm, phone 516-538-1500. A buyer's attorney will want a printout of what is paid and what is still open on your parcel.

Challenging your assessment before you sell

Yes, it can be done before a sale. Nassau County runs assessment appeals through its Assessment Review Commission, and the next window runs from January 4, 2027 to March 1, 2027. Filing costs nothing and you don't need an attorney.

The commission can lower an assessment but never raise it. It also corrects a wrong tax class and reviews cases where an exemption was denied. Set the county's adjusted market value for your house beside your own sense of its sale price, and appeal if yours is clearly lower. If you file, tell the buyer an appeal is pending.

One warning: sign no more than one authorization for a grievance service, and don't file for yourself if you already authorized a representative, because duplicate applications left unresolved are denied. The office is at 240 Old Country Road, 5th Floor, Mineola, NY 11501, phone 516-571-3214, open weekdays until 4:30 in the afternoon. The window opens after the new year, so a listing that closes this fall can't use it.

Permits and the Department of Buildings

The Town of Hempstead Department of Buildings enforces the building, plumbing, electrical and housing codes, along with the rules for how land and buildings are used and occupied. It is at One Washington Street, 2nd Floor, Hempstead, NY 11550, phone 516-538-8500, with a front counter open from 8 am to 4:45 pm. Permits and forms go through the town's Online Permit Center. Housing and Zoning Inspectors take calls at 516-812-3289 from 9 am to 10:30 am, before they leave for field inspections.

Before you list, ask the department what permits are on file for any addition, finished basement, deck or second kitchen. A buyer's attorney will find work that was never permitted, and clearing it up before a contract is signed is quicker than doing it under a closing deadline.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Hempstead houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax and deed recording

Expect to owe $2 for each $500 of the price, with any leftover part of $500 counted as a full unit, unless your contract shifts that cost to the buyer. The tax is reported on Form TP-584 and filed where the deed is recorded. Sales of residential property at $1 million or more also trigger a separate 1% charge, and the buyer pays it.

The Nassau County Clerk records Hempstead deeds and maintains the official index of who owns real property in the county, with land documents searchable online. In most sales your attorney or the title company files everything for you.

Checking a cash offer on a Hempstead house

Judge an offer by what lands in your account, not by the headline price. A smaller offer with no repairs, no showings and a short fuse can leave you even with a bigger listing that carries commission and fix-up costs.

  • Insist on a written offer that names the closing date and shows proof of funds.
  • Settle who bears the transfer tax and the other closing costs before you sign.
  • Let your attorney read the contract, and confirm the deed goes to the Nassau County Clerk.
  • Call the Receiver of Taxes about any open installment so it is cleared at closing.
  • Line up two or three bids, plus an agent's estimate of a listing price.

Frequently asked questions

Which office takes property tax payments in Hempstead?

The Town of Hempstead Receiver of Taxes does, from an office on North Franklin Street. It takes county, town, special district and school district payments, and 516-538-1500 reaches it.

Is the Village of Hempstead the same as the Town of Hempstead?

No. The village is one of 22 incorporated villages inside the much larger town, which also holds 38 hamlets such as Levittown and Uniondale. Name the exact village or hamlet when you describe your house to a buyer.

When can I file an assessment appeal in Nassau County?

The next window runs from January 4, 2027 through March 1, 2027. The county's Assessment Review Commission takes the filing free of charge and can only reduce an assessment.

Who pays the New York transfer tax when a house sells?

The seller, unless the contract says otherwise. The buyer is responsible for the extra 1% that applies once a residential price reaches $1 million.

Which office handles building permits in Hempstead?

The town's Department of Buildings, at One Washington Street in Hempstead, phone 516-538-8500. Applications go through its Online Permit Center.

Selling in Brookhaven?

Brookhaven housing at a glance

Brookhaven is a very large Suffolk County town on Long Island. A sale depends first on which hamlet or village the house is in, then on three offices: the Town Assessor, the Town Building Division and the Suffolk County Clerk. The 2025 estimate is 496,410 residents, up from 485,773 counted in 2020.

The median owner-occupied home is worth $489,200, and 80.9% of homes are owner-occupied. The town has 166,521 households averaging 2.85 people. Owners pay a median of $3,101 a month with a mortgage and $1,377 without one, and median gross rent is $2,314. About 91.7% of residents kept the same address over the past year, so the typical owner has been in place a long time and often holds large equity.

Villages, hamlets and commuting

The town reaches from Long Island Sound on the north to the Atlantic on the south and takes in part of Fire Island. It includes eight incorporated villages and roughly 50 hamlets.

  • Port Jefferson and Stony Brook: Port Jefferson is a downtown and the ferry terminal for Bridgeport, Connecticut, and Stony Brook is home to the university. Setauket, where the town began, sits between them.
  • Patchogue, Bellport and Mastic-Shirley: South Shore communities on the Great South Bay side, served by the Montauk Branch of the railroad.
  • Farmingville, Medford and Yaphank: inland hamlets.

Mean travel time to work is 32.3 minutes, and many buyers choose a house by its Long Island Rail Road station. Three lines cross the town: the Main Line, with stops at Medford and Yaphank; the Montauk Branch, with Patchogue, Bellport and Mastic-Shirley; and the Port Jefferson Branch, with Stony Brook and Port Jefferson. A listing near a station should state the distance, since commuters ask.

How assessments and exemptions work

The Town Assessor's Office values more than 184,000 parcels, keeps ownership current from recorded deeds and tracks new construction, demolition and consolidation of lots. The current roll is posted on the town website along with an interactive assessment roll where you can look up property and home valuations.

The office also approves real property tax exemptions for senior citizens, people with disabilities and military service members. Applications and renewals must be filed by March 1 each year. If you are selling before the next filing date, tell the buyer's attorney which exemptions currently reduce your bill, because the buyer will need to apply on their own.

Two online services help at sale time: a Certificate of Assessment application and a radius map and list application. The Assessor's Office is at One Independence Hill in Farmingville.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Brookhaven house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What the Building Division handles

The Building Division, part of the town's Planning Department, uses a Digital Services portal, and its paper drop-off has ended. An online help form can trace older applications if you cannot find them in the new system.

  • Commercial applications, and residential ones filed by expeditors or other professional filers, go through the portal.
  • Property owners can still file their own residential applications in person on paper, as long as every plan and supporting document is 8.5 by 11 inches.
  • The Division processes accessory apartment licenses, building construction permits, certificates of existing use, chain of title requests, house rental licenses, letters of correction and the voiding of permits or licenses.

If your house has an extra unit, a finished basement or a rental license, ask the Division which of those applications applies and whether anything is open. Tell any buyer, cash buyer included, about a rental license, since the buyer will want to know.

Rental licenses and a sale

Ask the Building Division whether a house rental license or accessory apartment license is in force. A buyer will want to know, and settling the status before you list keeps the closing from stalling. A property with an extra unit and no license is a case for a quick call to the Division before any offer is accepted.

Recording a deed in Suffolk County

Deeds for Brookhaven property are recorded with the Suffolk County Clerk, whose recording unit examines each document and collects fees, mortgage tax and real estate transfer tax. The clerk will not fill out forms for you or correct a defect, so a mistake means rejection.

What a Brookhaven deed package needs at the Suffolk County Clerk
DocumentRequirement
DeedNames and street addresses of all parties (no P.O. boxes), notarized seller signature, full property description
Cover sheetSuffolk County Recording and Endorsement page, legal size
RP-5217Real Property Transfer Report, filled in online and printed on legal paper
TP-584Transfer tax return, with Social Security or federal ID numbers for all parties
IT-2663Estimated income tax form for nonresident sellers

Transfer tax applies when the price tops $500, at $2 per $500 or fraction thereof, and a 1% additional tax applies to residences at $1 million or more. The extra Peconic Bay form is only for the five East End towns, which do not include Brookhaven. Checks go to the Suffolk County Clerk, and the transfer tax needs a certified check, cash, money order or an approved attorney or title company check.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Brookhaven houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

The 1% tax at $1 million or more

Below $1 million the only transfer tax is the base rate of $2 per $500, which the seller pays. At $1 million or more the buyer adds a 1% tax on the full price. Mention it early if your house is near that line, since it affects how a buyer frames an offer.

Getting your paperwork in order

Gather these before you accept an offer. Pull your Certificate of Assessment from the Assessor's online application, so the parcel details are on paper. Check with the Building Division on any open permit, rental license or accessory apartment license. Find your deed, a payoff statement from your lender and a list of the exemptions on your bill.

If the buyer is paying cash, the same folder lets them move straight to a price. If you list, it lets your attorney answer the title company without delay. In either case, the Suffolk County Clerk rejects a deed package with errors, so have the names, street addresses and signatures checked before it goes downtown.

Choosing how to sell

You can list with an agent, try to sell yourself, or accept a cash offer. With a median value near $489,200, many Brookhaven owners have enough equity to cover repairs, but time is the cost: showings, inspections and a buyer's mortgage approval.

A cash offer fits houses with old systems in Farmingville or Medford, inherited homes on the South Shore, or a property with a rental or apartment that lacks a license. Before you decide, compare the offer with what a listing would net after repairs, agent costs and carrying costs, and check your exemption status and rental license so the sale price is not the only number on the table.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where do I get a copy of my Brookhaven assessment?

Use the Town Assessor's interactive assessment roll, or the final roll posted on the town website. The office also runs an online Certificate of Assessment application. Visit One Independence Hill in Farmingville if you prefer an in-person answer.

When do I file for a senior, disability or military exemption in Brookhaven?

Applications and renewals must reach the Assessor by March 1 each year. File before that date for the next tax year.

Do I need a house rental license to sell a rental in Brookhaven?

Ask the Building Division. It issues house rental licenses and accessory apartment licenses, and a buyer will want to know whether yours is in force. Settle the license status before you list so the closing does not stall.

Which county office records a Brookhaven deed?

The Suffolk County Clerk. The deed must carry names and street addresses of all parties, a notary acknowledgment, the RP-5217 and TP-584 forms, and original signatures. The clerk examines each package and cannot fix errors for you.

How much extra tax applies to a Brookhaven sale at $1 million or more?

A 1% mansion tax on the full price, paid by the buyer. Below $1 million the only transfer tax is the base rate of $2 per $500, which the seller pays.

Your three ways to sell in Islip

Anyone selling in the Town of Islip picks one of three routes: hire an agent, handle it solo, or accept a cash buyer's bid. All three finish at the Suffolk County Clerk, where the new deed is recorded. Hamlets differ a lot, but the paper trail is identical across the town.

Population is 340,867, up 0.3% since 2020, spread over 102,205 households of about 3.28 people each. Houses tend to come up after an inheritance, a relocation or a money squeeze. Owners in that spot need answers on repairs required before closing, taxes and fees deducted from proceeds, and how soon they need the funds.

  • Agent listing: best for a house that shows well when you can tolerate showings and a buyer's loan process.
  • Selling yourself: only sensible if you are comfortable with contract, disclosure and attorney review minus a broker.
  • Cash offer: worth it when speed, condition or a messy title or occupancy matters more than getting top dollar.

Hamlets, water and flood paperwork

Islip stretches along Long Island's South Shore in Suffolk County. Babylon is its western neighbor, Smithtown lies north and Brookhaven east, while the Atlantic forms the southern edge. Of the town's 162.8 square miles, 103.2 are land and the remainder is the Great South Bay and barrier islands.

The town spans at least 17 ZIP codes. Sayville, Brentwood and Hauppauge are different markets with different price levels, so get recent sales for your own block from an agent or appraiser rather than trusting one town-wide figure. Pieces of Fire Island, Jones Beach Island and Captree Island sit inside the town lines.

A bayfront house or one near the barrier islands brings flood-zone and insurance questions that an inland Hauppauge house will not. Pull the flood and survey paperwork early. Because the town sits low, water is the weather problem that counts. In August 2014 a record 24-hour rainfall of 13.57 inches flooded the Southern State Parkway and Sunrise Highway, and any buyer's inspector will quiz you on past water in basements or crawl spaces. Keep repair receipts and insurance claims together. Snow averages 31.8 inches a year, so roof and gutter condition are routine inspection items.

Ownership and monthly costs

Islip is mostly a town of owners. Owners hold 80.5% of housing units, and the middle owned home is worth $535,300. Household income sits at $130,132 and the average commute is 28.3 minutes. With 92.7% of residents unmoved in the last twelve months, most sales follow a life event.

A short checklist helps when you decide how fast to move. List what the house needs before a buyer's inspector walks through. Total the taxes and fees that will come out at closing. Then decide the earliest date you can realistically hand over the keys. Those three answers tell you whether a listing, a solo sale or a cash offer fits, and they give you something concrete to compare when offers arrive.

Monthly costs push many owners toward a fast exit. Owners with a mortgage pay $3,222 a month at the midpoint, and gross rent is $2,209. If you are behind on payments or paying for a second property, those months pile up while the house waits for a buyer.

Building Division and permit history

One Manitton Court in Islip houses the Building Division, which issues permits and signs them off with a Certificate of Occupancy or Compliance. A sale often goes smoothly or stalls depending on that paperwork. The Records Office schedules inspections and fields requests for surveys, permits, certificates of occupancy, building plans and inspection reports.

Did you finish a basement, build a deck or convert a garage? Make sure each permit was closed out. Gaps surface when the buyer's attorney runs a records search. Requests go through the division's online Freedom of Information form, and the Records Office line is 631-224-5470. On weekdays the front counter shuts at 4:00 pm.

  • Permit applications are filed electronically, following the division's Electronic Submittal Process flyer.
  • Inspections are booked through the Records Office, because inspectors cannot schedule them directly.
  • Applications are now reviewed under the updated NYS Uniform Code and State Energy Code.

Before you list, ask the Records Office for the file on your address and read what is in it. Finding a gap now, while you control the timeline, beats hearing about it from a buyer's attorney a week before the closing date.

The town's Map Viewer shows the zoning district of any property, which answers a buyer who wonders if a second kitchen or accessory unit is permitted.

Recording fees and transfer tax

The deed package is usually prepared and paid for at closing by your attorney or title company, but reading the line items makes the settlement statement less confusing. Recording checks go to the Suffolk County Clerk, reachable at (631) 852-2000.

Transfer tax deadlineWithin 15 days of delivering the deed

A buyer takes on the state transfer tax only if the seller is exempt or skips it. East End towns use a Peconic Bay Region Community Preservation form, and Islip is outside that group. Sellers living out of state may also need form IT-2663 filed with the deed.

When does a cash offer fit an Islip house?

Cash works best for a house needing repairs, burdened by a title or tenant problem, or facing a tight deadline. If yours is well kept and in a popular hamlet, the open market may pay more.

Compare the bid with a believable listing outcome once you subtract commission, repairs, holding costs and the wait. Insist on written figures, settle who covers transfer tax and recording, and let a New York attorney read the contract. Also ask if the buyer will close despite an open permit or absent certificate of occupancy. Those are the issues that most often move the numbers on an as-is Islip deal.

  • Inherited houses where several heirs must agree and the estate needs cash.
  • Houses with deferred repairs, storm damage or open building permits.
  • Owners facing a move, a divorce or a mortgage default who need a firm closing date.

With no mortgage approval or appraisal involved, a cash sale moves at the speed of title work and attorney review. Gather your deed, latest tax bill, permit paperwork and any survey up front, and the closing is limited mainly by how quickly signatures come back.

Frequently asked questions

Is the state transfer tax my bill when I sell in Islip?

Yes, at $2 per $500 of price. A buyer pays only if the seller is exempt or does not pay. Deliver the deed and the tax is due within 15 days.

Where is a deed for an Islip house recorded?

At the Suffolk County Clerk. Expect to supply original signatures, a notary acknowledgment, each party's full name and street address, and a legal description naming village, town, county and state. A P.O. box will not do as an address.

Can I sell an Islip house that has an open building permit?

You can, but a title search or the buyer's attorney will probably raise it. Ask the Building Division Records Office whether a Certificate of Occupancy or Compliance can close it out.

How do I get building records for my Islip house?

Use the Building Division's online Freedom of Information form, or call the Records Office at 631-224-5470. Records include surveys, permits, certificates of occupancy, building plans and inspection reports.

Does the Peconic Bay form apply to a sale in Islip?

No. Only deeds in Riverhead, Southampton, East Hampton, Shelter Island and Southold need it. Islip deeds go in with the RP-5217 transfer report and TP-584 return instead.

Villages, hamlets and your mailing address

The Town of Oyster Bay is the easternmost of Nassau County's three towns and spans from the Long Island Sound shore to the South Shore, roughly 169.5 square miles with about 38 percent of that water. Inside it are 18 villages and 18 hamlets, served by 20 post offices and 30 ZIP codes. Post office names match those places, but the boundaries usually do not, so the town on your mailing address may not be the village or hamlet your lot sits in.

Begin with the section, block and lot printed on your tax bill, then ask the town whether your house is inside a village. That answer decides which offices handle permits and local rules for your property.

Owners and prices

The town had 301,115 residents in July 2025, living in 100,559 households. About 89.1 percent of homes are owner-occupied, the typical owned home is valued at $708,600, and median rent is $2,572 a month. Owners with a mortgage have a median monthly cost of $3,910, and median household income is $160,126. Since 93.3 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, listings are not plentiful.

With owners in nearly nine of ten homes, most sellers have a mortgage to pay off. Request a payoff figure from your lender early so the number is ready when you take an offer.

Receiver of Taxes: bills, due dates and penalties

Two bills come each year, a school bill mailed in October and a general bill mailed in January, and each splits into halves. Owners with an escrow account have the bills sent to their lender.

Oyster Bay tax payment windows
BillDuePaid without penalty through
General tax, first halfJanuary 1February 10
General tax, second halfJuly 1August 10
School tax, first halfOctober 1November 10
School tax, second halfApril 1May 10

A late payment picks up a 1 percent monthly penalty, counted back to the original due date. Collection closes on May 31 for school bills and August 31 for general bills, and after that unpaid amounts move to the Nassau County Treasurer. The word Arrears in the upper left corner of a bill means that has happened. Payments are taken at Town Hall North in Oyster Bay and Town Hall South in Massapequa, by mail and online. Only a United States Postal Service postmark proves a mailed payment arrived on time.

A new owner should write to the Receiver so the next bill goes to the right address. Banks, title companies and attorneys paying on someone else's behalf owe a $10 duplicate bill fee with each payment, a point to raise when the closing statement is drafted.

Filing an assessment complaint

Complaints go to Nassau County, and the deadline is March 1. The county's Assessment Review Commission meets through the year but accepts complaints only until that date. Ask the commission for forms and instructions. This is a different calendar from the spring Grievance Day that town boards hold in much of New York.

Home improvements can change an assessment through the Nassau County Department of Assessment in Mineola. If you added a dormer, finished a basement or built a deck, a buyer's tax bill may end up different from yours, so ask the county for the figure on file and compare it with the work you did.

What the Nassau County Clerk requires to record a deed

The clerk's office is at 240 Old Country Road in Mineola. Its Land Recording Guide puts the property's section, block and lot first. A missing or invalid number is the most common reason for rejection, and the clerk does not check it, so copy it from the current county tax bill.

  • Documents must be notarized, legible and signed in original ink, with party names matching exactly between the heading and the acknowledgment.
  • Post office boxes are not accepted as addresses.
  • Transfer tax goes by certified check; recording fees can go by personal check or Visa or MasterCard.
  • Present documents at least an hour before the closing.
  • Three approved companies offer e-recording, which title firms and attorneys usually use.

Forms TP-584 and RP-5217 travel with the deed. A nonresident seller who owes estimated income tax on the gain files Form IT-2663 and pays that tax to the recording officer when the deed is filed. Confirm current fees on the clerk's website before the closing.

Transfer tax for an Oyster Bay seller

New York charges two dollars on every $500 of price, counting a partial $500 as whole, and the seller carries that by default. Ask the Nassau County Clerk whether any county or local charge also applies to your deed, since the state rate is only the statewide piece.

At $1 million or more for a residence, a 1 percent mansion tax falls on the buyer. Read the contract anyway, since the parties may shift the base tax, and the state makes buyer and seller jointly liable when the tax goes unpaid.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Oyster Bay houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Disclosures and permits

An owner of a house with up to four units must sign the state's seller form and deliver it ahead of the buyer's contract signature. With a long Sound and bay shoreline, the flood section gets close reading. It asks about FEMA floodplain and flood hazard zones, flood insurance, elevation certificates, earlier flood claims, sump pumps and water entering the building from storm surge or tidal inundation.

Building permits run through the town's Department of Planning and Development, which posts application forms at oysterbaytown.com/building. Before listing, write down past work such as pools, fences, generators and solar panels and confirm each was permitted. The form also asks about certificates of occupancy, and an unclosed permit is easier to fix before a contract than after.

When does a cash purchase make sense for an Oyster Bay house?

It fits when time matters more than the top price. With no buyer lender involved, the schedule rests on payoffs, the tax steps above and recording in Mineola. Have your last tax receipt, your deed and any open permit paperwork on the table before you ask anyone for a number.

Ask for the offer in writing and find out who pays each closing cost. Confirm the buyer's plan for transfer tax, since the state makes buyer and seller jointly responsible if it is left unpaid. If the sale is a quick one, call the Receiver of Taxes for a current balance so that no school or general bill is waiting in arrears when the deed is delivered.

Frequently asked questions

When is the first half of Oyster Bay's general tax due?

January 1, payable without penalty through February 10. The second half is due July 1 and payable through August 10. The school bill keeps its own calendar, with October 1 and April 1 due dates.

What happens if I miss an Oyster Bay tax deadline?

A 1 percent monthly penalty accrues, counted from the original due date. After May 31 for school bills and August 31 for general bills, the unpaid balance is payable to the Nassau County Treasurer instead of the Receiver of Taxes.

What is the deadline to challenge an Oyster Bay assessment?

March 1. Nassau County's Assessment Review Commission accepts complaints through that date, and the commission can give you the forms.

Which number must appear on a Nassau County deed?

The section, block and lot, plus a unit number for a condominium. Copy it from the current tax bill and put it on the first page. Mistakes here cause more rejected filings than any other error.

Who pays the mansion tax on an Oyster Bay house that sells for $1 million or more?

The buyer. The mansion tax is 1 percent of the price on a residence sold at $1 million or more, and the seller owes it only if the buyer fails to pay. The base transfer tax of $2 per $500 is the seller's by default.

How can I sell my house fast in Buffalo?

Three paths exist: an agent listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, or a direct purchase by a company like ours. The direct purchase moves fastest because no lender has to sign off on the buyer. Condition usually decides it. A worn two-family with deferred repairs, or a rental that failed the city's inspection, drags on a listing, while an investor can price the same house as it stands.

Buffalo housing at a glance

Renters outnumber owners in Buffalo. Only 43.0% of homes house the person who owns them, which means much of the stock is income property that must satisfy city registration rules before it can legally collect rent. The 2025 estimate is 274,613 residents, a 1.3% drop since April 2020, living in 119,630 households.

  • Median value of an owner's home: $164,200
  • Median gross rent: $1,046 a month
  • Median household income: $50,041

With values in that range, a repair bill can swallow a large share of a sale price, and a buyer will subtract it from any bid. An investor who plans to rent the house out works backward from the rent figure, so a unit that cannot yet pass inspection has to be priced lower to account for the work.

Neighborhood, address and zoning

A house's address can move its value as much as its condition does, and buyers compare neighborhoods closely. The city's Green Code, adopted in 2017, replaced zoning rules more than sixty years old. If you plan a change of use, such as turning a house into a different number of units, ask City Hall which code district applies before you spend money.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Buffalo house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Winter wear on a Buffalo house

Lake-effect snow brings heavy winters, and roofs, gutters, porches and plumbing absorb the abuse, so inspectors look at those first. If a worn roof is beyond your budget, an investor will fold the replacement into the price instead of asking you to do it.

Buffalo's Rental Registry

Rental rules in the city affect how easily a tenant-occupied house changes hands, so read them before you list.

  • Every non-owner-occupied one- or two-family house must be on the Rental Registry, whether or not it is occupied. Some three-family and mixed-use buildings are covered as well.
  • A new registration costs $100. Since January 1, 2025 the yearly fee has been $50 for a single unit and $100 for a two-unit house.
  • Registered properties are scheduled for proactive inspection and must hold a Certificate of Rental Compliance. A property that fails cannot operate as an income property, and the tenants cannot be evicted for unpaid rent.
  • Landlords certify that a house built before 1978 may contain lead hazards, and the city will refuse a Certificate of Occupancy where lead paint is a hazard.
  • The city's Lead Hazard Reduction Grant offers up to $12,000 per unit in the Upper West Side and Schiller Park neighborhoods.

The Rental Registration office is at 65 Niagara Square, Room 304, phone 716-851-5621.

Short-term rental licenses

Short-term rentals need a separate license. A stay under six months qualifies, every address needs its own license, and renewal is yearly. The license stays with the owner, so a new owner has to apply from the start. Non-owner-occupied properties also need a special use permit. The short-term rental team answers at 716-851-4077.

What a tenant means for your sale

A sale can go ahead with tenants in place. Ask the Rental Registration office whether your address holds a current Certificate of Rental Compliance. A rental that fails inspection cannot operate as an income property, and a buyer will see that on the city's records. LLCs or corporations owning rentals must also supply owner details at renewal, so check that yours is up to date.

Why inspection status drives price

Buyers of rental houses in Buffalo look at paperwork before paint. A current Certificate of Rental Compliance tells them the house can collect rent today. A missing one means they must pay for repairs, schedule an inspection and wait, all before the first tenant pays. That delay is why failed-inspection houses linger on the market and why investors discount them.

If your house is older than 1978, the lead paint certification adds one more item. A cash buyer can take a house with lead issues and fold the cost into the offer. A buyer using a mortgage may find the lender balks. Knowing which route fits you before the first showing saves weeks, and it keeps you from accepting an offer that quietly depends on a lender.

When you speak to a buyer, offer the registry paperwork first, then the tax balance, then the deed. That order answers their three biggest questions in the sequence they usually ask them.

Erie County deed costs and transfer tax

Deeds for Buffalo houses are filed with the Erie County Clerk.

Erie County Clerk charges on a residential deed
ChargeAmount
Statutory recording fee$45, plus $5 for each written page
TP-584 transfer tax form$10 to file
RP-5217 transfer report (residential or farm property)$125 to file
Transfer tax, owed by the seller$4.50 per $500 of price ($2.00 state, $2.50 county)

The clerk keeps the original deed on record and mails it back after the indexing is verified. A Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form accompanies a residential deed. The deed is signed and notarized, then filed together with the TP-584 and the RP-5217.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

City taxes before closing

Inside the city, the Department of Assessment and Taxation reviews every deed filed to update ownership records. Its tax office sends delinquent notices, helps owners set up court-ordered payment plans and runs an annual In Rem foreclosure auction, so a house with unpaid city taxes is worth sorting out before an offer is signed. Ask that office for a current balance, including sewer rent, before you close, so no unpaid charge surprises you at the table.

Steps for a fast sale

  1. Confirm whether the house is on the Rental Registry and whether its Certificate of Rental Compliance is current.
  2. Ask the tax office for a balance that includes sewer rent.
  3. Collect the deed and a mortgage payoff statement.
  4. Compare any cash offer with what a listing would net after repairs and the months you would carry the house.
  5. At closing, the deed, TP-584 and RP-5217 go to the Erie County Clerk with the fees above.

Frequently asked questions

What if tenants still live in my Buffalo house?

A sale can go ahead with tenants in place. Ask the Rental Registration office whether your address holds a current Certificate of Rental Compliance, since a rental that fails inspection cannot operate as an income property.

What does registering a Buffalo rental cost?

The first application costs $100. After that the yearly fee is $50 for one unit or $100 for two units, and LLCs or corporations owning rentals must also supply owner details at renewal.

Which side owes New York transfer tax on a Buffalo closing?

The seller does. Erie County's clerk posts a combined rate of $4.50 for each $500 of price: $2.00 to the state and $2.50 to the county.

Is a permit required for nightly stays at a Buffalo house?

A Short-Term Rental License is required for any stay under six months. The license stays with the owner, so a purchaser who wants to continue short-term renting has to file a new application.

Which office files a Buffalo deed?

The Erie County Clerk's Office. The deed is signed and notarized, then filed together with Form TP-584 and the RP-5217 report, and the clerk returns the original by mail once it is recorded.

Quick ways to sell in North Hempstead

A seller in this town has three paths: list the house, sell it without an agent, or take a direct cash offer. Which one fits depends on the repairs the house needs and your deadline. Before anything else, find out which government covers your address, since this town of about 239,000 people holds 31 incorporated villages.

North Hempstead is one of three towns in Nassau County, on Long Island, with Manhasset as the town seat. Owners hold 79.5% of the housing, and the median owner-occupied value is $888,000. Rent is $2,318 a month at the median, and household income is $158,158. With that much money in play, repairs, carrying costs and tax proration all matter. Put a listing's likely net next to a firm cash figure before choosing.

Town or village: who covers your house

When a house stands inside one of the 31 villages, the village sets its own zoning, and the town covers only the unincorporated hamlets. The town's Department of Building, Safety, Inspection and Enforcement administers State and Town codes in those unincorporated areas.

Villages include Great Neck, Roslyn, Westbury, Mineola, Williston Park, Lake Success, Sands Point and Kings Point. Town-governed hamlets include Manhasset, Port Washington, Roslyn Heights, Carle Place, New Cassel, Albertson, Herricks and Searingtown. Check your tax bill or ask the town which applies before you request permit records, because a village house needs the village hall.

For hamlet properties, the town's Inspection Section issues building, plumbing and rental permits, and the Enforcement Section investigates construction and illegal housing complaints. Applications and records live in the town's online portal, and you can phone the building department at (516) 869-6311. Open permits and illegal conversions tend to stall a financed sale, so search for them first.

The last new village, Port Washington North, formed in May 1932. The map is therefore settled, and two houses a block apart may still answer to different building departments.

Property taxes at a closing

North Hempstead has two tax levies with different years, so the split at closing depends on the closing date. The Receiver of Taxes publishes a closing guide for attorneys and title companies that explains the periods.

Levy periods in North Hempstead
LevyPeriod covered
School, first halfJuly 1 to December 31
School, second halfJanuary 1 to June 30
General, first halfJanuary 1 to June 30
General, second halfJuly 1 to December 31

The school year runs July to June, while the general levy follows the calendar year. Villages send their own bills and may use assessed values that differ from the county roll, which gives a village owner a third bill. Assessments are managed by the Nassau County Department of Assessment, and improvements made before a sale, even unreported ones, can push the value past the 6% cap.

Sellers are often surprised by two things. A buyer cannot count on inheriting your exemptions and must apply for their own. And when an exemption is removed after a sale, Nassau County may bill restored taxes, prorated, on a later bill, sometimes as long as two years afterward.

School district codes

Many districts share the town, so your bill's district code settles which one serves you. The Receiver of Taxes keeps a code list that includes Westbury, Roslyn, Port Washington, Manhasset, Great Neck, Herricks, Mineola, Carle Place and Jericho. Residency disputes are for the district or the State Education Department, and the town has no role.

Transfer tax and recording

Outside New York City the state's base transfer tax of $2 per $500 of price is the seller's cost. The TP-584 goes to the county clerk where the property is, which here means the Nassau County Clerk at (516) 571-2664.

The state also applies an additional one percent buyer-paid tax on residences priced at $1 million or more. The median home is valued at $888,000, so many sales land close to the $1 million threshold. Both the TP-584 and any tax are due by the 15th day after the deed is delivered.

If an LLC owns the house or will buy it, tell your attorney early. The state requires names and addresses of members, managers and other authorized persons when an LLC is on either side of a transfer of a building with up to four dwelling units.

Older houses and permit records

Most of the town's growth landed between 1930 and 1960, so many houses are decades old and have had additions. Check the year built on your tax record and gather permit paperwork for later work before you list or take an offer. Weather also takes a toll, with about 45 inches of precipitation and 23 inches of snow a year in Manhasset, so roofs and basements deserve a look.

Questions to ask a buyer

Whatever route you take, ask each buyer a few plain questions. Can they close without a mortgage? Will they inspect the house, and what will they do about what turns up? Who pays the title and recording costs? Which tax levy will they take responsibility for after closing? A buyer who answers clearly and in writing is usually a buyer who closes. Compare answers side by side with the net each offer leaves you after the state transfer tax and any open balance.

Also be ready for village questions. If your house is inside a village, tell buyers up front which village hall holds the permits and which bill they will receive, so the surprise does not come from their attorney. Keep a copy of every permit, tax bill and levy statement for the buyer's attorney, because speed in a closing mostly comes from complete paperwork.

What to do before you accept an offer

Work through a short checklist. Confirm whether the town or a village covers your house. Pull the permit record, since open permits and illegal conversions are what stall mortgage buyers. Request tax proration figures from the Receiver of Taxes using the closing guide. Tell your attorney about any LLC involved. Then compare offers on what you actually net: a listing may bring a higher price but adds repairs and time, while a direct cash sale can close on a date you choose and takes the house as it stands.

On closing day your attorney handles the TP-584 filing with the Nassau County Clerk, and the deed is recorded afterward. If you had STAR, remember that your buyer applies for their own exemptions; yours does not transfer.

Frequently asked questions

Does the town or the village issue permits for my North Hempstead house?

That depends on the address. The town covers unincorporated hamlets such as Manhasset and Port Washington, and each of the 31 incorporated villages handles its own zoning. Check your tax bill or call the town if you are unsure.

Which office collects the tax bill for a North Hempstead house?

The Town Receiver of Taxes collects the town's general and school taxes, and incorporated villages collect their own village taxes. Nassau County's Department of Assessment sets the assessment.

Do exemptions like STAR carry over to the buyer?

Generally no. The buyer applies for their own exemptions through the Nassau County Department of Assessment, and a buyer who purchased after January 2, 2015 may be eligible for the STAR Credit program.

Who records the deed in North Hempstead?

The Nassau County Clerk records it. The seller pays the state transfer tax of $2 per $500, and the TP-584 is due within 15 days of the deed delivery.

How do I find my school district code?

Look it up on your tax bill or in the County Assessor's property search. The town lists codes from 001 for Westbury to 315 for Jericho, and residency disputes go to the district.

The Town of Babylon fronts the Atlantic side of Long Island in Suffolk County. About 78.3% of homes are lived in by their owners, with a typical value of $522,100. Mortgage holders spend close to $3,206 monthly, and a typical rent is $2,168. Residents numbered 219,766 in 2025, across 69,085 households averaging 3.13 people.

Buyers read the tax bill closely at those costs. Much of the stock was built after the war, which means buyers will ask how old the roof and furnace are.

Villages, hamlets and what changes between them

Three incorporated villages and a long list of hamlets share the town, so an address can follow different local rules than the town name suggests.

  • Villages: Amityville in the southwest, Lindenhurst in the south and Babylon in the southeast
  • Hamlets: Copiague, Deer Park, East Farmingdale, North Amityville, North Babylon, North Lindenhurst, West Babylon, Wheatley Heights and Wyandanch

Town Hall stands on East Sunrise Highway in Lindenhurst. For a house inside one of the villages, ask the village office what it adds on top of the town's taxes and permits. Tell buyers which Long Island Rail Road station is nearest, because commuters sort listings by it.

Water, flood zones and sewer billing

More than half of the town's 114 square miles is water, and the land averages about 6.6 feet above sea level. That low ground drives insurance costs and buyer questions. Your insurance agent can tell you whether the house is in a flood zone, so ask before the listing goes live.

Sewer billing changed on January 1, when all Suffolk County sewer districts merged into the Suffolk County Wastewater Management District. Your rate or the way you are billed may differ now. Read the sewer line on your tax bill, and have the title company verify it before closing.

Tax calendar and late payment costs

Each tax year begins December 1 and finishes November 30, with a lone bill mailed near mid-December. Pay all at once or in two halves. Half one comes due in the second week of January, and half two at the end of May.

What late taxes cost in Babylon
Payment statusAdded cost

The Receiver of Taxes only collects. Budgets from the school district, county and town set the amounts, and the school portion is generally the largest. Not receiving a bill does not excuse a late payment, so ask for a copy if yours never arrived.

How to pay, and who can get a copy of the bill

Three ways to pay: online through the processor, by mailed check with the stub, or in the main hallway at Town Hall. The counter accepts cash and checks but no cards, and a drop box takes checks during business hours. A mailed payment is credited on its postmark date, though a metered postmark is not accepted.

Anyone 65 or older, or disabled, who lives in a one, two or three-family house may name a consenting adult to get duplicate bills and unpaid-tax notices. Applications are due October 1. Selling a parent's house? Check whether anyone was ever named, since an unopened bill is how many balances turn delinquent.

Exemptions

Babylon's Department of Assessment takes exemption applications until March 1 and denies late ones. Programs include Enhanced STAR, Aged, Alternative military service, Cold War service, volunteer firefighter and ambulance worker, disability with limited income, Capital Improvement, and a break for first-time buyers of a newly built home. Newcomers to Basic STAR get a state credit in place of a school tax exemption.

The exemption is tied to you, not the property. If your bill shows a senior or military exemption, it ends at the sale and the buyer's bill may go up. Say so up front.

Assessment complaints

To dispute an assessment, file Form RP-524 at no cost. The town review boards in Suffolk County meet on the third Tuesday in May, and in 2027 that is May 18. The town builds values from square footage and amenities, so check those details on your record first.

Closing costs and sale routes

New York's transfer tax is $2 per $500 of price, and it usually lands on the seller. The Suffolk County Clerk handles the TP-584 return, and the money is due inside 15 days of delivering the deed.

Third-party payers such as banks, title companies and attorneys pay a $1 duplicate tax bill fee, sent as a separate check. Plan for that when a title company clears your open tax bill at closing.

Listing ties you to the buyer's mortgage schedule. A cash buyer accepts the house as is and closes when you are ready, which helps with postponed repairs, a late tax balance or an estate. Whichever you choose, collect the deed, your newest tax statement and a payoff from the lender.

What happens at the closing table

The title company orders payoffs for your mortgage and any open tax, then subtracts them from the price. You sign the deed, the transfer tax is calculated, and the $1 duplicate bill fee goes out as its own check. The county clerk receives the TP-584 and records the deed, and you receive whatever remains. If a delinquent balance sits with the Suffolk County Comptroller, it is paid first so the buyer takes the house free of it.

Ask for a closing statement ahead of time and read each line against your payoff letters. Cash buyers can often shorten this stage because no lender needs its own conditions met.

Steps to take before you accept an offer

  1. Pull your newest tax bill and confirm both halves are paid.
  2. If the Comptroller holds a balance, request a payoff that adds in the penalty and interest.
  3. List every exemption on the house and warn the buyer which ones will end.
  4. Look up your sewer line and flood zone so the answers are ready when buyers ask.
  5. Learn how the title company plans to clear the open bill and cover the $1 fee at closing.

Also gather any paperwork on past repairs. Buyers near the water ask about basement moisture and storm damage, and a folder of receipts answers them before they turn into price cuts. If you owe a tax balance, a sale can still go forward: the title company pays it from the proceeds, which is why the payoff figure matters before you agree to a price.

These steps barely slow a cash sale. With payoff figures in hand and a clean title search, a cash buyer can set the closing date.

Frequently asked questions

When do Babylon tax payments come due?

One bill goes out in mid-December. You can split it: the first half is due in January and the second at the end of May, and a late first half adds 1% a month.

Where do Babylon taxes go after May 31?

Unpaid balances move to the Suffolk County Comptroller's Office in Riverhead. A 5% penalty applies, along with 1% monthly interest running from February 1.

Does my STAR or senior exemption pass to the buyer in Babylon?

No, the buyer must apply on their own by March 1, and expect a higher bill meanwhile.

Do Babylon sellers owe a transfer tax?

Yes. The state rate is $2 for each $500, and sellers usually pay it. File the TP-584 with the Suffolk County Clerk within 15 days after the deed.

When must a Babylon assessment complaint be filed?

Review boards in Suffolk County's towns sit the third Tuesday of May. Use form RP-524, which is free.

Owners can hire a broker, sell privately, or deal with a cash buyer who takes the house in its present condition. One cost to plan for is a city transfer tax of 1.5 percent of the price, charged to the seller above the state's own tax.

Yonkers lies in Westchester County just north of the Bronx, and it had 212,603 residents in the July 1, 2025 estimate, the most of any city in the county. Layout of the city and its quarters

The city has about 18 square miles of dry land. The Hudson River forms its western edge, the Bronx River separates it from Mount Vernon, Tuckahoe, Bronxville and Scarsdale on the east, and the Bronx begins at its southern line. The Saw Mill River splits the city into four quarters and meets the Hudson at Getty Square, the downtown and civic center.

  • Northeast: Crestwood, Colonial Heights, Cedar Knolls and Lawrence Park West, close to several Metro-North stations.
  • Northwest: Nepera Park, Runyon Heights, Homefield, Glenwood and Greystone, with Victorian houses and views of the Palisades.

Trains, highways and flooding history

Rail is a big draw. Hudson Line trains stop at Ludlow, Yonkers, Glenwood and Greystone on the way to Manhattan, Amtrak's Empire Service calls at the Yonkers station, and Harlem Line stops lie along the eastern boundary. Highway links include I-87 and the Saw Mill, Bronx River, Sprain Brook and Cross County parkways.

Flash flooding in September 2023 brought a local state of emergency, and crews pumped water from homes afterward. A basement that took water will draw questions from the buyer's inspector and insurer, so keep repair receipts.

Housing and Buildings Department files

The Department of Housing and Buildings grants building permits and certificates of occupancy, inspects work and looks into complaints. Applications are filed online through City Squared.

  • A permit to renovate an existing dwelling for one to three families requires a Home Improvement Contractor's License, which the Consumer Protection Bureau issues.
  • Property files are reviewed by appointment, so have the block and lot at hand. The department is digitizing paper records and emails a link in place of an office visit.
  • The link may arrive after the appointment date, which is a reason to ask early.

Older Yonkers houses commonly have additions and finished basements, and the file is where a buyer's attorney checks for matching permits.

Property tax bills and installments

  • Second: October 6, shifted off a weekend if needed.
  • Third: January 6, shifted off a weekend if needed. The next one is Wednesday, January 6, 2027.

Yonkers offers no grace period. Late installments earn 15 percent annual interest, figured daily from the confirmation date, and the city says it cannot forgive that interest. The envelope postmark decides whether a mailed payment was on time.

Title and mortgage companies may research parcels free online or order a Tax Office search at $5 per property per year, with a two to three week lead time. Payments go to City Hall, Room 108, at 40 South Broadway.

Print the current county and City and School bills so the buyer's attorney can see which installments are paid.

If tenants live in the house, add the leases and rent records. If the basement ever took water, add the repair receipts. With those in hand, the attorney can file the city transfer tax return the moment the deed is delivered and stay inside the seven-day window.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal and takes the house in its current condition, which spares you repairs and the wait for a bank. The city and state transfer taxes, the tax installments and the county recording still apply, so the stamped receipt and the deed paperwork are the items to line up. If timing is tight, ask your attorney to prepare the return in advance, since the city says email is the quickest way to get the stamp.

Contesting a Yonkers assessment

The Assessment Department keeps a fixed calendar, and the filing period lasts only two weeks.

  • October 15: taxable status date, and the last day to file or renew senior, disability and military service exemptions.
  • November 1: tentative roll published.
  • November 1 to 15: complaints go to the Board of Assessment Review.
  • December 15: cutoff for added information or a personal hearing request.
  • Last Monday in January to the third Friday in February: hearings.
  • April 10: final roll. Owners who protested can seek Small Claims Assessment Review through the county from April 10 to May 10.

The period closes on November 15 every year, and anyone who misses it waits twelve months.

Transfer tax and closing steps

The city tax is 1.5 percent of the selling price and falls on the seller. Sales of $25,000 or less owe nothing, and co-op units are exempt. The payment is due within seven days after the deed is handed over and before it is recorded. Seller and buyer each file a return, even if no tax is owed.

The order of steps: file the return, pay, collect the stamped receipt, then bring that receipt to the Westchester County Clerk when the deed is recorded. The city says email is quickest for getting the stamp, and mailed copies go to City Hall, Room 108.

The state adds its own base tax, and Form TP-584 goes to the county clerk within 15 days of delivery. The buyer owes a 1 percent mansion tax once a residence reaches $1 million.

The city charges 1.5 percent of the price. The seller pays the city within seven days after the deed is delivered and before it is recorded.

Wednesday, January 6, 2027, for the third installment of the 2026/27 bill. Installments fall in late July, on October 6 and on January 6 each year.

Does Yonkers add interest if a payment is a day late?

Yes. With no grace period, interest of 15 percent a year accrues from the confirmation date, figured daily, and the city says it cannot be waived.

How do I see the building file for my Yonkers house?

Book an appointment with the Department of Housing and Buildings and supply the block and lot. The department then emails a link to its paper and digital records.

Which office records a Yonkers deed?

The Westchester County Clerk does. Yonkers stamps its own transfer tax receipt first, and that receipt goes to the clerk along with the deed.

Rochester's neighborhoods and older housing

Rochester sits on the southern shore of Lake Ontario, with the Genesee River running through the city. It is the seat of Monroe County and defines 35 neighborhoods, among them Corn Hill, Park Avenue, the South Wedge, Charlotte, Browncroft, Highland Park, Dutchtown and the 19th Ward. The 2025 estimate stands at 206,108 people.

The city grew in waves, with its population topping out at 332,488 in 1950. Much of the housing built for those workers is still standing, so many sellers own a house that is a century old or more. The city's certificate of occupancy inspection checks items such as smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, outlets, handrails and porch guards, and older houses tend to fail on exactly those details.

What homes cost and who owns them

A typical Rochester home is valued at $139,600, yet just 38.1 percent of households own where they live. Renting is the norm.

  • 93,261 households averaging 2.14 people.
  • Typical rent is $1,081, and typical household income is $47,213.
  • Owners pay $1,244 a month with a mortgage and $593 without.

With values this low and renters in the majority, a Rochester seller may be a landlord, an heir to a two-family house, or an owner facing repairs. Those are the cases where a fast cash sale gets a second look.

Winter and the heat rule for rentals

Rochester gets heavy lake-effect snow, over 100 inches in an average year, which is hard on roofs, gutters, porches, furnaces and pipes. City rules also set a heat standard for rentals: owners must provide heat from September 15 to May 31 and keep it at 68 degrees minimum.

If you are selling a tenant-occupied house in the cold months, check the furnace and the heat log before a buyer's inspector does. Buyers in this market look hard at the roof, the gutters and the heating system.

Does a Rochester house need a certificate of occupancy?

It depends on who lives in the house. The city's Certificate of Occupancy program centers on rentals, and its chart assigns each property type a renewal cycle.

When a Rochester certificate of occupancy is required
Property typeCertificate required?Renewal cycle
1 or 2 family, owner-occupiedNo (may be needed if newly occupying)None

Rental units built before 1978 are covered by lead-related testing. Fees for permits, licenses and certificates change from time to time, so get a current fee from the city before you budget.

The Building Owners Registry

The Building Owners Registry is a city list on which the owner of every building must give contact details, as City Code section 90-20 requires. If the owner is an LLC, the registry asks for the names of the natural persons behind it, a rule in effect since January 1, 2024.

An updated registration is due within 10 days of any change in contact details or any sale of the property. An owner who lives outside the Rochester-area ZIP code ranges, or uses a P.O. box, must name a property manager who is a natural person with an address in Monroe County. Skipping the update after you sell can leave violations or tickets tied to your name.

Property tax installments

The City of Rochester bills for itself and the Rochester City School District in one bill, mailed each July. It is payable in four installments, due July 31, September 30, January 31 and March 31. An installment not paid by its deadline accrues interest at 1 percent per month. Monroe County charges are billed separately, and its Real Property Tax Service Office can be reached at 585-753-1125.

State law makes the owner responsible for paying on time even when a bill never arrived. If you sell in the middle of the year, check which installments are paid and have your closing attorney spell out in writing how the remaining ones will be divided.

Monroe County deed filing costs

Rochester deeds go to the Monroe County Clerk's Office, 39 West Main Street, Room 105. The land records page charges $50 for a one-page deed plus $5 per added page, $5 for the TP-584 and either $125 or $250 for the transfer report, depending on property class. A $10 charge on each residential deed has applied since March 11, 2020.

State transfer tax runs $4 per thousand dollars. To get same-day recording you need to be in line by 4:30, and the deed must carry both parties' names and addresses, a full legal description and a notary acknowledgment. The clerk's office answers at 585-753-1600.

Which sale route fits a house that must sell quickly?

An agent, a sale by owner and a cash buyer are the three routes. The condition of the house and your deadline usually decide between them.

  • Hiring an agent works best for a house that is ready to show in a neighborhood with steady interest.
  • Going solo fits an owner comfortable with the disclosure form, the contract and buyer inspections.
  • A cash buyer deserves a quote when the house has open code violations, a lapsed certificate of occupancy, tenants, an estate title problem or repairs you cannot pay for.

With any buyer, ask who takes responsibility for open code violations and whether the sale is truly as-is.

Paperwork to pull together first

Whichever route you choose, gather the documents a buyer's attorney will ask for. For a rental, that means the current certificate of occupancy and its renewal date. For any house, collect the most recent city tax bill, the county bill if you have one, and a note of the Building Owners Registry entry. If a violation notice has ever been issued, bring the closing paperwork showing how it was resolved.

With those in hand, the closing attorney can ask Monroe County for the right figures, prepare the deed and transfer forms, and file everything at the clerk's office before its 4:30 same-day cutoff.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling a tenant-occupied or distressed house

Landlords and heirs often sell with tenants in place, a lapsed certificate of occupancy or open code violations. A buyer using a mortgage will want those cleared, and that can take a long while. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, but ask in writing who is responsible for the violations after closing, and whether the price already reflects them. If the house has a certificate that needs renewing, ask the city what inspection would be required, because the renewal cycle runs three or six years depending on the property type. Finally, tell the tenants about the sale plans early so showings and inspections can be scheduled around the heat and safety checks the city expects.

Frequently asked questions

Does an owner-occupied Rochester house need a certificate of occupancy to sell?

No, not if it is a one- or two-family home you occupy yourself. A rental house needs a current certificate, and a buyer who will newly occupy a building may need one.

What happens to my Rochester tax installments if I sell mid-year?

Ask your attorney. Rochester bills in four installments (July 31, September 30, January 31, March 31), so check which ones are paid and have the attorney set out how the rest get divided.

What happens to my Building Owners Registry entry when I sell?

File a revised registration within 10 days of the sale, since the city requires an update whenever a property is sold. Bills and notices go to the owner on the Monroe County deed record.

How much snow falls in Rochester?

Just over 100 inches in an average year, much of it lake-effect snow off Lake Ontario. Expect buyers to look hard at the roof, gutters and furnace.

Where does the Rochester deed get filed?

File it with the Monroe County Clerk at 39 West Main Street, Room 105. The clerk's office answers at 585-753-1600.

Selling in Huntington?

How owners sell in Huntington

The usual choice is an agent. Some owners sell without one, and some sell outright to a buyer who takes the house in any condition. The deciding factors are the work the house needs and how long you can keep paying its bills.

Huntington sits at the high end of Long Island pricing, and nearly nine in ten of its homes are occupied by their owners. A tidy house in a district buyers ask for can attract plenty of bidders on a regular listing. A house with old systems, a probate holdup or a tenant in place may be better served by a direct sale that closes without fix-up work.

  • Through an agent: wide exposure and often the top price, set against repair costs, showings and a lender's timetable.
  • On your own: the listing fee stays in your pocket, while the contract and marketing work lands on you and your lawyer.
  • Direct as-is: a simpler and faster close with fewer conditions, priced to reflect the buyer's repair bill.

Collect each offer on paper with its closing date, proof of funds and a split of closing costs, then work out what you would really keep.

Where Huntington is and what shapes its housing

Huntington runs along Long Island's North Shore in the northwest of Suffolk County, bordered by the Sound on the north and Nassau County on the west. Four incorporated villages sit within the town: Asharoken, Huntington Bay, Lloyd Harbor and Northport. Everywhere else is a hamlet, including Huntington Station, Dix Hills, Commack, Melville, Greenlawn, Centerport, Cold Spring Harbor, East Northport, Elwood, South Huntington and West Hills. Buyers often search by hamlet or by school district rather than by the town name, so describe your house that way.

Several districts serve the town, including Cold Spring Harbor, Commack, Elwood, Half Hollow Hills, Harborfields, Huntington, Northport-East Northport and South Huntington. Roads include the Long Island Expressway, the Northern State Parkway, Jericho Turnpike (NY 25) and NY 108. The Long Island Rail Road's Port Jefferson Branch has stations from Cold Spring Harbor through Northport. A short walk to a station is worth a line in your listing.

Huntington housing figures

Roughly 206,000 people live in the town, a gain of 0.8% since the 2020 base. The 2025 estimate is 205,891 residents in 71,542 households. Owners live in 88.7% of homes. The midpoint value of an owned home is $715,600, the midpoint monthly cost with a mortgage is $3,889, rent at the midpoint is $2,358, and household income at the midpoint is $168,029. The average commute is 35.2 minutes.

Residents 65 and older make up 20.9%, so some sales come from downsizing or an estate. When the seller is an heir, collect the papers showing who may sign the deed before you take offers.

Property tax due dates and penalties

Huntington's Receiver of Taxes collects property tax from December 1 to May 31, in two halves due January 10 and May 31. The office collects for the town, the county and the school districts together, plus other taxing districts. Once January 10 passes, the unpaid first half grows by 1% per month.
