Unpaid taxes turn delinquent after May 31, and then the Suffolk County Comptroller is the one to pay. That office adds a 5% penalty and interest of 1% a month counted from February 1, and its phone is 631-852-3000. Tax payments are taken from 9:00 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays at Huntington Town Hall, 100 Main Street. Before closing, get the parcel's exact status from the Receiver or your title company so any open balance is cleared at the table.

Grieving a Huntington assessment

The complaint, signed, goes to the Town Assessor's Office by Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in May. By that rule the next one falls on May 18, 2027, and the Assessor's Office can confirm the date.

An originally signed copy is required, and faxed or emailed complaints are refused. Forms and a fact sheet with instructions are at the Assessor's Office, Room 100 of Huntington Town Hall, 100 Main Street, Huntington, NY 11743, once April 1 arrives, and they also appear on the Forms and Applications page of the town website.

Because a lower assessment benefits the next owner too, some sellers cite a pending grievance during negotiations. Gather evidence of market value, such as a recent appraisal or sales of similar houses, because the burden of showing that an assessment is too high sits with the owner.

Transfer tax and who records the deed

The state charges $2 for every $500 of price, and unless your contract says the buyer covers it, you pay. Form TP-584 reports it to the county recording officer. Residential prices of $1 million or more add a 1% charge that the buyer bears.

In Huntington the recording officer is the Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead. Its recording unit receives and examines each instrument and works out the fees, mortgage taxes and transfer taxes owed. Call 631-852-2000 with questions. Your closing lawyer or title company usually carries the deed there. You sign on time and supply a mortgage payoff letter.

Preparing a Huntington house for sale

Before offers arrive, confirm three things. First, the exact tax status of the parcel from the Receiver of Taxes or your title company, so no balance surprises you at the table. Second, which of the town's districts and hamlets you will name in the listing, since buyers search that way. Third, whether anyone besides you must sign. For an estate, bring the papers that show who may sign the deed, and for a house with a mortgage, order a payoff letter. A buyer paying cash will still ask for these, and having them ready is what keeps a quick closing quick.

Comparing a direct offer with a listing

Compare what you would keep, not what is advertised. A listing can show a bigger number, but commission, repairs, carrying costs and a financing collapse can all shrink it.

  • Ask the buyer to confirm in writing that nothing is deducted at closing beyond the costs listed in the contract.
  • Find out how long the buyer needs, since a closing date you choose may matter more than a few thousand dollars.
  • Check whether any open tax installments, a mortgage payoff or an estate matter has to be settled before title can pass.
  • Get a second opinion on value from a local agent who knows your hamlet and school district.

Frequently asked questions

What day is Huntington's next Grievance Day?

The town sets it on the third Tuesday of May, so the next is May 18, 2027. Deliver an original signed complaint to the Assessor's Office by then, since faxes and emails are refused.

Where does a Huntington tax payment go once May is over?

The Suffolk County Comptroller takes over once May 31 passes. A 5% penalty and monthly interest of 1% from February 1 are added to what is owed.

Does Huntington have any incorporated villages?

Four: Asharoken, Huntington Bay, Lloyd Harbor and Northport. The rest of the town is made up of unincorporated hamlets such as Huntington Station, Dix Hills and Commack.

Who bears the state transfer tax on a Huntington sale?

The seller does, by default. A contract can move it, and the extra 1% on residential prices of $1 million or more falls on the buyer.

Which office files a Huntington deed?

The Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead. The office records the deed and collects the fees, mortgage tax and transfer tax due on it, and its phone number is 631-852-2000.

Start by finding out who bills your house

Ramapo is a patchwork of overlapping governments. Before you list, find out which of them bills and permits your house, settle the tax and certificate questions early, and pick a buyer who can close without waiting on a lender. The first step matters because the town holds a dozen incorporated villages and several hamlets, and each village collects its own taxes.

Ramapo lies in Rockland County, with New Jersey to the south and Orange County to the west. The mid-2025 estimate is 161,564 residents, 8.5% above the 2020 base. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $653,100, and the average household has nearly four people, so extra space is in demand.

Villages, hamlets and school districts

The villages are Airmont, Chestnut Ridge, Hillburn, Kaser, Montebello, New Hempstead, New Square, Pomona, Sloatsburg, Spring Valley, Suffern and Wesley Hills. Monsey, Viola, Hillcrest, Tallman and Sterlington are hamlets, not villages. Which one your street belongs to decides who sends the tax bills and who issues permits.

  • Suffern Central School District serves the western part of town.
  • East Ramapo Central School District serves the east, including Spring Valley, Monsey, Pomona, Chestnut Ridge and New Hempstead.

The district on your parcel decides which school tax bill a buyer inherits, so name it correctly in the listing and on the disclosure form.

Housing figures for the town

Buyers will compare your house with these numbers, so it helps to know them before you set a price.

With households this large, additions and converted basements are common, and they are the usual reason a certificate of occupancy question comes up. Listing materials in more than one language can also widen your pool of buyers, since 59.0% of residents aged five and older speak another language at home.

Who collects tax, and how it plays out at closing

The Town of Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes collects school and property taxes for about 30,000 parcels, but not for the villages. Each village bills and collects separately, so a house in Airmont or Suffern has a village bill that the town does not handle.

  • County and town tax may be split into four installments for a 5% service charge. The town takes the first by January 31, and the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance collects installments 2 through 4.
  • School tax cannot be split, because the Receiver does not take partial payments on the school bill.
  • Penalties begin in October for school taxes and in February for county and town taxes.
  • Under Real Property Tax Law section 922, a bill that never arrived does not excuse lateness.

The Receiver advises anyone about to sell to skip the installment plan. It adds 5% of the bill and can muddy the closing, where the seller is credited for the unused part of the taxes. The tax office at (845) 357-5100 can supply a payoff or a tax history, and your attorney should check village bills on their own. Owners who pay off a mortgage should send the satisfaction letter to both the town and village tax offices so later bills reach the right address.

If a tax bill looks wrong or a payment runs late

An error on a bill goes to the Town of Ramapo Assessor first. The Receiver cannot change a bill alone, and a corrected one is issued only after signed Correction to the Tax Roll paperwork comes back from the Rockland County Real Property Tax Department.

Timing is strict. Only an official U.S. Postal Service postmark counts as proof of payment date, and a meter stamp does not. Checks sent through a bank's bill pay often carry no postmark, so the payment must actually arrive by the due date. Credit and debit cards work online only, with a third-party processing fee. Penalties are fixed by state law, and the Receiver cannot waive them for any reason.

Before closing, settle these points so a payment does not cross the title date: confirm what has been paid, ask whether any installment remains open, and get the school, county and town figures in writing for your attorney.

What to check with the Building Department

Building, Planning and Zoning reviews permits and supports the Planning Board and the Zoning Board of Appeals. Its page carries forms that matter for unusual properties.

  • A list of required inspections for one- and two-family dwellings, which shows the steps a permitted project must pass.
  • A Certificate of Use application.
  • A Secondary Dwelling application, for a second unit on the property.
  • A Plumbing Test Certification form.

An online Property Search tool is also available. Use it with the permit application package to compare the town's file against what stands on the lot. After a basement conversion, a new kitchen or an addition, confirm a certificate of occupancy exists, because buyers' attorneys ask and New York's disclosure form puts the same question to the seller. The department's phone is (845) 357-5100.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Ramapo houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Transferring the deed

The Rockland County Clerk receives the deed along with the TP-584 transfer tax return and the RP-5217 transfer report. The county sets recording fees, so ask the clerk for the current amounts, and ask your attorney when the TP-584 must be filed.

The state transfer tax is two dollars per $500 of price, rounded upward, and the seller usually pays it. A buyer of a residence at a million dollars or more pays a further 1% mansion tax.

The disclosure form carries its own duty. A seller of a house with up to four dwelling units signs it and delivers it ahead of a binding contract. If you later learn something that makes the form inaccurate, a revised copy is due as soon as practicable, though never after title transfers or the buyer moves in, whichever comes first.

A short checklist for Ramapo sellers

Start with the tax bills: identify the village, school district, town, county and any open installment. Then pull the certificate of occupancy and permits for every addition, finished basement or second unit. Next, decide how you want to sell. A listing reaches the widest group of buyers but depends on a buyer's mortgage and on lawyers on both sides. A cash sale leaves out the lender, the appraisal and the financing contingency, so the date depends mostly on title and paperwork.

Either way, the closing attorney will want the tax history, the disclosure form and the deed information together before the closing date is set.

Frequently asked questions

Will the Town of Ramapo's tax office bill my village taxes?

No. Each village bills and collects separately, so a house inside a village has a village bill on top of the town, county and school bills.

Is Ramapo's installment plan a good idea before a sale?

No. The Receiver of Taxes advises against it, since it adds a 5% charge and can cause problems at closing.

How do I tell which school district my Ramapo house belongs to?

The west, including Suffern, Montebello, Airmont, Sloatsburg and Hillburn, is mainly Suffern Central, and the east is East Ramapo Central. Confirm against your school tax bill.

How is the state transfer tax figured on a Ramapo sale?

It is two dollars per $500 of the price, rounded up, and the seller usually pays it. Ask your attorney to confirm who pays under your contract.

How do I learn whether my Ramapo house has a certificate of occupancy?

Try the town's Property Search tool first, then confirm with the Building Department by phone at (845) 357-5100.

Selling in Syracuse?

Which sale route suits a Syracuse house?

It depends on what the house needs and how soon you need the money. A sound house on a block with steady demand usually does best on the open market. A house with a failed inspection history, a tenant who will not leave, or a probate that has dragged on is often easier to move through a direct sale to a cash buyer.

Whichever route you take, the paperwork ends in the same place: a signed deed, a state transfer tax return, and a filing with the Onondaga County Clerk. In Syracuse there is an extra layer, because the city runs its own registries and bills taxes and water through one office. Many owners check the city side first and only then pick a buyer.

  • Open market: widest audience, but repairs, showings and a lender's appraisal set your timeline.
  • Selling by yourself: you keep the agent's share and do the pricing, contracts and negotiating.
  • Direct cash sale: the house goes as it stands, and you and the buyer agree on a date.

Get any offer in writing, then subtract taxes, water charges and recording costs to see what you would really receive.

Syracuse at a glance

Syracuse had 144,896 people on July 1, 2025, roughly 3,700 fewer than the 148,602 counted for 2020. It is the biggest city in Central New York, in Onondaga County, with about 25 square miles of land. Interstates 81 and 90 meet here, with Buffalo 150 miles to the west and Albany 145 miles to the east.

Many neighborhoods started as their own villages, so housing changes block by block: University Hill, Tipperary Hill, the Valley, Armory Square and Franklin Square each draw a different crowd. Syracuse University and SUNY Upstate Medical University drive University Hill, and Micron Technology started building a chip plant complex in the northern suburbs in 2024. A house near either campus attracts different shoppers than one on a quiet residential street, so describe your location plainly.

The Syracuse City School District covers the entire city, so a buyer who moves across town stays in one district.

Home values and who owns them

The median home value is $138,400 for 2020 to 2024, and fewer than half of households own: the ownership rate is 41.6 percent. The city has 59,816 households and a $1,039 median rent.

With roughly six in ten households renting, landlords and small investors make up much of the buyer pool, and many houses are one or two-unit buildings that fall under the city's rental rules. Tell buyers early if a tenant lives there, because they will want the lease and the rent amount.

Median household income is $47,819, which limits what many buyers can pay. Compare your house with recent sales on your own street instead of a citywide average.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Syracuse house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

City registries and certificates

The Division of Code Enforcement runs three programs under its periodic inspections rules, and each can touch a sale.

  • One or two-unit rentals: a Rental Registry Certificate and inspection every three years, or after the property is sold, at a $150 fee.
  • Three or more units, mixed use, inns, dormitories and Greek housing: a Certificate of Compliance and inspection every three years, or on a transfer of title before the sale, at $55 plus $20 for each unit above two.
  • Vacant properties with exterior code violations: registration on the Vacant Property Registry, with a certificate that lasts one year and renews while the building stays empty.
Where Syracuse sellers get answers

Assessment and exemptionsDepartment of Assessment, (315) 448-8270

State transfer tax of $2 per $500NYS Tax Department, form TP-584

If your house is a rental or has sat empty, call Code Enforcement before accepting an offer. Even a buyer who takes houses with violations needs to know which certificate applies.

Taxes or water bills behind

The City Payment Center collects city, school and county property taxes alongside water bills, and it services more than 42,000 taxpayer accounts and over 39,000 water accounts. It also chases delinquent property taxes, sells tax-delinquent properties, and runs payment plans called tax trusts for owners who have slipped behind.

Houses taken through tax foreclosure go to the Greater Syracuse Property Development Corporation, the Land Bank. Selling before that stage keeps the decision with you. Ask the Payment Center for a payoff on taxes and water before you fix a closing date, so the amounts are in your net figure.

Assessment grievances and exemptions

The Board of Assessment Review takes grievance forms during the last two weeks of January, and each form needs an original signature. Bring evidence that the assessment is unequal, excessive or unlawful.

Syracuse applies STAR to city and school taxes, and the city lists senior, disability, flood zone, historic and property improvement exemptions. They follow the owner who qualifies, so a buyer files for their own.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Syracuse houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Winter weather and a showing

Syracuse gets about 38.5 inches of precipitation a year, and its snow usually comes in small, near-daily amounts over several days. The 1993 blizzard dropped 42.9 inches in 48 hours. With winters like these, buyers pay attention to roofs, gutters, furnaces and basements, and a folder of recent repair receipts supports your price.

Tree canopy covers about 27 percent of the city, and a limb over the roof or a heaved sidewalk slab can complicate an inspection. The city's main water supply is Skaneateles Lake, and your water account runs through the same Payment Center as your taxes. Close the account out when the keys change hands so the next owner starts with a clean slate.

A short pre-sale checklist

Before you take an offer, call the Payment Center for a payoff on taxes and water, and ask Code Enforcement whether a rental, compliance or vacant certificate applies. Pull your deed from the Onondaga County Clerk if you do not have a copy, and confirm everyone on the title will sign.

Then gather any lease, repair receipts and notices from the city. Buyers in Syracuse move faster when the file is complete, and a cash buyer can close on your date once title is clear. Keep a written record of each call so you can show what the city told you.

If the house has been vacant, do not forget the registry. An empty building with exterior violations has to be registered, and the certificate renews each year while it stays empty.

Frequently asked questions

Can a house with a tenant be sold?

Yes, and investors buy occupied rentals here regularly. Check with Code Enforcement first, since a one or two-unit rental needs a Rental Registry Certificate after a sale and larger buildings need a Certificate of Compliance before the title moves.

What is a tax trust?

It is a payment plan from the City Payment Center for homeowners who have fallen behind on property taxes. Ask about the plan or a payoff figure before choosing how to sell.

Where can a seller check an assessment or owner record?

Start with the Department of Assessment, which can explain the figure and the exemptions on your account. The Image Mate lookup shows ownership of any address in the city.

How do I get a copy of my deed?

Ask the Onondaga County Clerk, the official keeper of deeds. The same office records the new deed when the house changes hands.

What slows down a cash closing?

Title work, open registry questions and unpaid city balances. A buyer without a lender skips the appraisal, but the deed still has to be signed, the state return filed and the transfer recorded, so ask for the closing date in writing.

Amherst housing in brief

Amherst is Buffalo's biggest suburb, up in the north of Erie County. About 130,442 people lived here in mid-2025, in 53,343 households. Owners live in 69.9% of homes, and a typical owned home is valued at $311,600. Owners with a mortgage pay about $1,945 a month, and typical gross rent is $1,393.

Over one resident in five is 65 or older, and 86.4% were at the same address a year earlier. Long tenure like that often ends in a downsize or an estate sale, and many of the town's subdivisions are decades old. A financed buyer may ask for repairs to kitchens, baths and mechanical systems. A cash buyer will usually fold them into the price.

Hamlets, the village and mailing addresses

Most names on an Amherst address are hamlets or post-office areas with no government of their own. Williamsville is the exception, an incorporated village inside the town.

  • Eggertsville and Snyder, in the older southwest, near Buffalo
  • Williamsville, the incorporated village in the south
  • Getzville and the Audubon area, near the center
  • East Amherst and Swormville, shared with the Town of Clarence
  • North Bailey, around Bailey Avenue and Maple Road

Villages and hamlets also differ in who answers the phone for permits and local rules. Before you list or accept an offer, confirm with the town whether the parcel falls under a village office as well.

Mailing addresses can cross town lines. Some homes east of Transit Road carry a Williamsville address yet belong to the Town of Clarence for taxes and schools. Read the tax bill to see which municipality applies before you write any paperwork.

Which school district is your house in?

Four public districts divide the town. Williamsville Central takes the eastern half and some of Clarence. Amherst Central has the southwest, around Eggertsville and Snyder. Sweet Home Central has the northwest, including West Amherst and Getzville, and Clarence Central has a small southeastern corner.

Two homes sharing a ZIP code can fall in different districts, so name the district whenever you describe the house. The tax bill names it, and the Assessor's Office can confirm.

Rental registration when tenants live in the house

Chapter 44 of the town code bars renting a unit until the owner holds a rental registration certificate. An owner-occupied property with two or fewer units, if not used for short stays, is exempt.

Amherst rental certificates

Standard rentalUp to three years$75 inspection fee for each unit
Short-term rental (stays of 1 to 30 days)One year, with an annual inspection$250 a unit if the owner lives there, $500 if not (2025 form)
  • No certificate issues until the unit passes inspection and local property taxes are current.
  • Owners living outside Erie, Niagara and Genesee counties need a local agent.
  • Houses built before 1978 carry a lead paint certification on the form.

A buyer can take over a certificate's remaining term by filing a transfer application with the Commissioner of Building within 30 days of the deed, so hand over the certificate and inspection paperwork at closing. Skipping registration can double the fee, add a $75 fine and lead to a notice to vacate. A code violation can bring up to $1,500 or 15 days in jail.

Contesting your assessment

Each parcel is valued by the town Assessor. If you disagree, form RP-524 is free to file. Most communities use the fourth Tuesday in May as the cutoff, which would be May 25 in 2027, so confirm the day with the Assessor's Office at 5583 Main Street in Williamsville. Call ahead, since the office has taken paperwork by mail or drop-off as well as hearings in person.

If you are close to selling, a lower assessment helps the buyer more than it helps you. A wrong square footage or unit count should still be corrected, because an appraiser pulls the same record.

County tax liens

Erie County may foreclose on liens that sit unpaid for two years or longer. Owners receive notice and a final redemption date. To redeem, an owner pays the back taxes plus a $500 statutory fee by cash, certified check, bank check or money order to the County Director of Real Property Tax Services. Parcels not redeemed head to public auction, and later years' taxes keep accruing.

Owe back taxes? Ask Erie County Real Property Tax Services for a payoff number, because fees and interest keep adding to the balance. Sale proceeds can clear the lien, so ask your title company to order that figure soon.

Transfer tax and your sale options

Sellers normally cover New York's conveyance tax, which runs $2 for every $500 of price. File the TP-584 return with the Erie County Clerk within 15 days of handing over the deed.

Three routes are open: hire an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer. A listing means showings plus a closing date that follows the buyer's lender. A cash buyer takes the house in its current condition, which suits a rental near the end of its certificate, an inherited house or a parcel with back taxes.

How a sale unfolds in Amherst

Start by deciding which municipality your parcel sits in, since a Williamsville mailing address can still mean Clarence taxes. Next, settle the open items attached to the house: a rental certificate that needs transferring, a code violation, or back taxes owed to the county. The title company will find each of these anyway, and a seller who raises them first controls the conversation.

With a mortgage-backed buyer, an inspection comes first, then an appraisal, and the lender sets the calendar. With a cash buyer, the house is reviewed as it stands and you pick the day. Either way you sign the deed at closing, and the title company settles your mortgage and any unpaid tax out of the proceeds before the return and tax go to the clerk.

A tenant adds one more task. Pass the lease and certificate to the buyer, and make sure the transfer application is filed inside the 30 day window so the registration survives the handover.

What to gather before you sell

  • The deed and your lender's payoff statement
  • The latest town and school tax bills
  • Any rental certificate and inspection paperwork
  • A written payoff from Erie County if any back taxes are owed

Bring those four and the title search can start the same day. A cash buyer can name a closing date once the numbers are settled, with no appraisal in the middle.

Frequently asked questions

Does a tenant-occupied Amherst house need a rental certificate at sale?

Registration is the owner's duty while the unit is rented. A buyer can take it over by filing within 30 days of the deed, so hand over the certificate and inspection paperwork.

What is the cutoff for contesting an Amherst assessment?

Most New York communities use the fourth Tuesday in May. Check the exact day with the Amherst Assessor's Office. The form is RP-524, and there is no charge to file.

What happens when county tax liens stay unpaid on an Amherst property?

Erie County can foreclose once liens are two or more years old. Owners receive notice and a last redemption date, with a $500 fee, and anything left unredeemed goes to public auction.

Who pays the state transfer tax on an Amherst sale?

Usually the seller. The rate is $2 for each $500, and a leftover partial $500 counts as a whole one. The Erie County Clerk receives the return within 15 days of the deed.

How do I find which district my Amherst house belongs to?

It is one of Williamsville, Amherst, Sweet Home or Clarence Central, depending on location. The tax bill names it, and the Assessor's Office can confirm.

Which Smithtown address do you have?

Smithtown lies on Long Island's North Shore in Suffolk County, with the Sound on its north edge and Islip, Brookhaven and Huntington on the other sides. The name covers more than one place: the town includes the hamlet of Smithtown, plus Kings Park, St. James, Nesconset, Fort Salonga and parts of Commack, Hauppauge and Lake Ronkonkoma. Three incorporated villages sit inside it too, Head of the Harbor, Nissequogue and the Village of the Branch.

That patchwork decides which rules, school district and tax collector apply to your house. A home in Kings Park belongs to a different school district than one in Smithtown hamlet, and a house inside one of the three villages may have village code on top of town code. Check your deed and tax bill for the exact district before you describe the property to a buyer.

Smithtown housing market

Smithtown is a high-value, owner-heavy town where people stay put. Nearly nine in ten homes (88.7%) are lived in by their owners, and the typical value is $669,900. Turnover is low, with 95.0% of residents unmoved in the past year. Population reached 116,847 in mid-2025, a 0.4% gain on 2020.

  • Land area: 53.75 square miles
  • Households: 39,611, at 2.87 persons each
  • Typical gross rent: $2,233
  • Typical household income: $152,636

Mortgaged owners in the town carry monthly costs of $3,809, so a buyer is committing a large budget and will look hard at condition. A house with deferred work is usually priced against that expectation, and a seller who documents repairs and permits starts from a stronger position.

Trains, roads and school districts

Smithtown commuters rely on a mix of rail and parkways. The Long Island Rail Road's Port Jefferson Branch stops at the Kings Park, Smithtown and St. James stations. By car, the Northern State Parkway reaches the town at Commack, the Sunken Meadow State Parkway winds northeast to Sunken Meadow State Park, and Routes 25, 25A, 111 and 347 carry local traffic. The average commute is 32.2 minutes.

  • Smithtown Central School District, with its own elementary, middle and high school campuses.
  • Kings Park Central School District, which is also based in the town.
  • Portions of the town fall in the Commack, Hauppauge and Sachem districts.

Mention the train station and school district by name in your listing, since those are the first things a Smithtown buyer asks about.

Building Department and certificates of occupancy

Smithtown's Building Department applies the New York State Building Code and local zoning, permits new construction, additions and alterations, and issues a certificate of occupancy once work is done. Each transaction stays on permanent record, so a buyer's attorney can request your house's permit history.

Did you add a deck, finish a basement or convert a garage? Check that the work was permitted and closed out with a certificate, and if not, talk to the department before listing. Its office is at 23 Redwood Lane, the phone is (631) 360-7520, and inspections are scheduled at (631) 360-7522 or through an online form.

  • Neighbors and buyers can file a complaint on a property through the department's form.
  • Records requests go through a FOIL form.
  • For a house that has had tenants, ask the department whether any registration applies.

Property tax due dates

The town's Receiver of Taxes collects town, county and school district taxes on a single bill. The tax year runs from December 1 to November 30, and bills go out once a year around mid-December. The first half is payable by January 10 and the second by May 31, with no grace period for either date.

Smithtown tax collection calendar
StepTiming
Tax yearDecember 1 to November 30
Bills issuedAround mid-December
First half dueJanuary 10
Second half dueMay 31
After the May deadlinePaid to the Suffolk County Comptroller

The office accepts a partial payment of $200 or more, and a penalty lands only on the unpaid remainder. Paying by phone or online adds a service fee, while checks, counter payments and the Town Hall side-entrance drop box are other routes. Find the Receiver of Taxes at 99 W. Main Street in Smithtown, and bring your latest bill to closing so the half you paid is credited.

Recording a deed in Suffolk County

The Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead records Smithtown deeds and turns away anything that misses a rule. Get the deed form from your attorney or a legal stationer, because the clerk does not hand them out. The document has to list every party's name and a street address (no P.O. boxes), carry the seller's original signature with a notary's acknowledgment, and describe the property including its village, town and county.

  • A Suffolk County Recording and Endorsement page goes on top, printed on legal-size paper.
  • The RP-5217 transfer report is needed on every deed from November 1, 1980 onward.
  • Form TP-584 is the transfer tax return.
  • Recording fees can be paid by check, cash or money order, but transfer tax needs certified funds, cash, a money order or an approved title or attorney escrow check.

The extra Community Preservation form applies only in the five East End towns, Riverhead, Southampton, East Hampton, Shelter Island and Southold. Smithtown is not one of them, so that form is not part of a Smithtown recording.

The state transfer tax is two dollars for each five hundred dollars of price, due at recording. Homes sold at $1 million or more draw an added 1% charge on top.

Selling fast: what a cash sale skips

A standard listing means prepping the house, hosting showings, then sitting through a buyer's loan approval, appraisal and inspection. Where condition and permit history get scrutiny, any of those steps can reopen the price. Cash removes the appraisal and the lender's clock, so the house can close in its current state. Paperwork does not vanish: the deed, TP-584 and RP-5217 still reach the Suffolk County Clerk, and a tax half you already paid is still credited.

Ahead of any buyer conversation, assemble your latest tax bill, certificates of occupancy and a list of work done on the house.

What a Smithtown seller should expect at closing

Your attorney will order a title search and ask for the latest tax bill, so keep it handy. Next comes the deed, which you sign before a notary while the buyer's side delivers funds. What you take home is the price minus transfer tax, any tax still owed and an existing mortgage payoff.

With prices this high, mortgage buyers often come back after the inspection asking for credits, and that haggling can add weeks. Sellers who want one firm date and no renegotiation can look at a cash offer for the house in its present state. Get the terms on paper so your move can be planned around them.

Frequently asked questions

Which school district serves a house in Smithtown?

It depends on the street. The town holds the Smithtown Central and Kings Park Central districts, and portions fall in Commack, Hauppauge and Sachem. Your tax bill names the district.

Should my addition have a certificate of occupancy?

The town issues one when construction is complete, and a buyer's attorney may ask to see it for an addition or conversion. The Building Department can confirm what is on file for your address.

What if the second-half tax payment is late?

Anything postmarked after May 31 cannot be accepted by the Receiver of Taxes. The balance moves to the Suffolk County Comptroller, at (631) 852-3000.

Is Smithtown property tax paid in installments?

Yes. The bill splits into a first half due January 10 and a second half due May 31, and a payment of at least $200 can also be made at any time.

Who records the deed on a sale?

The Suffolk County Clerk in Riverhead records it, along with the Recording and Endorsement page, RP-5217 and TP-584. Closing professionals usually submit that bundle for you.

Selling a house in Albany

Albany is the seat of Albany County, with Colonie to the north, Guilderland to the west and Bethlehem to the south. Renters outnumber owners here. Owners live in just 38.2% of homes, and a typical owned home is worth $234,700. The city had an estimated 101,698 residents in mid-2025, spread over 44,357 households of about two people each.

Buyers shop by neighborhood first: Arbor Hill, Center Square, Pine Hills and the South End are among the best known. Name the neighborhood in any listing or offer conversation. If your building has tenants, expect questions about leases and inspection certificates early on.

Registries that can hold up a closing

The city's Buildings and Regulatory Compliance department keeps several registries. When a registration expires, a hold goes on the property record and no permits issue until the lapse is fixed.

The vacant building rule dates to July 1, 2000. Register as soon as a building empties, or when you buy an empty one. Not registering risks a penalty of up to $1,000 a day. An unpaid waste fee moves to the next bill with late charges.

Red placards on some empty buildings tell firefighters about structural hazards. If one of those is yours, ask the department where the registration stands before you take an offer.

Vacant house questions

The city requires the vacant building registration to stay current, but it does not require repairs before a sale. A buyer who takes the house as is inherits the registration duty, so confirm the annual fee is paid before closing.

Larger and non-residential buildings pay more under the city's schedule. If the house has been empty for a while, call the department, ask for the current registration status in writing and bring that paper to the title company.

How to challenge your Albany assessment

Complaints can be filed from May 1 until the fourth Tuesday in May. The next window opens May 1, 2027, and the form is RP-524. There is no filing charge, and the Assessor's Office at City Hall has forms starting May 1.

New construction, fires, demolitions and periodic citywide updates are what move an assessment. If your records show a change like that, tell the assessor, because buyers see the same number you do.

Exemptions

Exemption applications, Basic STAR included, are accepted January 1 through March 1, and all owners sign. A buyer who wants a STAR or senior exemption applies on their own after the deed, so mention the March 1 date if your sale lands in winter.

If you hold an exemption now, tell your buyer plainly that the tax bill under new ownership may look different. Surprises at the closing table cost more goodwill than the number itself, and a buyer who hears it early can plan around it.

Ask the assessor for a printout of the current record at the same time. Compare the unit count and square footage with what you actually have, and correct anything wrong before the house goes on the market or in front of a cash buyer.

Tax bills and due dates

A city bill can be split. Half is due January 31 (February 6 for eligible seniors) and the rest is billed in July. Split payments are limited to check or cash, and online payment covers only full amounts. Mailed payments count on the postmark, so skip bill-pay services that do not use one.

Before you close, have the title company check the city bill, the waste collection fee and the school tax line by line. Each can carry a different balance, and a payoff that covers only one of them leaves the others to surface later.

A sale of an Albany house usually moves in this order.

  3. Request the current city bill, the waste collection fee balance and the school tax figure.

  5. At closing the seller signs the deed, and the TP-584 return and transfer tax go to the Albany County Clerk within 15 days.

A hold on the record is the item that most often surprises sellers. It stops permits, and a buyer's lender may balk, so clearing it before you sign saves a delay at the table.

Selling a rental or a house with tenants

Tenants in place do not block a sale, but the paperwork matters. The buyer will want the leases, the latest rental dwelling certificate and proof that the 24 month inspection is current. A certificate that lapsed can be renewed for $50 a unit, and fixing it before listing keeps a retail buyer from discounting the price.

If the building is empty instead, the vacant registration steps up each year, from $250 to $1,000. Owners who plan to sell a long-empty house often decide that a quick cash purchase costs less than another year of fees.

What does an Albany sale cost in state tax?

The state transfer tax is $2 per $500 of the sale price and is usually the seller's cost. The Albany County Clerk receives the TP-584 return and payment within 15 days of the deed. A 1% mansion tax applies to residences of $1 million or more and is paid by the buyer.

Going through an agent means preparing the house, hosting showings and waiting on a buyer's lender. A cash purchase skips that and closes when you pick, which fits an empty house, a lapsed rental certificate or an estate.

Documents to gather before you sell

Either way, pull together the same paperwork:

  • The deed and your lender's payoff letter
  • The most recent city and school tax bills
  • Proof that registry certificates are current, including any rental registration or certificate of occupancy paperwork
  • Leases and the latest rental dwelling certificate, if tenants live there, so a buyer can see the inspection status at a glance

Having these in one folder shortens the title search. It also speeds a cash offer, because the buyer can price the house without waiting on records from three different offices.

Can I sell a vacant house in Albany without fixing it first?

Yes. The city requires the vacant building registration to stay current, but it does not require repairs before a sale. A buyer who takes the house as is inherits the registration duty, so confirm the annual fee is paid before closing.

When is Albany's grievance deadline?

The fourth Tuesday in May, with the window opening May 1. The next one opens May 1, 2027. Forms are available from the Assessor's Office at City Hall beginning May 1.

How much is the vacant building fee in Albany?

For a one to three unit residential building it is $250 in the first year, $500 in the second, $750 in the third and $1,000 for each later year. Larger and non-residential buildings pay more under the city's schedule.

Does the buyer or the seller pay New York's transfer tax?

The seller pays the base state transfer tax of $2 per $500, unless the contract says otherwise. The 1% mansion tax applies to residences of $1 million or more and is paid by the buyer.

What documents should an Albany seller have ready?

Bring the deed, the most recent city and school tax bills, proof that registry certificates are current, any rental registration or certificate of occupancy paperwork, and a mortgage payoff statement. If tenants live there, add leases and the rental dwelling certificate.

Greenburgh is in the west of Westchester, where the Hudson forms its border on one side, Yonkers lies below it, Mount Pleasant above, and White Plains and Scarsdale beside it. About half of residents live in villages. The rest live in unincorporated areas such as Fairview, Greenville and Hartsdale, plus North Elmsford and South Ardsley.

The Building Department takes complaints only for the unincorporated area, and the Tax Department sends village residents to their own Village Hall for due dates. A seller in Tarrytown therefore checks two sets of offices, while a seller in Hartsdale deals mostly with the town.

Housing market snapshot

Greenburgh had 94,537 residents in 2025 across 35,813 households, and owners occupy 74.0% of homes. The median home is worth $697,100. Renters pay $2,316 at the median, the middle household earns $152,256, and getting to work takes 34.4 minutes on average. At that price level, closing costs and the state's one percent charge on high-value homes both start to matter. If you are weighing a sale against renting the house out, that rent figure is the number to test.

Commuting questions come up first with buyers. Hudson Line trains of Metro-North stop at Hastings-on-Hudson, Dobbs Ferry, Ardsley-on-Hudson, Irvington and Tarrytown, and Hartsdale has a Harlem Line station. Drivers have the Thruway, the Cross Westchester Expressway, the Saw Mill River, Bronx River and Sprain Brook parkways, US 9 and routes 9A, 100 and 119. The county's Bee-Line buses run here too.

Ten school districts feed into the tax office's billing, so the district printed on your bill can change the total between neighboring streets. Get your current bill in hand before pricing the house.

Building permits to check before listing

The Building Department's FAQ casts a wide net: building, fixing, improving, altering or tearing down anything calls for a permit. Re-roofing a one or two family house is included, and structural roof work needs drawings sealed by a New York State architect or engineer.

  • Sheds of any size need a permit. The limit is one per lot, placed in the rear yard, at most 150 square feet and 10 feet high.
  • Fences need no building permit up to six feet in a front or side yard and eight feet in the rear, with a 30 inch cap near corners.
  • Repaving an existing driveway needs nothing, but enlarging it does, and Public Works may also require a curb cut or right-of-way permit.
  • Pulling or abandoning a heating oil tank takes its own permit and inspection.
  • No residential zoning district lists short-term rentals as a permitted use.

If a buyer mentions a vacation rental, raise that last rule early. Bring or mail applications to 177 Hillside Avenue on a weekday. Current hours are posted on the forms page.

Property taxes and what happens at closing

One office, the Receiver of Taxes, sends bills covering the county, the town, the fire districts and ten school districts, making it the largest municipal collector in Westchester. Ask it for the next due date and a balance on paper before you close.

  • Checks go to the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes, 177 Hillside Avenue. Paying online by card adds a fee that varies, and ACH payments cost nothing.
  • Liens are the exception: they can't be paid online.
  • Once title passes, the new owner should call so later bills find the right mailbox. If you've moved, send the office your forwarding address in writing.

State law adds two limits. Not receiving a bill doesn't wipe out the tax or its interest (Real Property Tax Law section 922), and the Receiver may not waive a penalty (section 920).

Assessment roll and tax dates

Greenburgh assessment and collection dates
DateWhat happens
June 1Tentative roll open for public viewing
Until September 15Appeals heard by the Board of Assessment Review
September 15Roll becomes final
January 31, April 30, September 30Receiver's office stays open until 7 p.m. on the final payment day

Once final, the roll is fixed, and later small claims changes don't alter it. Compare your own line with recent nearby sales. The buyer's attorney reads the same entry, and the Assessor's Office will answer questions about the newest figure.

What the Westchester County Clerk needs for a deed

Filing a deed means going through the Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk. Its recording guide lists what to submit: a cover page generated in the county's PREP system, form TP-584, the RP-5217 transfer report, and a payment cover page that shows the fees and tax.

The state charges $2 for each $500 of the price, rounding up, and sellers usually pay. At $1,000,000 or more, a one to three family house or condo picks up an extra one percent mansion tax. Clerk's staff can't write a deed or give advice about one, so your attorney handles the document.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Greenburgh houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with a lien or an open tax balance

An unpaid tax bill won't stop a sale, but it must be cleared when you close. Start by asking the Receiver of Taxes for a written balance. A lien is handled differently from an ordinary bill: it can't be paid online, so someone has to bring the payment to the Tax Office at 177 Hillside Avenue or send it by check made out to the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes. Your closing attorney normally arranges this and takes the amount from your proceeds.

The Receiver has no power to waive a penalty, so a late bill costs what it costs. If you are behind and the house needs work you can't afford, a direct purchase by a cash buyer can pay the balance at the table and still leave you something. Compare that figure with what a listing would bring after commission, repairs and the months of carrying costs.

When a village bill applies as well as the town bill, collect both. The village office, not the town, sets the due dates for village taxes, so call that Village Hall for its schedule.

Preparing to sell

Start with the property condition disclosure statement required by Real Property Law section 462. The buyer must receive it before any binding contract is signed.

  • Certificates of occupancy or completion for finished space, and permit records for recent work.
  • Town, county and school tax bills, plus a village bill if you live in a village.
  • A lender payoff letter and details of any lien.
  • Your STAR status, since the state asks owners to close a registration after a sale.

A cash buyer who takes the house as is can skip showings and repair negotiations, but title work, payoff and recording still take time. Ask for a written closing date and proof of funds with every offer.

Frequently asked questions

Do village homes in Greenburgh use the town Building Department?

Generally not. The town department handles complaints only in the unincorporated part of Greenburgh. For a house in a village such as Tarrytown, ask the village hall about permits and due dates.

Is a permit needed for a new roof in Greenburgh?

Yes. A roof covering replacement on a one or two family house needs a building permit with drawings, and a structural change needs plans from a New York State architect or engineer.

Can the next owner run a short-term rental from a Greenburgh house?

Short-term rentals aren't a permitted use in any residential zoning district. A buyer with that plan should confirm with the Building Department before closing.

What transfer tax applies to a Greenburgh sale?

State tax is $2 for every $500 of price. The one percent mansion tax starts at $1,000,000 for one to three family homes and condos, and the buyer pays it.

Where do Greenburgh property tax payments go?

To the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes at 177 Hillside Avenue, which collects for the county, town, fire districts and ten school districts. Village residents follow their village's own schedule.

Selling a house in Greece

Greece is Monroe County's most populous town and wraps around Rochester's northwest corner. Houses run from Ridge Road in the south to the Lake Ontario shoreline. The 2025 population of 94,484 sits below the 96,926 counted in 2020, so demand isn't being pushed up by new arrivals. Owners live in 72.7% of the homes. Values center on $190,300, median rent is $1,170, and workers spend 20.5 minutes getting to their jobs, a detail that tends to appeal to buyers relocating from elsewhere.

Braddock Bay and other wetlands and ponds sit along the northern edge. New York's disclosure form has questions on wetlands and flood zones, so go slowly over those lines if your lot is close to the water.

Three districts split the town: Greece Central, Hilton Central and Spencerport Central. ZIP code 14468 is Hilton and 14559 is Spencerport, which means a mailing address can point to a different district than you expect. Spell out the district whenever you describe the house to anyone.

Town rules that can slow a sale

On a Greece house, two problems stall closings more than any others: permits that were never finished and code violations visible from the street. The Building Department sits within Technical Services at One Vince Tofany Boulevard. A remodel or addition to a single-family house needs a permit, and once the work costs more than $20,000 the plans must be professionally prepared.

  • A permitted project passes through footing and foundation, rough framing, insulation and final grading checks. An electrical sign-off comes from one of three listed inspection agencies, and the town does a last inspection at the end.
  • The town's property maintenance law reaches vacant buildings and empty land too. The penalty is as much as $1,000 or a year in jail for each violation, and the town can make the repair itself and send you the cost on your tax statement.
  • Trash pickup has to be active at every home. Vehicles that are dismantled or unlicensed can't be left in the yard.
  • Keep your for sale sign to one, no bigger than six square feet, and off the roadside right of way and utility poles.

Rental applications, both short-term and long-term, are posted beside the building forms. Look at them if tenants will stay after the sale. And before any contract is signed, have the department confirm that earlier work was closed out.

Property tax billing and payment

Each January the Receiver of Taxes collects the town's general taxes for the calendar year. The mailing in early January combines the Town, Monroe County, the Greece Fire District, the Greece Central School District and any special districts. A school or water charge left unpaid gets re-levied onto that same bill, so ask the closing attorney to check whether one is waiting.

Rates for the county, fire district and schools aren't the town's to set. Town Hall just collects. You can pay in person on weekdays or leave a payment in the 24 hour drop at the Service Mall entrance. Online payments run through Monroe County's website with a 3 percent charge on cards. Phone payments aren't taken.

Take your latest bill to the attorney. The other side will ask for a printout of paid and open amounts on the parcel, and the Receiver's office can supply it.

Contesting your assessment

There are three stages. The first is free and happens early in the year. Because a lower assessment also helps whoever buys next, winning before you list can back up your asking price.

  • Informal hearing: by appointment with the Assessor's Office, from January to March.
  • Board of Assessment Review: file form RP-524 after May 1 and by the fourth Tuesday of May, and request either a hearing or a review of the papers.
  • Judicial review: when the board's result still seems wrong, form RPTL-730 and fees must be filed within 30 days after the final roll is published.

The town assesses as of March 1 and uses the July 1 before that as its valuation day, so work finished after March 1 shows up on the next roll. A spring sale can overlap with an appeal that hasn't been decided. Tell the buyer if so.

What recording a deed costs in Monroe County

The Monroe County Clerk records Greece deeds at 39 West Main Street in Rochester, and same-day recording means standing in line by 4:30 p.m. The clerk's land records page shows the going charges.

Monroe County recording charges for a residential deed
Recording chargeAmount
One page deed$50, plus $5 for each added page
TP-584 form$5
Equalization form RP-5217$125 for common residential cases, otherwise $250
Transfer tax$4 per thousand dollars of price
Residential deed add-on$10 per deed

Most sellers never visit the counter, because the attorney or title company files the deed and tallies every charge ahead of closing.

From accepted offer to closing

Once you and the buyer settle on a price, the two attorneys exchange a contract while the buyer orders a title search. Anything it uncovers, such as unpaid school or water bills, open permits or liens, is paid off or credited at the table. Real Property Law section 462 also requires you to hand over a signed property condition disclosure statement before the contract is signed.

The closing itself is mostly signing: the deed, the transfer forms and the payoff to your lender, which comes straight out of your proceeds. Then the deed goes to the county clerk. Buyers paying cash for a house as is can often close sooner, since there's no loan approval or appraisal in the way. Clear title still matters, and so does a closing date you've agreed to in writing.

Paperwork to gather before offers arrive

  • The signed disclosure statement.
  • Permit records for each finished basement, deck, pool or addition.
  • A current tax bill showing every taxing line.
  • A payoff figure from your lender, plus any liens.
  • Keys, access and the closing date you want.

Selling for cash gets rid of showings, appraisals and an inspector's repair list. The paperwork above still applies. Pull it together now and any route to closing goes faster, whether you list or take a direct offer.

Comparing offers

Look at the amount that reaches your account, not the headline price. A listing may show a bigger number, but commission, repairs and carrying costs come out of it. A direct buyer's lower figure may leave you even if it closes quickly and asks for no fix-up work. Request each offer in writing with the closing date and proof of funds, and settle who pays the transfer tax and recording charges before you sign.

Frequently asked questions

Is Greece, NY part of Rochester?

No. Greece is its own town in Monroe County, with the city of Rochester on its eastern border. Taxes come from the Town of Greece, the county and the fire district, and the schools are Greece Central, Hilton Central or Spencerport Central.

Do I need a permit record to sell a Greece house?

Selling doesn't call for a permit. Still, open building permits and exterior code violations can stall a closing, so ask the Building Department to confirm that earlier work was closed out.

When do Greece town and county taxes get billed?

The bill is mailed in early January for the year from January 1 through December 31. The Receiver of Taxes collects it, and any unpaid school or water charge is added to it.

How much is the Monroe County transfer tax on a deed?

It is $4 per thousand dollars of the sale price, plus the recording and form fees. Your attorney can give you the exact total before closing.

What is the deadline to grieve a Greece assessment?

File form RP-524 after May 1 and by the fourth Tuesday of May. The Assessor holds informal hearings earlier, from January to March.

Selling a house in Clarkstown

Clarkstown is the most densely populated town in Rockland County, on the county's eastern edge with the Hudson River as its boundary. It covers about 47 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 86,855 residents. The hamlet of New City is the county seat and the seat of town government, and about 41 percent of the town's people live there.

The town also holds Bardonia, Congers, Central Nyack, Nanuet, Valley Cottage, West Nyack, Rockland Lake, Mount Ivy, the village of Upper Nyack, and the eastern part of the village of Spring Valley. Commuters use the Thruway (I-87 and I-287) and the Palisades Interstate Parkway, NJ Transit's Pascack Valley Line at Nanuet, and Rockland Coaches express buses to the Port Authority Bus Terminal.

School districts by address

Several districts divide the town, so the address matters. The Clarkstown Central School District serves most of it, including New City, Bardonia, Congers and West Nyack. Nyack Public Schools serve Upper Nyack, Valley Cottage and Central Nyack, the Nanuet Union Free School District serves Nanuet, and a small slice on the western border belongs to East Ramapo.

Quote the district from the tax bill, since one street can sit in a different district from the next.

Property tax due dates

Clarkstown's Town Clerk, at 10 Maple Avenue in New City, collects town and county property tax for a calendar year. Full payment is due by January 31 with no penalty. Late charges and the quarterly option are in the schedule below.

Payment choiceDate or windowCharge
Full payment, no penaltyBy January 31None

Full paymentMarch 1 to 31Additional 2%
Quarterly paymentsJanuary 15, April 15, July 15, October 155% service charge

The second to fourth quarterly installments are payable to Rockland County Budget and Finance in Pomona. No official can waive a statutory penalty, and a missing bill does not change what is owed. If no bill arrives in the first week of January or September, call the office for a duplicate.

What is on a Clarkstown tax bill

The bill is a line-by-line list: county tax, town tax, an open space charge, fire district, water district, lighting district, sewer, refuse, ambulance and charges set by Rockland Green. A one, two or three family house counts as homestead, and anything larger counts as non-homestead. Fire districts vary, so two Clarkstown neighbors can pay different amounts.

When you sell, the closing attorney prorates the bill between you and the buyer. Have the most recent bill in hand at the first meeting, along with proof of any amount already paid. If a quarterly installment is still open, the payoff comes out of your proceeds, and a cash buyer can close around that without waiting on a lender.

The assessment calendar

The July 1 before a roll is the valuation date, and all properties are valued at market conditions on that date. March 1 is the taxable status date, when ownership and condition are fixed and exemption applications must reach the Assessor. The tentative roll is filed May 1, which opens the formal grievance period. Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May, when the Board of Assessment Review hears complaints and every application must be on file. The 2027 date is May 25.

Timing matters for a seller. A house sold in December still carries the status it had on March 1, and the next roll uses the next July 1 valuation. If you think the tentative figure is too high, collect comparable sales and photographs before May. The town posts an online property assessment search for checking your record.

Certificate of occupancy

A Certificate of Occupancy is the town's assurance to a prospective buyer that a building is legally occupied and meets zoning and minimum repair and maintenance standards as of the issue date. One is required for an initial occupation, an alteration of an existing building, a change in use, or whenever a building permit has been issued. No certificate is issued while a deficiency or material violation remains uncorrected.

  • An altered, extended or enlarged building may not be used for more than 30 days after completion without a certificate.
  • A temporary certificate can be issued for a building in full compliance with zoning and near compliance with other rules, and it expires in 90 days.
  • Buildings that predate zoning and building codes, or permits that expired, carry an additional fee.
  • You apply at the Building Department, Room 101 on the lower level of Town Hall, 10 Maple Avenue.

Clarkstown does not require fence permits, but zoning limits residential solid fences and walls to 4 and a half feet along any lot line, and caps other fences at 6 feet unless they are set back from the lot line. Wood stoves and fireplaces always need a building permit. Ask the Building Department what is on file for your address before you list.

Rental registration

If the house has tenants, the town's Rental Registry Law applies. Every owner of a one-family or two-family dwelling who rents it must register with the Building Department, unless the owner lives there. An approved registration lasts two years, and the town inspects registered rentals every two years, including smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers.

Brokers must verify that a current rental registration exists before they list, show or offer a registered dwelling unit for lease, rent or sale. Penalties start at $4,500 to $6,000 for a first offense and rise for repeat offenses, with a separate weekly fine for each week a violation continues. If you inherited a rented house, ask the Building Department whether it is registered before you set a closing date.

Recording the deed in Rockland County

The Rockland County Clerk records deeds, mortgages and satisfactions for Clarkstown. Documents must be originals in recordable form, legible, signed and notarized. The clerk charges a $45 filing fee and $5 per page, plus a $10 notification fee for deed filings and the current fees for the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms.

State law sets transfer tax at $2 for each $500 of price, paid by the seller, and the TP-584 is due within 15 days of delivering the deed. A 1 percent mansion tax is owed by the buyer on residences of $1 million or more. Ask your closing attorney early about the title search and the deed form, since a cash sale is recorded the same way as a financed one.

Frequently asked questions

How many people live in Clarkstown, NY?

The 2020 census counted 86,855 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 89,659. New City makes up about 41 percent of the town.

When are Clarkstown town and county taxes due?

Full payment is due January 31 without penalty, with 1 percent added in February and 2 percent in March. The quarterly plan adds a 5 percent service charge and has installments on January 15, April 15, July 15 and October 15.

Does Clarkstown require a certificate of occupancy to sell a house?

The town requires one for new occupancy, alterations, a change in use, or when a building permit was issued. Ask the Building Department what is on file for your address before you list.

Do I have to register a rental house in Clarkstown?

Yes, if you own a one or two-family dwelling and rent it out without living there. Registration lasts two years and the town inspects rentals every two years.

When is Grievance Day in Clarkstown?

It is the fourth Tuesday in May, the day the Board of Assessment Review hears complaints on the May 1 tentative roll. The 2027 date is May 25.

Cheektowaga housing numbers

An estimated 88,160 people lived in town in mid-2025, below the 89,877 counted in the 2020 census and above the 88,226 of 2010. Homes are affordable by regional standards: the median owner's home is worth $185,000, against $164,200 in Buffalo and $332,700 nationwide. Most of the housing was built in the postwar subdivision boom of the 1950s and 1960s. A buyer's inspector will therefore look hard at the heating, the electrical panel and the age of the shingles. After lake-effect winters, a roof patched more than once or a basement that takes on water in the spring thaw can push a repair estimate past what a seller wants to spend. Selling as is passes that job to the buyer.

Neighborhoods and school districts

Cheektowaga borders Buffalo on the west, Amherst on the north, Lancaster on the east and West Seneca on the south. Several of its neighborhoods have their own school districts.

  • Bellevue, between Union Road and the Depew line
  • Cleveland Hill, on the north town line, with its own school district
  • Maryvale, west of the airport, which is also a school district
  • Pine Hill, on the Buffalo border near Villa Maria College
  • Doyle, South Line and U-Crest in the south and southwest
  • Sloan, a village and the seat of the Cheektowaga-Sloan school district

Eight separate public school districts operate inside the town, so a buyer's first question is often which one covers the house. Boundaries follow the parcel, so ask the district itself before answering. Buffalo Niagara International Airport lies within the town, and the New York State Thruway, I-90, crosses it from north to south. Union Road (NY 277), Harlem Road (NY 240), Transit Road (NY 78) and Broadway (NY 130) carry local traffic, with the Kensington Expressway (NY 33) and I-190 leading toward Buffalo.

Landlord and vacant property registration

If you own property in the town outside the villages of Sloan and Depew and you do not live there, you must register it. Chapter 194 of the town code, the Landlord Rental and Property Owner Registration Ordinance, requires registration every two years whether the building is occupied or vacant.

  • The registration fee is $20.
  • New owners file a registration statement within 30 days of buying.
  • Failing to register violates section 194-6 and carries a fine.

With a rental or an inherited house that sits empty, bring the registration up to date before closing. The town's Building Department covers building, plumbing, fire safety and neighborhood preservation, and the Town Clerk and Receiver of Taxes publishes the registration page. Buyers' lawyers sometimes ask for proof, and a lapsed registration costs less to fix now than at the closing table.

Transfer tax and deed recording

Deeds for Cheektowaga houses are recorded by the Erie County Clerk. The seller pays transfer tax when the TP-584 goes in: $2.00 per $500 of price to the state plus $2.50 per $500 to the county, or $4.50 per $500 in all. A seller aged 62 or older who has owned and lived in a one- or two-family house for at least a year can lower the rate to $2.00 per $500 by signing an affidavit, which the County Clerk's office provides free.

A 1% Mansion Tax applies once the price on a residential conveyance reaches $1 million. Home sales come with a separate Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form. The clerk's office cannot help fill out legal forms, so a lawyer or title agent normally drafts the documents and handles the filing.

Assessments in Cheektowaga

The Cheektowaga Assessment Office, phone 716-686-3440, can confirm your assessed value, and the town website posts the tentative and final assessment rolls. Before you sell, ask whether your parcel has an exemption on file. A buyer who takes over the house may need to apply for their own, and knowing what is in place now avoids a surprise on the first tax bill.

First steps for a Cheektowaga seller

Cheektowaga sales often involve an older house with years of deferred upkeep, a rental the owner no longer wants to manage, or an inherited home. Each of those has its own paperwork, and handling it in the right order saves time.

Walk through the house with a notebook before you call anyone. Note the roof, the furnace, the water heater, any basement dampness and the windows, and write down which repairs you have already paid for. A direct buyer will want these details, and having them ready gets you a firmer first offer.

Four items keep a quick sale on track.

  • Confirm from the deed and tax bill whether the house is in the town outside the villages or inside Sloan or Depew.
  • Register the property with the town if you do not live in it, and pay the $20 fee.
  • Request a payoff letter from your lender, and check with the Assessment Office on any exemptions.
  • Gather the deed, the TP-584 and the RP-5217 so the Erie County Clerk can record the transfer at closing.

Owners live in 71.5% of homes here, so most sellers are individual homeowners rather than investors. A direct buyer can build the closing around a mortgage payoff, a probate timeline or your move date. For a house left by a parent, gather the death certificate and the papers showing who has authority to sell, since the title company will ask for them. Tell the buyer which of those applies, and the schedule can be set around it. If a family member needs to sign, arrange that early, since an out-of-town heir is a common cause of delay.

Frequently asked questions

Is Cheektowaga a city or a town?

It is a town in Erie County. It contains the village of Sloan and half of the village of Depew, and it sits next to Buffalo on the city's east side.

What does Cheektowaga charge to register a non-owner-occupied house?

The fee is $20. Registration repeats every two years, and the first statement is due within 30 days after you buy.

Is there a senior discount on Cheektowaga transfer tax?

Yes. Erie County allows owners aged 62 or older to reduce the rate from $4.50 to $2.00 per $500 if they owned and lived in a one- or two-family home for at least a year before the sale. The County Clerk's office hands out the affidavit at no charge.

Which office handles Cheektowaga assessments?

The town Assessment Office, reachable at 716-686-3440. Its website also carries the tentative and final assessment rolls.

Which school district serves a given Cheektowaga house?

Eight public districts operate within the town, among them Cheektowaga-Sloan, Maryvale and Cleveland Hill. The answer depends on the parcel, so verify with the district before telling a buyer.

Cash sale or listing in Colonie

It depends on what the house needs and how quickly you must move. Colonie is the most populous suburb of Albany, and plenty of owners there list the traditional way. Deferred repairs, tenants, a probate delay or a tax problem point toward a cash buyer who takes the house as is.

Listing the house means getting it ready, fitting in showings and then waiting for the buyer's bank. A cash sale replaces that with a walkthrough and a closing date you help choose.   • List with an agent for a house that shows well and a schedule with room in it.
  • Sell without an agent if you have a buyer in hand and can manage the contract.
  • A cash offer fits an inherited house, a rental with difficult tenants, storm or fire damage, or a move on a fixed date.

Colonie housing and location

Colonie sits north of Albany, with the Mohawk River along its northern line and the Hudson on the east. Interstates 87, 787 and 90 and US Route 9 cross it, and Albany International Airport lies inside the town. The town contains two incorporated villages, Colonie and Menands, plus hamlets such as Latham, Loudonville, Newtonville, Boght Corners, Verdoy and West Albany. Postwar suburban building took off here, and the population rose from 29,522 in 1950 to 69,147 in 1970. The 2020 count was 85,590 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 86,837.

School districts

Six public school districts serve the town: South Colonie, North Colonie, Watervliet, Menands, Niskayuna and Mohonasen. South Colonie covers much of the west, including West Albany and the village of Colonie, while North Colonie, which feeds Shaker High School, serves Latham and most of Loudonville and Newtonville.

When you list or sell, name the district and the nearest park, because Colonie buyers shop by both. The Town runs the Mohawk River Park and Pool Complex and a Parks and Recreation program, which is worth passing along to a family relocating from outside the Capital Region.

Property tax due dates

The Receiver of Taxes mails the general tax bill on December 31, and it is payable in January without penalty. Colonie is a town of the first class, and its collector is an elected Receiver of Taxes and Assessments.

  • General bill: due January 1 to 31, then 1% in February and 2% in March.
  • April 1: unpaid general bills go to the Albany County Department of Finance.
  • School bills: mailed August 31, due in September, then 4% in October.
  • November 1: unpaid school bills go to the county, and after December 1 they move onto the next general bill with a 7% penalty.

The office collects school tax for five districts and also bills water for Latham Water, about 22,000 accounts twice a year, with a 5% penalty after 30 days. If a prior owner received an exemption they no longer qualified for, an exemption payback charge can show up on the bill. Ask the office for a duplicate bill and any open balance before closing.

Owners who are 65 or older, or disabled, and live in a one, two or three family house can name a third party to receive duplicate bills on form RP-923, which helps when an aging parent is selling. Counter hours stretch to 6 p.m. during the last five business days of January and September. If January 31 is a weekend day, payment is due the next Monday.

Assessments, grievances and STAR

The Assessor's office in Memorial Town Hall, 534 New Loudon Road in Latham, runs the standard New York calendar. Exemptions and the taxable status date fall on March 1, the tentative roll is filed May 1, Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May and the final roll is filed July 1.

A complaint must reach the office by 8:00 p.m. on Grievance Day. A postmark that day does not count, and electronic service is refused. Colonie asks owners to come with a recent purchase contract, sales of similar homes nearby or a current appraisal, and the owner carries the burden of proof. Colonie's 2027 Grievance Day is in late May.

A sale that closes in the fall or winter still carries the status the house had on March 1, so check your exemptions before you list. Anything you hold now, such as a senior or disability exemption, does not transfer automatically to the buyer.

Owners who bought after March 2, 2015, or never claimed STAR on a primary home, are told to register for the STAR credit, which pays by check. The Basic STAR income limit is $250,000, and above that you need the credit. A buyer in that group should register after closing, and exemption forms are handed out at the Assessor's counter on weekdays during business hours.

Recording the deed in Albany County

Albany County records deeds and mortgages, and deed and mortgage records since 1980 are searchable online. The seller usually pays state transfer tax at $2 for every $500 of price, and Form TP-584 must reach the county clerk within 15 days of delivering the deed. Confirm current recording fees with the clerk.

Setting up a Colonie sale in order: first confirm the amount owed on any mortgage, then pull your general and school tax bills, then decide whether the house is better sold as it stands or after repairs. For a house with tenants, read the lease for the term and the deposit before you talk to a buyer. For an estate, the person with authority to sign needs to be named early, since the title company will ask for the papers. Each of these steps is faster when you start with the paperwork in hand.

Latham Water bills twice a year, so check whether a water balance is open on the parcel. A balance left behind can follow the property, and the buyer's attorney will want it cleared. The Town's official website is townofcolonie.gov, so use that address when you look up departments.

Before you accept a cash offer, gather the deed, the latest general and school bills, a payoff statement for any loan, and the lease if there are tenants. The closing attorney uses them to order the title search and to split taxes between you and the buyer.

Will a cash buyer take a Colonie house with tenants in it?

Many will, but terms differ, so say so up front. Tell the buyer the lease dates, rent and deposit, and check your lease before you sign anything.

When is a Colonie property tax payment late?

After January 31. February adds 1% and March adds 2%, and on April 1 unpaid general bills go to the Albany County Department of Finance.

Does Colonie handle school taxes at Town Hall?

Yes for five districts. The Receiver of Taxes collects South Colonie, North Colonie, Menands, Niskayuna and Mohonasen bills, which are mailed August 31 and due in September.

What is the next Grievance Day in Colonie?

May 25, 2027. Complaints must be in the Assessor's office by 8:00 p.m. that day, and exemption forms are due March 1.

Which county office records a Colonie deed?

The Albany County Clerk. Form TP-584 goes with the deed, and the clerk can quote current fees.
