Which way of selling fits a Troy house?

Troy owners can go through an agent, handle the sale alone, or take an all-cash bid. Every version finishes with a deed, a state transfer tax return and a filing at the Rensselaer County Clerk, so the choice turns on speed, condition and how much effort you can give it.

A listing pays off for a house that is ready to move into, because mortgage buyers order an appraisal and an inspection. Direct cash deals turn up more often where repairs were put off, a tenant is in the way, a code question is open or an estate is involved. In all cases, set aside your latest tax bill, any lease and repair receipts.

  • Agent route: the biggest audience, along with prep work, showings and a bank-driven closing.
  • Solo route: no commission, but all contracts and haggling are yours.
  • All-cash route: the house sells as it stands and the closing date is negotiable.

Judge each bid by the cash you would leave with after tax balances, liens and the transfer tax, rather than the number on page one.

Troy as a place to sell

Troy is the Rensselaer County seat, set on the Hudson's east bank just northeast of Albany. It has 50,912 people, a 0.7 percent dip from 2020, on 10.36 square miles of land. Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, Emma Willard School, Russell Sage College and Hudson Valley Community College are all within the city limits.

Ground is flat beside the river and rises sharply eastward to about 500 feet. The north end used to be the separate city of Lansingburgh, and the Poesten Kill and Wynants Kill cut through town on their way to the Hudson. On a sloped lot, buyers may ask how water drains away from the house, so have any answers ready.

US 4 follows River Street, NY 7 uses Hoosick Street, NY 2 runs along Congress Street, and Interstate 787 ends in the city. The Troy and Lansingburgh school districts both serve parts of town, and whichever covers your street sends your school tax bill.

Troy housing numbers

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $206,500, and just 37.4 percent of homes are occupied by owners. Rents have a median of $1,175 among 21,265 households (2020 to 2024 figures).

With renters in the majority, small landlords and investors shape demand. Selling a two or three-unit building means supplying rent rolls, leases and utility costs. Median household income is $58,477, so price against close comparables instead of a citywide figure.

Troy is humid continental, averaging 25.5 degrees in January with about 42 inches of precipitation yearly, so have the ages of the roof and heating system on hand.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Troy house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Assessments, tax dates and bills

The city assessor builds a roll of about 13,400 properties every year, and 2013 was the last revaluation. A roll that old can sit well away from current prices, so an assessed value is a weak guide to what your house will bring.

Assessment and billing calendar
DateWhat happens
March 1Status date, and the last day to file exemptions
May 1Tentative roll filed; change notices go out that week
Fourth Tuesday of MayGrievance Day hearings
July 1Final roll filed; school, city and county taxes follow it
January and JulyCity and county installments

The Troy and Lansingburgh districts bill school taxes on their own, and penalties on those build monthly after the due date. The Treasurer's Office, 518-279-7115, can give a balance. Owners get a copy of a bill at no cost, while anyone else pays $5.

The Assessor's Office will also estimate taxes without exemptions for a prospective buyer, so a seller can steer a shopper there.

Exemption deadlines

Renewal packets for the senior and disability exemptions go out by mail each fall and are due back before March 1. The city and county income cap is $48,399 of 2025 household income.

  • STAR: first-time applicants go to the NYS Tax Department, not City Hall.
  • Seniors and owners with disabilities: send the signed renewal with your 2025 federal return, or the income worksheet if you do not file.
  • Military service: forms RP-458-a (alternative) and RP-458-b (Cold War).
  • Buyers of newly built homes, owners making capital improvements and owners rehabilitating historic buildings each have their own forms.

Exemptions stay with the owner who qualifies. A buyer files fresh paperwork, which is one reason a bill can climb after a sale. If your senior exemption lowers your bill, warn the buyer's side that their figure will differ.

Code enforcement and a sale

The Bureau of Code Enforcement handles building permits, housing and construction inspections, vacant building inspections, and certificates of occupancy and compliance. Troy enacted a new zoning ordinance and use maps in April 2023, so check them before you advertise a house as a legal two-family or mixed-use property.

Phone the bureau at 518-279-7180 before listing and ask whether open violations, vacant building requirements or certificate questions are tied to your address. Defects alone rarely stop a direct buyer, though unresolved city paperwork can hold up a closing. If the building has been empty, ask about its vacant building inspection requirements before you sign anything.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Troy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Finding out exactly what is owed

Start with the city's searchable tax roll, a document you can scan with your browser's find function by last name, account number or tax map ID. If you do not have the tax map ID, the Rensselaer County property search site shows it. Online payments carry a processing fee, but that fee goes to the outside vendor and not to the city.

Troy issues garbage bills as well as tax bills. Receipts for tax and garbage bills are only handed out when the entire bill is presented with the payment, and the top portion is then stamped as paid and returned. Keep that stamped stub with your closing papers as proof the bill was settled.

City and county installments fall in January and July, and school taxes follow a separate calendar. Ask the Treasurer's Office what is open on each before you agree to a closing date.

Preparing a Troy house for buyers

Before you list or accept a bid, collect the paper a buyer will ask for: your latest tax bill with its stamped stub, any lease and rent ledger, and the receipts for roof, heating and electrical work. Call the Treasurer's Office for a balance and the Bureau of Code Enforcement for open items.

If you live in a rental building, tell tenants early. If the house is vacant, confirm the vacant building rules. A tidy file lets a buyer price the property fast, and it shortens the wait between a handshake and a closing.

Frequently asked questions

When is Troy's Grievance Day?

The fourth Tuesday of May, which falls on May 25 in 2027. By then the tentative roll has been on file since May 1.

How are city and county taxes paid?

In two installments, one due in January and one in July. School taxes come separately from the Troy or Lansingburgh district, and the Treasurer's Office handles questions about your bill.

What does the state transfer tax cost on a sale?

New York's base tax is $2 per $500 of price and falls on the seller. The return goes to the county clerk with the deed.

Does a senior exemption pass to the buyer?

No. It belongs to the qualifying owner, so a buyer applies on their own by the March 1 deadline.

Can a Troy house with violations be sold?

Yes. Start by asking the Bureau of Code Enforcement what is open at your address, since a direct buyer can accept rough condition but open city items still need attention.

Selling a house in Orangetown

An Orangetown homeowner has three realistic paths: hire an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer. Speed depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close. Villages sit inside the town, so work out which government actually covers your street before anything else.

Orangetown occupies the southeastern edge of Rockland County, bordered by the Hudson on one side and New Jersey on another. Its population was 50,377 on July 1, 2025. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $638,100 and make up 74.2% of housing. Median gross rent is $2,015 a month and median household income is $145,007. With prices like these, a repair bill or a slipped closing date costs real money, so set a firm cash figure beside whatever a listing would leave you after repairs, commissions and months of carrying costs.

Buyers who commute will ask about transit. Pearl River station has New Jersey Transit service on the Pascack Valley Line, and I-87 runs through town as the New York State Thruway. Look at the school district named on your tax bill, because many buyers filter by it.

Which parts of Orangetown does the town government cover?

Town government in Orangetown serves the unincorporated hamlets. Nyack, Piermont and Grand View-on-Hudson are villages that run their own local affairs. Building safety in the unincorporated areas falls to the town's Building Department.

The hamlets are Blauvelt, Nauraushaun, Orangeburg, Pearl River, Palisades, South Nyack, Sparkill, Tappan and Upper Grandview. South Nyack was a village from 1878 until 2022. A house inside one of the villages has its permit history at that village hall, so begin your records request there.

Building Department permits

Plenty of everyday projects in Orangetown call for both a permit and a certificate of occupancy, even ones owners think of as upkeep. The department's list covers:

  • Additions, interior alterations and decks
  • Hot tubs, pools, fireplaces and chimneys
  • Oil and gas heating units and tanks
  • Retaining walls and solar panels
  • Central air conditioners and ductless units
  • Window and door replacement
  • Sheds over 100 square feet in residential districts

An application needs fees, a survey or plot plan, and contractor details: a Rockland County license plus workers' compensation and disability coverage. Building without a permit can bring prosecution and fines, so settle any past project that never got a final sign-off before you put the house on the market. Zoning-based denials go to the independent Zoning Board of Appeals. Call the department at (845) 359-8410.

Chapter 15 of the town code adds a certificate of compliance for property uses other than one- and two-family homes, and that certificate cannot be transferred to a new owner. Selling a single-family house falls outside it. Owners of multi-unit or commercial buildings should ask the department what applies to them before signing a contract.

Tax bills, due dates and penalties

Two bills arrive each year: town and county in January, school in the fall. One combined office now handles both the Town Clerk's work and tax collection.

Orangetown tax collection windows
BillMailing and due dateLate penalty
Town and countyMailed in early January for January 1 to December 31. Pay through January 31.1% through February 28, then 2% through March 31
SchoolMailed in early September for July 1 to June 30. Due September 30.5% until collection ends, usually October 31

After March 31, town and county bills left unpaid are passed to the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance. School bills end up there as well, and once the re-levy date arrives they reappear on the following year's property tax bill carrying a 7% penalty plus interest. The Orangetown tax office takes school tax payments for the Pearl River, South Orangetown, Nyack and Nanuet districts.

Selling with taxes owed

Village and school charges that went unpaid can be re-levied onto the property tax bill. Another trap: an exemption the previous owner had, which the new owner was not entitled to, can come back as a prorated charge. Either one can show up late in the sale.

Request a written balance from the tax office well ahead of closing and hand a copy to whoever is handling the paperwork. Whatever remains unpaid is normally settled from your sale proceeds on closing day, and knowing the number early keeps it from holding up the deed.

Older houses and hilly lots

The population climbed from 26,662 in 1940 to 53,533 in 1970, dipped to 46,742 by 1990, and was 48,655 in 2020. A lot of local housing dates to that mid-century boom. Your tax record lists the year built, and an older date points a buyer's inspector toward the heating, wiring and plumbing.

Terrain is uneven: rocky hills to the east, and the Nyack Hills climbing 300 to 500 feet beside the river. A retaining wall needs a permit, so if yours stands on a slope, check that it has one before listing.

Deed recording and transfer tax

The Rockland County Clerk records the deed when an Orangetown house sells, and the seller owes New York transfer tax at $2 for each $500 of price. Land records at the clerk's office are searchable online at any hour, a handy way to see exactly what is on file against your property.

File Form TP-584 with the clerk of the county where the house stands. Both the form and the tax must be in within 15 days after the deed is delivered. Homes selling for $1 million or more carry an extra one percent tax, which the buyer pays. Your attorney or title company normally drafts the deed and fills out the return.

Inherited the place? A transfer by devise, bequest or inheritance does not count as a taxable conveyance under state rules. Your attorney can tell you how the estate paperwork lines up with the sale date.

Paperwork for a quick closing

A fast closing mostly depends on documents being ready. Collect these first:

  • The current town and county bill and school bill, with a written balance from the tax office
  • Permits and certificates of occupancy for earlier projects such as decks, pools, heating units and retaining walls
  • Your deed, and any survey or plot plan you have
  • A New York attorney or title company ready to prepare the deed and the TP-584

With a cash buyer there is no lender appraisal or loan approval to wait for, which leaves title work, the deed and recording at the Rockland County Clerk. Insist on a written offer, agree on who pays each closing charge, and let your attorney review the contract first. Transfer tax and any tax payoff remain the seller's job.

Frequently asked questions

Does the Orangetown Building Department cover every address in the town?

No. The town's building authority covers the unincorporated hamlets. Nyack, Piermont and Grand View-on-Hudson are incorporated villages that run their own local government.

When are Orangetown school taxes due?

September 30. After that a 5% penalty runs until collection closes, usually October 31, and bills still open go to the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance.

Do I need a permit to replace windows in Orangetown?

Yes, windows and doors are on the town's permit list, along with a certificate of occupancy. A quick call to the Building Department settles any doubt.

Where is the deed recorded after an Orangetown sale?

At the Rockland County Clerk's office. Transfer tax of $2 per $500 falls on the seller, and Form TP-584 must be filed within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

How do I appeal a building permit denial in Orangetown?

Take it to the Zoning Board of Appeals, which is independent of the department. It hears permits turned down for zoning noncompliance and weighs each case on its own facts.

Listing versus an as-is sale

The answer depends on the house's condition and your deadline. Irondequoit boomed after World War II, which means an old roof, furnace or damp basement frequently tips the choice.

Roughly 78.8% of homes are owner-occupied and the midpoint value is $182,500. On a price like that, one big repair eats a noticeable share of the proceeds. Collect a contractor quote or two before you decide. Cosmetic fixes point toward a standard listing. A big repair list, an empty or inherited property, or unpaid taxes can make an as-is sale the cheaper way out, since it ends the monthly carrying costs.

  • Agent listing: reaches the most buyers, but you pay commission, host showings and wait on a buyer's loan.
  • Selling by owner: no commission, but the marketing, negotiating and paperwork are yours.
  • As-is cash sale: few contingencies and a closing day you frequently get to choose, generally for less money.

Have every bidder commit to price, closing date, proof of funds and closing costs on paper, then calculate your true take-home from each.

Town or city: check your tax bill

Irondequoit occupies the north-central part of Monroe County, wedged between the Genesee River and Irondequoit Bay, with Lake Ontario to the north. Rochester borders it to the south and west.

The line with Rochester has quirks. A narrow ribbon of city land follows the east bank of the Genesee northward, and the upper half of Durand Eastman Park and all of Seneca Park are city property, not town property. If your mailing address says Irondequoit but the house is near those parks, look at the tax bill to learn which government taxes it. Two school districts cover the town: West Irondequoit and East Irondequoit.

Local market snapshot

The town has about 50,200 residents, down 1.7% from the 2020 base. People 65 and over are 22.6% of the population, and estate sales are one reason houses come to market. Nearly 92% of residents were in the same home a year earlier, so listings are not plentiful, and a tidy house priced sensibly gets attention fast.

When are Irondequoit property taxes due?

Irondequoit homeowners get two tax bills a year from the Tax Office, which the Receiver of Taxes runs. Town and County tax arrives in late December and must be paid by February 10. School tax arrives in late August and must be paid by October 1.

Closed on the due date? Payment is accepted the next business day. A bill that never reached you does not erase the tax, and penalties cannot be waived by the office. Owners who pay directly rather than through escrow who have no bill a week after mailing should call 585-336-6050 for a duplicate. Monroe County's website displays bills as well.

For a parcel lookup, go to the county's Real Property Portal, accept its disclaimer, enter your street address and choose the Pay Property Taxes icon. School and combined town and county statements appear there with the payment history. Print the current pair for your closing attorney.

Assessment calendar

The town's tax year turns on eight dates, and a pending sale holds none of them back. Schedule your listing with them in mind.

  • March 1: taxable status date, and the last day to file new or renewal exemption applications.
  • May 1: the tentative roll goes public; a paper copy sits at Town Hall.
  • Third Tuesday in May: school budget vote.
  • Fourth Tuesday in May: Grievance Day.
  • July 1: final roll and valuation date. You have 30 days after it to ask for a judicial review (SCAR hearing).
  • Early September and early January: school bills and Town and County bills go out.

The final roll sets the figures for the next school and Town and County bills, which means a summer buyer inherits it. Review it before choosing an asking price.

How to challenge your assessment

File with the Assessor's Office any time from May 1 through Grievance Day, which is the fourth Tuesday of May. The next is May 25, 2027. You must go through this town step before a small claims review is available.

Bring Form RP-524 as one original and four copies, and attach backup documents for every board member. A hearing needs an appointment, and the paperwork has been due a week in advance. The assessor's tentative value is presumed right, so the proof falls on you. Recent appraisals, purchase contracts, comparable sales lists and a broker's written value opinion all count as credible evidence. Your tax bill does not count as proof of value.

The assessor may propose a stipulation before the hearing. You can decline it; if you accept, the assessed value is locked at the agreed number. If you still disagree with the board, a Small Claims Assessment Review in Monroe County Supreme Court is the next step, filed under Section 730 of the Real Property Tax Law for $30. The town also holds informal review appointments in the spring and keeps a comparable sales book of recent sales for owners to study.

Transfer tax and filing the deed

New York charges sellers $2 for every $500 of the price, though a contract can move that cost. Form TP-584 reports the tax. Residential prices of $1 million or more bring a further 1% charge for the buyer.

The Monroe County Clerk records Irondequoit deeds at 39 W. Main Street, Room 101, Rochester, NY 14614. Your closing attorney or title company usually drops them off. Your part is to sign where shown and keep copies of every page, since lenders and future buyers sometimes ask for them years later.

Checklist before accepting a direct offer

Add up your net after every cost, then check the calendar. A higher listing price can lose its edge to commission, repairs and months of mortgage, tax and utility bills.

  • Make the buyer commit in writing to who covers transfer tax and closing costs.
  • Ask for proof of funds and a fixed closing day.
  • Print the Monroe County portal statements so unpaid tax gets cleared at closing.
  • Ask a local agent for a listing-price opinion to use as a yardstick.
  • Let your own attorney go through the contract first.

A cash sale has no lender approval and no appraisal, the two steps that most often stall a financed closing. There are no showings or open houses either, so the house can stay as is while you pack. When taxes are owed, the closing attorney pays them out of your proceeds at the table, which is why current statements help.

Frequently asked questions

When is Grievance Day in Irondequoit?

Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday of May, which makes May 25, 2027 the next one. You can file from May 1 until then, and a hearing requires an appointment.

When are Irondequoit property taxes due?

Town and County tax is due February 10, School tax October 1. If the office is closed that day, the next business day works with no penalty.

How much does a small claims assessment review cost in Irondequoit?

The fee is $30 under Section 730 of the Real Property Tax Law, and Monroe County Supreme Court hears it. The town grievance has to come first.

Who pays the transfer tax when an Irondequoit house sells?

Sellers pay $2 per $500 unless the contract says otherwise. Buyers pay an added 1% when a residential sale hits $1 million.

Is Seneca Park part of Irondequoit?

No. Seneca Park and the northern half of Durand Eastman Park belong to the City of Rochester. If your house is near them, check which municipality taxes it.

Which Rye does this page cover?

Two places in Westchester County carry the Rye name, and this page is about the town, not the city. The town consists of the Village of Port Chester, the Village of Rye Brook and the Rye Neck section of the Village of Mamaroneck, and it holds around 11,000 parcels. The City of Rye became independent in 1942, so a house inside the city is handled by city offices, and the town assessor has no file on it.

The town comes in two separate pieces: Rye Neck lies to the southwest, apart from Rye Brook and Port Chester. Work out which village your street belongs to first. That one fact tells you who issues permits, who bills the village portion of your tax and which building department holds your certificate of occupancy.

Mid-2025 population is 50,011, a 0.8% rise since 2020. Two Metro-North stations and I-95 serve the area.

What are the ways to sell fast?

How fast you can sell depends on the condition of the house and when you need the cash.

  • Broker listing: works for a house that shows well and an owner who can wait out showings and a buyer's loan. Ask for a written estimate of net proceeds.
  • Owner-handled sale: you skip the broker fee but answer every inquiry yourself, with your own attorney on the contract.
  • Investor purchase for cash: the buyer takes the property as it stands. Estates, two-families with tenants and houses with open violations fit this route.

Westchester prices turn small percentage gaps into large sums, so compare what each path would actually put in your hands.

Assessment and tax calendar

Assessments are set at 100% of market value, which means your figure should roughly match a sale price. A few dates drive the cycle.

  • Taxable status date is May 1, which is also the last day to file for exemptions.
  • The tentative roll goes up June 1, with grievance day on the third Tuesday of June.
  • Board of Assessment Review decisions are mailed near September 15, when the final roll is filed.
  • Billing years differ by levy: county and town taxes follow the calendar year, village taxes run June to May, and school taxes run July to June.

The Receiver of Taxes takes payments and mail at 222 Grace Church Street, third floor, Port Chester. The Port Chester and Rye Brook village bills are each paid in two installments with their own windows.

How to challenge your assessment

File Form RP-524 with the assessment office in person, in the secure drop box, or as an emailed PDF. A mailed form must reach the office by 8 p.m. on grievance day, and a same-day postmark is too late. If the board's answer disagrees with you, a one-to-three-family owner can file a small claims petition electronically with the county clerk inside 30 days of the final roll, which makes October 15 the deadline.

Exemptions at a sale

The assessor needs exemption applications and renewals, senior citizen ones included, by May 1 each year. Basic and Enhanced STAR have moved to the state: new homeowners register with the Department of Taxation and Finance, and the town's assessor no longer takes STAR forms.

Limited-income seniors, owners with Cold War or alternative military-service exemptions, and volunteer firefighters can apply through the assessor. Tell your buyer early so they do not assume your current bill carries over untouched.

Permits and the certificate of occupancy

The town runs no building or planning department. The villages do, so permits and your certificate of occupancy sit with your village building department.

The assessor's property record card shows the use on file there, which does not prove the use is legal. Before listing, hunt down these items:

  • Permits and final sign-offs for any addition, finished basement or garage conversion.
  • The certificate of occupancy, which states the authorized use.
  • Zoning district and map, which come from the village building or planning office.
  • Radius and abutter search instructions, which also come from the village building department.

A cash buyer will often accept a house with a paperwork gap, and the offer will simply account for the cost of closing that gap.

Recording a deed in Westchester

Westchester's County Clerk records the deed through its online PREP portal, which also builds the cover page, the state TP-584 and the RP-5217 report. For a residential deed in a single municipality the fees are a $45 statutory fee, $5 a page, $5 for the TP-584 and $125 for the RP-5217.

State transfer tax adds $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up. The 1% mansion tax starts at $1 million and falls on the buyer. The clerk accepts transfer tax by ACH, certified or bank check, attorney escrow check or a check from an approved vendor, while credit cards cover fees only.

Steps from offer to closing

Once you accept an offer, the work splits between you, your attorney and the village. You gather the permit file and certificate of occupancy from your village building department. Your attorney asks the Receiver of Taxes for the current balances on the county, town, village and school bills. The buyer's side orders title work and, for a mortgage buyer, an appraisal. A cash buyer skips those last two, so title and the village paperwork set the pace.

At closing you sign the deed. It then goes through the county's PREP portal, where the cover page, the TP-584 and the RP-5217 are built together. Because Port Chester, Rye Brook and Rye Neck each bill separately, ask your attorney to confirm that every bill was paid and that the buyer knows which windows apply to the next installment. Telling the buyer early about exemptions that will drop off avoids a surprise at the first new tax bill, and it keeps the closing from stalling over a bill nobody expected.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Town of Rye the City of Rye?

No. The town contains Port Chester, Rye Brook and Rye Neck, while the City of Rye became independent of the town in 1942. Your tax bill and village will show which one applies.

When is grievance day for Rye property owners in the town?

The third Tuesday of June. The tentative roll appears June 1, which leaves roughly two weeks to file Form RP-524 with the assessor.

Can I sell my Port Chester or Rye Brook house without a certificate of occupancy?

You can try, but the buyer or their attorney will probably raise it. Ask the village building department what it has on record, and mention any gap to a cash buyer at the start.

Who pays New York transfer tax on a Town of Rye sale?

Sellers pay it by default. The rate is $2 for each $500 of the price, rounded up, and the buyer owes the extra 1% mansion tax at $1 million or more.

Where do Town of Rye tax payments go?

Mail them to the Receiver of Taxes at 222 Grace Church Street, third floor, Port Chester, NY 10573. The town's tax schedule page lists separate due periods for Port Chester, Rye Brook and Mamaroneck village taxes.

Choosing a sale route in Henrietta

Repairs and timing should drive your choice. Around Rochester's southern suburbs, three routes are realistic: an agent listing, a sale you manage yourself, or an as-is cash purchase. Owners live in about 70% of Henrietta homes and the rest are rented.

At a midpoint value of $223,700, even a few thousand dollars of commission or repairs cuts deeply into your proceeds. Price the work before you choose. A house needing only paint and a deep clean can go to market. One with a failing furnace, a wet basement or years of put-off upkeep may net about the same through a quick as-is sale.

  • Listing: the widest audience and usually the best price, at the cost of commission, repairs and a buyer's loan schedule.
  • By owner: you save the commission and take on pricing, showings and the contract.
  • As-is cash: fewer steps, and often a closing day of your choosing, at a price that covers the repairs.

Whatever you lean toward, get each offer in writing, showing the price, the date and each side's closing costs.

Henrietta at a glance

In southern Monroe County, Henrietta is roughly seven miles from downtown Rochester. The Genesee River forms its western edge, with Brighton to the north, Pittsford and Mendon to the east and Rush to the south. The town includes the hamlets of East Henrietta and West Henrietta and Riverton, a planned community. Rush-Henrietta Central School District serves it. Buyers like the quick Thruway and I-390 access, the 17.6 minute average commute, and the campus and retail district that keep the town busy.

About 48,800 people live here, 3.6% more than at the 2020 base. The 2025 estimate is 48,832 residents in 17,959 households of about 2.34 people. Owners occupy 69.8% of homes. The midpoint monthly cost for an owner with a mortgage is $1,720, rent is $1,344, and household income is $85,943. Just 78.7% of residents were at the same address a year earlier, which suggests turnover and plenty of renters. If your house was a rental, keep its rent history handy.

Property tax bills and where to pay

Henrietta's Receiver of Taxes is the Town Clerk's office. Two separate bills come from it each year.

Henrietta tax bills

Combined bill, Town and CountyLast business day of DecemberFebruary 10

Town Hall takes school tax payments only until early November. After that, any balance goes to the Monroe County Treasurer, who sets a cutoff in November for school tax payments, and anything still owing after that rolls onto the following year's Combined bill. The Treasurer can give you the current cutoff. Confirm at closing that the school bill is paid in full, so nothing carries onto the next owner's bill.

  • Town Clerk tax office: mail to Receiver of Taxes, Henrietta, P.O. Box 579, Henrietta, NY 14467; duplicate bills at 585-359-7035.
  • Monroe County Treasurer: 39 West Main Street, Room B-2, Rochester, NY 14614; phone 585-753-1200.
  • Online: the Monroe County Real Property Portal displays bills and what has been paid.

Due dates are the same with escrow. When a lender pays your taxes, it gets the bill, and after the loan is paid off you file a Bank Code Removal Request Form so the bill comes to you again.

The Assessor's Office

The Assessor's Office prepares the annual assessment roll, runs the grievance and tax certiorari process, administers exemptions including STAR, and manages the town's continuous revaluation. The town's assessor is a New York State certified assessor appointed to a six-year term. The office phone is 585-359-7032.

Ask it two things before you list. First, which exemptions the house carries, since STAR appears only on the school bill. Second, whether your parcel is part of any exemption correction. A notice on the office's page says some limited-income senior and disability exemption holders may get corrected school tax bills, and that an increase would be added to the 2027-28 school bill. A buyer will want to know what the taxes will be after the sale, so ask what applies to a new owner.

For a grievance, contact the office early in the year for the current window and form. Bring evidence of value to back it up, because the owner has to show the assessment is too high.

Transfer tax and deed recording

The state's transfer tax is $2 per $500 of price, and it falls on the seller unless the contract says otherwise. Form TP-584 reports the tax. Residences bought for $1 million or more carry an extra 1%, paid by the buyer.

For Henrietta deeds, the place is the Monroe County Clerk's downtown office, 39 W. Main Street, Room 101, Rochester, NY 14614, open 9 to 5 on weekdays. Email is the way to reach staff. The Clerk is the official registrar of deeds, mortgages, judgments and liens, and your attorney or title company normally brings the deed in.

Getting ready to list

Ask the Town Clerk's tax office for a duplicate bill before showings begin, and check that the school bill shows as paid. Ask which exemptions the Assessor has recorded. STAR appears only on the school bill, so a buyer will want to know what the bill will look like for a new owner. If a mortgage remains, request a payoff figure. Last, pick a closing date that fits your move, since a cash buyer can often work to it. Write that date into the offer, along with who pays each closing cost, so nothing is left to argue about at the table.

Cash sale or listing

Figure out your take-home first, then the calendar. A listing can fetch more, but commission, repairs and the lender's timeline come with it. An as-is cash sale gives up part of the price in return for speed and certainty.

  • Agree on who pays the transfer tax and closing costs.
  • Put proof of funds and the closing date on paper.
  • Check the school and Combined Town and County tax status with the Town Clerk or the Monroe County portal.
  • With tenants in the house, ask how the buyer will treat the lease.

In both cases an attorney or title company searches title, prorates taxes and files the deed. Paying cash means no wait for a loan, but any lien or unpaid tax still has to be cleared before title passes.

Frequently asked questions

When are Henrietta property taxes due?

February 10 is the due date for the Combined Town and County bill. The school bill is due October 1 in full, or in two parts with the first by September 15. Mailings go out on the last business day of December and of August.

Where do I pay a Henrietta school tax balance late in the year?

With the Monroe County Treasurer, at 39 West Main Street, Room B-2 in Rochester, phone 585-753-1200. Town Hall stops taking school tax in early November, and the county sets its own November cutoff.

Who handles exemptions and assessment grievances in Henrietta?

Call the Town Assessor's Office at 585-359-7032. It prepares the roll, runs grievances and tax certiorari, and administers exemptions such as STAR.

Who pays the New York transfer tax on a Henrietta sale?

Normally the seller, at $2 per $500 of price, though a contract can move it to the buyer. A separate 1% tax applies on residential sales of $1 million or more, and the buyer pays it.

Where are deeds recorded for a house in Henrietta?

Monroe County's Clerk records them, at an office on West Main Street in downtown Rochester. That office keeps the county's official files on deeds, mortgages, judgments and liens.

Selling in Niagara Falls?
We buy Niagara Falls houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Ways to sell a Niagara Falls house quickly

Sellers in Niagara Falls can go three ways: hire an agent, sell on their own, or accept a direct cash offer and set the closing date themselves. A cash deal avoids showings and haggling over repairs. City rules and paperwork below apply to all three.

Niagara Falls is the largest city in Niagara County, set on the Niagara River gorge about 16 miles from Buffalo. Population is 47,255, 3.0% below the 2020 base, and the city peaked at 102,394 people in the 1960 census, so the housing stock was built for a much larger population.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $115,300
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 58.5%
  • Median gross rent: $823 a month
  • Median household income: $49,101

With homes typically near $115,300, one big bill for a roof, boiler or foundation can eat a large part of the value. Many owners therefore compare an as-is sale with the cost of fixing up for a listing.

Older streets and neighborhoods

Industry shaped the older streets. Cheap hydroelectric power drew paper, rubber, plastics, petrochemical and abrasives plants, and many houses went up near them. Neighborhoods that buyers and sellers talk about include Deveaux in the northwest, built mostly in the 1920s to 1940s, Hyde Park beside the municipal golf course, Little Italy along Pine Avenue, the North End along Highland Avenue and the East Side between the gorge and Main Street. The city also has three national historic districts: Chilton Avenue-Orchard Parkway, Deveaux School and Park Place.

Winter wear on houses

Cold weather does the most harm. About 72.4 inches of snow fall each year on roughly 51 days, with thaws between storms. Cycles of freezing and thawing punish roofs, gutters, porches, chimneys and basement walls.

Water stains or a failing roof turn up in inspections, and the buyer will ask for a credit. Some owners avoid that by choosing a buyer who accepts the house as it stands.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Niagara Falls house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Code enforcement and rental rules

The city's Department of Code Enforcement handles permits, inspections and certificates of compliance, occupancy and capacity. Its permits page also hosts the landlord rental and property owner registration packet and the short-term rental requirements.

Renting the house out? Ask Code Enforcement if your registration is current before you sell, since a lapse can snag the closing. Short-term rentals have their own rules under the zoning ordinance:

  • Only the owner of record can apply, and only inside the designated short-term rental area.
  • Three or more units in one structure cannot be used as short-term rentals.
  • An owner needs a special permit first, valid for one year, and then a license within that year. The license renews annually.
  • Each of the permit and the license costs $250 for a single-family dwelling and $400 for a two-unit dwelling.
  • No outstanding property taxes, liens or other city fees can be owed when a permit or license is issued.

Running a short-term rental without both documents is illegal. An investor who wants to continue one will ask if you held a permit, so collect any paperwork you have.

Property tax due dates

Three bills arrive each year, each on its own schedule. You can pay at City Hall in Room 109 or online.

Niagara Falls tax calendar
Bill or stepTiming
City tax, first installmentJanuary
City tax, second installmentMay
Niagara County taxFebruary 15 to March 15, one installment
School tax, first installmentAugust
School tax, second installmentNovember
Taxable status dayMarch 1
Tentative roll and grievancesMay 1, with grievances May 1 to 31

County tax paid March 16 to April 15 carries a 2% penalty, and April 16 to May 1 carries 5%. Exemption applications run from October through February. Before closing, get payoff and proration figures for every bill from your attorney or title company.

Deeds and transfer tax

A Niagara Falls deed is recorded with the Niagara County Clerk, and the seller pays New York's transfer tax of $2 for each $500 of price, which equals $4 per $1,000.

The deed must come with a signed and notarized original, a TP-584 transfer tax form completed by both parties, and an RP-5217 real property transfer report that is downloaded and completed online. Recording hours are Monday to Friday, 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM, and the recording office number is (716) 439-7022. The TP-584 and tax are due no later than the 15th day after the deed is delivered, so closing attorneys and title companies normally file them with the deed.

A direct sale uses the same paperwork as a listed sale. The difference is speed, and the cash number is worth comparing against what a listing would net after repairs and carrying costs.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Niagara Falls houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Schools and getting around

The Niagara Falls City School District has the same boundaries as the city, so every house inside city limits belongs to one district. Six state routes pass through the city, along with the LaSalle Expressway. Amtrak stops at the Niagara Falls station, and NFTA runs transit with a hub at the Niagara Falls transportation center. The mean commute is 19.1 minutes, short enough to mention in a listing.

Questions buyers ask about the house

Buyers of older Niagara Falls houses tend to ask the same few things. How old is the roof, and has the boiler been serviced? Has water ever entered the basement? Are the permits for any past work closed, and is a certificate of occupancy on file? Is the house registered as a rental? Written answers prepared before showings begin keep the talks short and the price steadier. Hiding a problem rarely works, because an inspector will find it, and then the price drops further than an honest upfront discount would have.

Steps from decision to closing

Start with your deed and the latest bills for city, county and school tax. If the house is a rental, confirm the registration with Code Enforcement. A direct buyer can also review the house in person and quote a price quickly. Ask a contractor or an inspector what the roof, boiler and foundation need, then weigh the cost of fixing against an as-is offer. When you accept a buyer, your attorney or the title company orders the search, prepares the deed with the TP-584 and RP-5217, and prorates each tax bill to the closing date. A cash buyer skips the loan, so timing is set by the title work.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Niagara Falls house that needs a new roof?

Yes. A house with an aging roof can be sold as-is. A conventional buyer's inspector will likely ask for a repair or a credit, while a cash buyer builds the work into the offer.

Who records the deed after a sale in Niagara Falls?

The Niagara County Clerk records it. The deed goes in with a TP-584 and an RP-5217, and the seller pays transfer tax of $4 per $1,000 of price.

When is Niagara Falls school tax due?

School tax is due in two installments, August and November. City tax is due in January and May, and county tax is due from February 15 to March 15.

Do I need a permit to rent my Niagara Falls house short term?

Yes. The owner of record needs a special permit and then a license, at $250 each for a single-family house. Houses with three or more units cannot be short-term rentals, and unpaid taxes or liens block approval.

How do I contest my Niagara Falls assessment?

File a grievance during the May 1 to 31 window, after the May 1 tentative roll. Taxable status day is March 1, and the City Assessor's office can explain the form.

Palm Tree and Kiryas Joel

Palm Tree became an Orange County town on January 1, 2019, and its borders match the village of Kiryas Joel exactly. Voters approved the split from the Town of Monroe in a referendum on November 7, 2017, and a 2018 state law moved the start date up by a year. In 2019 residents also chose a single consolidated town and village government that operates like a village.

The footprint is only 1.5 square miles, so the population is dense: the April 2020 count was 32,954 and the mid-2025 estimate of 47,147 is 43.1 percent above that base.

Deeds, tax maps and surveys from before 2019 may name Monroe or the village, while newer records name Palm Tree. Check that the deed, the tax bill and the survey all describe your lot the same way before you list.

Housing in Palm Tree

Palm Tree has 7,505 households averaging 5.08 people. Only 33.4 percent live in a home they own, owner-occupied houses carry a median value of $758,800, and median rent is $1,604 a month. Owners pay a median of $2,616 a month with a mortgage and $1,075 without, and median household income is $50,032.

Appraisers look at how each unit is used, so keep floor plans, unit counts and rent figures handy.

Many residents speak a language other than English at home, and some prefer paper copies to email. If a seller or buyer wants another language or paper documents, tell your attorney and title company at the start. The disclosure form, contract and closing statement can then be explained in a way everyone follows, and signing will not depend on online portals.

Recording a deed in Goshen

Deeds are recorded at the Orange County Clerk's Record Room, on the second floor of the Government Center at 255 Main Street in Goshen. Documents on file there include deeds, mortgages, mortgage satisfactions, federal tax liens, judgments and lis pendens.

  • Office computers let the public search at no cost, and an online search site is also available.
  • Copies run 65 cents a page plain (minimum $1.30) and $1.25 a page certified (minimum $5.00).
  • Your own deed costs about $5 from the clerk, and the office cautions against outside firms that bill for the same copy.
  • A free Fraud Alert sign-up sends a notice whenever a deed or mortgage is filed under your name.

The clerk's office also provides notary services free of charge, which helps when a deed needs an acknowledgment. Search for judgments and liens against your name before you list. A seller who finds one early can arrange the payoff, and the title search will turn it up anyway.

Type of tax billUsual collection period

Because Palm Tree and Kiryas Joel are the same territory, ask the tax collector which of these bills apply to your parcel. Questions about delinquent amounts and penalties go to the county finance office at 845-291-2480.

Most communities in the state hold Grievance Day on the fourth Tuesday in May, so verify the date with your assessor. A complaint on Form RP-524 goes to the assessor or the review board at no charge, and only the current tentative roll can be contested. Ask Palm Tree's assessor for next year's date.

State transfer tax and forms

The state taxes each $500 slice of the price at two dollars, with partial slices rounded up, and the seller pays unless the contract moves it.

Form TP-584 is the combined return. File it with the county clerk by the 15th day after the deed changes hands, with the tax. A buyer owes a further 1 percent mansion tax if the residence costs $1 million or more.

Investors should note a separate rule. If an LLC sits on either side of a deal for a building of up to four units, the return is not accepted without names and addresses of its members, managers and authorized persons, and any member that is itself a business must be traced down to individuals. Collect those details before closing day.

On a typical closing day, your attorney or title company prepares the deed and the TP-584, collects the transfer tax from your proceeds, and files everything at the Orange County Clerk in Goshen. Ask beforehand who will carry the documents, and request a copy of the filed deed afterward for your records.

Which questions on the state form matter when a Palm Tree house is rented?

Before the buyer signs, the owner of a house with up to four units must supply the state's seller disclosure form. Selling as is remains allowed, and the form is no warranty.

Question 4 asks whether anyone besides the owner has a lease, easement or other right to use or occupy any part of the property. Since only 33.4 percent of households here own their homes, buyers tend to ask about leases and rents early, so pull together copies and a rent roll. Other topics on the form include certificates of occupancy, shared walls or driveways, flood zones, water and sewage service, detectors, and the roof, heating and plumbing.

With the town and village governments merged, ask Palm Tree town hall which office issues building permits and certificates of occupancy for your street. Get the reply in writing if work was done on the house.

Selling for cash

Owners with a deadline, deferred repairs or occupied units sometimes prefer a cash sale. Without a lender, closing turns on payoff letters, title clearance and recording in Goshen. Ask for terms in writing, find out who covers each transfer cost, and have a New York lawyer review the contract.

Prepare ahead. Gather your deed, the latest tax bills, copies of leases and a rent roll if any unit is occupied, and payoff letters for loans or liens. A buyer who sees complete records can order title work immediately, which keeps the closing date from slipping. If a lease runs past the planned closing, say so in the first conversation, since it changes who can move in and when.

Frequently asked questions

Is Palm Tree just another name for Kiryas Joel?

Their boundaries match. Palm Tree took over the village's territory when it separated from Monroe on January 1, 2019. A deed may name either one, so confirm which description your title company uses.

Where does a Palm Tree deed get recorded?

In Goshen, with the Orange County Clerk, whose Record Room is on the second floor of the Government Center at 255 Main Street. Owners can also enroll in the clerk's free Fraud Alert.

How is the state transfer tax figured on a Palm Tree sale?

At two dollars per $500 of price, rounded up. The seller normally covers it. A buyer owes the 1 percent mansion tax only when a residence reaches $1 million, and the TP-584 return and payment go to the county clerk within 15 days of delivery.

Which months does Orange County use to collect county and town tax?

Mostly January to March, with school bills running September to November. Periods vary by municipality, so the Palm Tree tax collector has the final schedule for your bill.

Do tenants have to be listed on the form for a Palm Tree house?

In effect, yes. Question 4 asks whether anyone other than the owner has a lease or a right to use or occupy any part of the property. Answer from your own knowledge, attach extra pages if needed, and hand the form over before the contract is signed.

Selling in a tight, dense market

Kiryas Joel is a small, crowded village in Orange County, and the housing market is tight. As of 2020, vacancy was 0.1% for owned homes and 2.5% for rentals, across 6,207 housing units (6.0% vacant) and 5,837 households.

The population is 47,147, up 43.1% over five years from the 2020 base. The typical owned home is worth $758,800, and 33.4% of households own. Gross rent is $1,604 at the midpoint. Households average 5.08 people, so bedroom counts and room layout carry weight. Since 95.3% of residents were in the same house a year earlier, a house that does come up gets attention. Be ready to describe bedrooms, kitchens and any additions.

  • Check that every addition and finished space has a closed permit and a certificate of occupancy.
  • Collect water and sanitation, village tax and town and county tax paperwork before the contract.
  • Decide whether to market privately, list publicly or take a cash offer.

Large households mean buyers look hard at how the space is used. Tour your own house the way a buyer would, counting bedrooms, bathrooms and kitchens that your certificate of occupancy actually allows. A finished basement or added floor needs its permit and final sign-off in hand. Attorneys usually request those papers before the buyer commits, and hunting them down early is easier than doing it mid-deal.

Village and Town of Palm Tree

Kiryas Joel is a village that now shares its boundary with the Town of Palm Tree. It incorporated in 1976 out of the Town of Monroe, and in 2019 the village separated from Monroe to form the new town. The village covers 1.1 square miles, with a 2020 density of 22,540.4 people per square mile.

Since the village and the town cover the same ground, ask the village which office holds the building and occupancy records for your house, and expect separate village and town bills at tax time.

Records for older work may sit with either government, depending on when the permit was issued. A phone call to the village before you list saves a scramble once a buyer's attorney starts asking.

Ask the same office how the village and the town divide permit work today, since the answer decides where you send an application for an addition and where a buyer's attorney requests the file.

Bills and utilities at closing

The village's official site runs a bill-payment page with three links: water and sanitation, the village property tax bill, and the town and county property tax bill. A closing therefore means settling at least three accounts, not one.

Who to contact for each closing item
Closing itemWhere it goes
Water and sanitationVillage bill-payment page
Village property taxVillage bill-payment page
Town and county property taxVillage bill-payment page, with county questions to Orange County's Department of Finance
Deed recordingOrange County Clerk, 845-291-2690

Prior to signing, request the current balance on each account from the village. Your attorney or title company orders tax searches and a water and sanitation reading so buyer and seller split the bills fairly on the closing date. Orange County's Department of Finance takes county questions about tax bills and needs the town and tax map number for the parcel. Assessment questions go to the local assessor, and the county's online parcel search can give you the tax map number if you lack it.

Because a tax question can involve both governments, ask for answers in writing and keep receipts in your closing file.

One practical habit helps: make a one-page list of the three accounts with the account numbers, the latest balances and the date you checked each. Hand it to the closing attorney with your deed. It answers the questions that otherwise arrive one at a time during the final week, and it shows a buyer that the house has been kept in good order.

Recording the deed and paying transfer tax

Deeds for Kiryas Joel properties are filed with the Orange County Clerk. Questions about filing costs and policies go to the clerk's office at 845-291-2690.

Recording charges are separate from New York's real estate transfer tax. Under Article 31 of the Tax Law, any conveyance over $500 is taxed at two dollars per $500 or fraction, due 15 days after the deed is delivered. Sellers are responsible; a buyer pays only when the seller is exempt or fails to. Residential conveyances of $1 million or more add a 1% tax charged to the buyer.

The clerk runs a free Fraud Alert service that tells owners whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded in their name. Getting a copy of your deed straight from the office runs approximately $5. Online record searching through the clerk's contractor costs $15 for one day of access, with printing at $5 per document. Skip any company that offers to obtain your deed for a fee, since the clerk warns about them.

Closing follows a plain sequence. Balances for taxes and utilities get confirmed, the deed and transfer tax return are drawn up, you sign before a notary, and the clerk receives the filing. Because the 15-day transfer tax period runs from delivery of the deed, ask your attorney who is tracking that date.

Is a cash offer a good choice for a Kiryas Joel house?

A cash offer is worth pricing out when you need a fast close, the house needs repair, or an estate must be settled among several heirs. A financed sale to a family buyer may bring more when the house is in good shape and your timeline is flexible.

Whatever you choose, get terms in writing, agree on who covers transfer tax and recording, and let a New York attorney review the contract. Confirm that your certificate of occupancy covers the present number of rooms and units, since an unpermitted conversion can stall a closing. Also make sure the water and sanitation account and both property tax bills are current on the closing date.

Without a lender or appraisal, a cash sale runs on title work, tax searches and the account readings above. Request those early and signatures become the only thing left to wait for.

With several heirs on the title, line up every signer before accepting an offer. A single absent signature can freeze the deed however eager the buyer is. Keep the deed, permits, account statements and signed contract in one folder and share a copy with your attorney.

Frequently asked questions

Which town is Kiryas Joel in?

The Town of Palm Tree in Orange County. From 1976 to 2019 the village belonged to the Town of Monroe, then split off as the Town of Palm Tree. Village and town share the same boundary.

Where do I record a deed for a Kiryas Joel house?

With the Orange County Clerk. Call the clerk at 845-291-2690 about filing costs. Normally your attorney or title company handles the deed at closing.

How much is New York transfer tax on a Kiryas Joel sale?

The seller pays $2 for each $500 of price, counting any fraction. Residential sales reaching $1,000,000 also trigger a 1% tax on the buyer.

What paperwork should I have ready to sell in Kiryas Joel?

Pull together your deed, permits and certificate of occupancy for additions, plus up-to-date water and sanitation, village tax and town and county tax statements. Expect the buyer's attorney to request each one.

How are the village's bills split when a house sells?

The village lists separate payment links for water and sanitation, village property tax and town and county property tax. Get a current balance from each before closing; your attorney or title company then divides the charges between you and the buyer as of closing day.

Quick-sale options in Perinton

Owners in Perinton may hire an agent, sell on their own or accept cash. A cash quote is worth getting when the house needs repairs or the closing date is tight. The town has just finished a townwide revaluation, so every parcel carries a new assessment and buyers will read it closely.

Perinton lies in eastern Monroe County about 10 miles southeast of Rochester. Local paperwork runs through the Assessment Office and the Building and Codes Department, both at Town Hall on Turk Hill Road, and the Monroe County Clerk in Rochester records deeds.

Perinton housing and who sells

The town covers 34.56 square miles and includes the Village of Fairport on the Erie Canal, plus hamlets such as Egypt and Bushnell's Basin. It had 47,479 people in 2020 and an estimated 46,823 on July 1, 2025. Owners occupy 79.2 percent of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $310,200, median gross rent is $1,349, and median household income is $112,093 across 20,347 households.

About a quarter of residents are 65 or older, so many sales involve retirees who are relocating, shrinking their space or closing out an estate. For them a reliable closing day can matter more than squeezing out the top price.

The 2026 revaluation

Every assessment was redone because the last full update came in 2018 and its equalization rate had slid from 100 percent to 57 percent. A revaluation adds nothing to the total tax collected. It only redistributes the same levy among owners, and the new values first appear on the 2026 to 2027 tax bills.

The Assessment Office mailed 18,234 preliminary notices and completed 2,152 informal reviews. The Board of Assessment Review received 819 applications and scheduled 334 in-person hearings. Together the reductions from preliminary values came to $189,622,437, or 2.1 percent of the roll.

Before setting a price, set the new assessment beside actual closing prices of similar houses, especially if you bought or sold under the old values.

How do I contest a Perinton assessment?

Taxes cannot be grieved, but the assessment can. Grievance Day for the next cycle is Tuesday, May 25, 2027, and applications are accepted from May 1 until 8:00 p.m. that day. A mailed form must arrive by the deadline regardless of its postmark.

  • File New York form RP-524, with all four pages completed and signed.
  • Submit one original and five copies of the form with its supporting papers.
  • Back it with evidence such as a closing statement, listing history, comparable sales, an appraisal or building costs.
  • Rental or commercial property calls for income and expense figures covering at least three years.

You do not have to appear in person. Decisions are mailed on or before July 1. After that, the final roll sets the school tax bill for September 1, the town and county bill for January 1 and any village bill for June 1.

Assessment timeline before you list

The assessment cycle gives a rough timeline. The Assessment Office inspects new construction, remodeling and demolitions from July 1 through March 1, and informal reviews open each October 1. The tentative roll is filed May 1 and the final roll July 1, so a sale in late spring happens while next year's number is still being argued.

Perinton assessment cycle
DateStep
October 1Informal reviews open
March 1Inspections for new work end and exemption applications are due
May 1Tentative roll filed and grievance applications open
July 1Final roll filed and Board decisions mailed by this date

Read your preliminary assessment notice and check it against recent sales on the town's sales file. Make sure each deck, finished basement or addition has a closed permit. Find out if the house is in Fairport village, where a village bill may apply. With the deed, payoff statements and exemption paperwork in hand, you can judge an agent sale, a private sale and a cash offer side by side.

Exemptions

Apply by March 1 for exemptions the town runs. The Assessment Office covers these:

  • Senior Citizen.
  • Persons with Disabilities and Limited Income.
  • Veteran exemptions.
  • Volunteer Firefighter or Volunteer Ambulance Worker.
  • STAR, which the State administers at tax.ny.gov/star or (518) 457-2036.

Seniors who already hold an exemption are mailed a renewal, and each renewal sets an intake appointment. Call the Assessment Office at (585) 223-0770 with questions. The buyer files after closing.

Building and Codes and your sale

Skipping a required permit can hold up a sale and may complicate an insurance claim. The town can also issue stop work or cease and desist orders until a permit is obtained. Permits are needed for decks, porches, three-season rooms, finished basements, garages, sheds, fireplaces, generators, fences, hot tubs and pools that hold 24 inches of water or more.

Re-roofing, re-siding, flooring, cabinet installation and replacing windows or doors without enlarging openings usually do not need one. A final inspection leads to a Certificate of Compliance or Occupancy, and the space cannot be used until one is issued. A home business needs both a building permit and a Certificate of Occupancy before it starts. Ask the Building and Codes Department for your address history before listing.

What to bring and what a cash sale skips

Pull together a folder before you call buyers: the deed, your latest school and town and county tax bills, proof of any exemption, permit records with the Certificate of Compliance or Occupancy for decks and finished basements, and payoff statements for any mortgage or lien. With it you can compare offers quickly.

A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal or loan approval, so the timeline depends on title work, the payoff and recording with the Monroe County Clerk. Ask for the offer in writing, find out who pays each closing cost, and have an attorney read the contract. If you hold an exemption, tell the buyer that it ends with the sale and the new owner files for their own.

Police, fire and unpaid taxes

The Monroe County Sheriff provides primary law enforcement, and the Village of Fairport has its own police department. Four volunteer fire protection districts split the town: Bushnell's Basin, Egypt, Forest Hills and Perinton. A house inside the village can also carry a village tax bill, so ask where the parcel sits.

Delinquent taxes lead to Monroe County's in rem foreclosure, so clear any balance before you sell. Recording a deed at the county costs $50 for the first page, and the state taxes the transfer at $2 per $500.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Did Perinton reassess every home recently?

Yes. The town completed a townwide revaluation in 2026, the first since 2018. The Assessment Office mailed 18,234 preliminary notices, and the new values appear on the 2026 to 2027 tax bills.

When is the next Perinton Grievance Day?

May 25, 2027, with filing open from May 1 and a final deadline of 8:00 p.m. that evening. Late or postmark-only mailings will not be reviewed.

Does a revaluation raise my taxes?

Not by itself. The town's tax levy is set through budgets, so a new assessment only changes how that total is shared. Your bill can rise, fall or stay level depending on how your value compares with others.

Is Fairport the same as Perinton?

No. The Village of Fairport is one part of the town of Perinton, located on the Erie Canal. A village tax bill may apply to parcels inside the village.

Can unpermitted work stop a Perinton sale?

It can. Work done without a required permit may hold up a sale and complicate insurance claims, and a space cannot be occupied until the Building and Codes Department issues a Certificate of Compliance or Occupancy.

Selling in Binghamton?

Binghamton housing at a glance

Binghamton is the seat of Broome County, and a sale here involves the city for permits, Broome County for tax collection and recording, and a housing market priced well below most of New York. The 2025 estimate is 46,418 residents, down 3.1% from the 2020 base. Of 21,393 households, only 44.0% own, so most households rent.

A typical owned home is worth $124,800 and typical rent is $870 a month. With values this low, a realistic price for your block depends on recent sales nearby. Look at your own street before relying on any citywide figure.

Floods, winter and the older house

Major floods hit Binghamton in 1865, 1935, 1936, 2006 and 2011. After the 1935 and 1936 events the city built flood walls along the Susquehanna and Chenango rivers, and Broome County maintains 17.5 miles of levees, many of them in the city.

  • Buyers near the rivers will ask about basement water, sump pumps and any past repairs. Gather receipts before you list.
  • Yearly snowfall averages 86.5 inches, so roof condition, gutters and heating systems get close attention in an inspection.

A house with water damage, an old furnace or a tired roof is a common reason owners here sell as is rather than paying for repairs first.

Who collects Binghamton property tax

Broome County collects it. The City Treasurer no longer collects property and school taxes. The county's tax office also handles in-rem foreclosures, bankruptcies and tax certificates for the city and the Binghamton City School District. Mail goes to the county's post office box in Binghamton, and you can also pay in person.

If back taxes are the reason you are selling, the county runs an installment program for delinquent owners in danger of foreclosure. It requires 25% down and 24 monthly payments at 1% monthly interest, and all new taxes must be paid on time during the plan. A sale that pays the balance at closing ends the problem sooner.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Binghamton house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Assessment complaints

The City Assessor handles assessments. A complaint goes on form RP-524 to the city's review board by Grievance Day. Call the Assessor's Office for the next date and file before it. A lower assessment helps whoever owns the house next, so a seller about to close gets little from filing late.

Permits for repairs before a sale

The Building Construction and Code Enforcement office requires a building permit under Section 200-9 of the city code for construction, alteration, removal, demolition and work on electrical, plumbing and HVAC systems. A permit must be on display before work begins.

  • Plumbing work in every kind of occupancy, including one- and two-family homes, must be done by a Master Plumber.
  • Demolition and work that affects a structural element need a permit, and landmark or historic-district buildings go through the Commission on Architecture and Urban Design first.
  • Street work, including a dumpster in the public right of way, needs a separate permit from the Department of Engineering.

The old grid near the rivers gives way to curving streets on the Southside hills, and the Railroad Terminal Historic District and the Abel Bennett Tract on the West Side are historic districts. If your house sits in one, expect design review before any demolition.

The First-Time Homebuyer Program loan

The city's First-Time Homebuyer Program gives deferred loans of up to $10,000 for down payment and closing costs. If title to the home is sold or transferred within 5 years, or it stops being the owner's principal residence, the whole loan comes due. After 5 years it is forgiven.

If you bought through this program, expect a payoff at closing and ask the Housing Division for the figure. The full loan is repayable from your sale proceeds when you sell inside the five years, so do the math before you agree to a price.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Binghamton houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Recording a deed in Broome County

Recording happens at the Broome County Clerk's office in the County Office Building on Hawley Street. The clerk estimates about $190 for a standard two-page residential deed once the state forms are counted. Sellers sign the deed before a notary, and the TP-584 and RP-5217 must be signed by both seller and buyer.

Broome County Clerk fees for a residential deed
Document or chargeFee
Deed$45 plus $5 per page
Transfer tax return (TP-584)$10 filing fee plus tax owed
Real property transfer report (RP-5217)$125 for residential property
Transfer tax in Broome County$5 per $1,000 ($4 state, $1 county)

Round an uneven price up to the next $500 before applying the rate. Houses at $1 million or more add a 1% buyer-paid tax. A seller who lives out of state also completes form IT-2663 for estimated income tax. The clerk's Fraud Alert service emails you when a document is recorded under your name, which is useful once the house is sold.

What a Binghamton closing looks like

Plan the sale in this order. First, find out who you owe: Broome County for taxes, the Housing Division if a first-time buyer loan sits on the house, and your mortgage lender. Second, ask the Code Enforcement office whether any permit on the house is open. Third, sign the deed in front of a notary, and have both parties sign the TP-584 and RP-5217. Fourth, the paperwork goes to the Broome County Clerk on Hawley Street, where the recording fees in the table apply.

A seller who lives out of state adds form IT-2663 to the stack. Ask your title company which charges it collects at the table so the net figure on your statement matches your expectations. When back taxes are in an installment plan, ask the county for a payoff letter, since the plan ends when the balance is paid off at closing.

A cash buyer can work from the same list. The difference is that no lender sits between you and the closing date, so the timing comes down to the title search and how quickly the payoffs arrive.

Choices for a Binghamton seller

An agent listing, a private sale and a cash purchase all work here, and the right choice turns on what shape the house is in and how soon you need to close. Listing suits a turnkey single-family home on a quiet block. A cash sale suits a house with flood history, a vacant two-family with code issues, or an inherited property that you would rather not renovate.

Before you accept any figure, pull the assessed value and recent comparable sales, price out the repairs a buyer would ask for, and confirm what, if anything, you owe in back taxes or program loans.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where do Binghamton tax payments go?

Pay Broome County's Real Property Tax Services. The county is the collection agent for the City of Binghamton and the Binghamton City School District, so the city treasurer no longer takes tax payments.

How do I contest my Binghamton assessment?

File form RP-524 with the city's review board by Grievance Day. Call the City Assessor's Office for the date.

What happens to my first-time homebuyer loan if I sell?

The full loan becomes due. Under the city's program, selling or transferring title within 5 years, or moving out of the home, makes 100% repayable. After 5 years the deferred loan is forgiven in full.

How much transfer tax will I pay selling in Binghamton?

Expect $5 per $1,000 of the price in Broome County, rounded up to the next $500. The state takes $4 of that and the county $1. Houses at $1 million or more add a 1% buyer-paid tax.

Is a permit needed for repairs before I sell my Binghamton house?

Yes, for most structural, electrical, plumbing and HVAC work. Section 200-9 of the city code requires a building permit displayed on site before work starts. Historic-district buildings get design review first.

Town of Poughkeepsie or City of Poughkeepsie?

Poughkeepsie is two municipalities, a city and a town, and this page is about the town. Your tax bill settles which one you live in in about a minute, and it spares you a wasted call to the wrong office.

The town sits in Dutchess County and curves around the city. Its communities include Arlington, Rochdale, Fairview, Red Oaks Mill, Spackenkill and the hamlet of New Hamburg. Once you know you are in the town, the selling work is short: tidy up the building file, understand how the tax bills arrive, and have the deed filed with the Dutchess County Clerk.

School districts matter to buyers. Different parts of the town belong to the Arlington, Spackenkill, Hyde Park and Wappingers districts, so copy the district name from your school tax bill into the listing or the disclosure form.

Housing and prices in the town

The town has about 45,986 residents, and roughly two of every three homes are lived in by their owners. A buyer comparing your house with the neighborhood will usually hold it up against the figures below.

Town of Poughkeepsie housing snapshot, 2020 to 2024 estimates
Housing measureTown figure
Households16,940
Owner-occupied share65.9%
Median home value, owner-occupied$354,900
Median owner cost per month with a mortgage$2,453
Median gross rent$1,677
Median household income$97,724

If your buyer plans to rent the place out, the $1,677 rent figure is a fair starting point for their math. Mail in the town can carry ZIP codes 12601 through 12604, and a small part uses the Wappingers Falls code 12590, so confirm the municipality before you rely on a ZIP code.

Town fees at sale time

The town's fee schedule prices most of what a seller is likely to need. A municipal violation search on a one or two family dwelling costs $175. If you ask for a certificate of occupancy for an existing building through that search, a residential property adds $25.

  • Temporary certificate of occupancy for a residence: $100 for each 90-day period.
  • Final water reading by town staff: $50 per appointment.
  • Water and sewer each run $3.00 per 100 cubic feet, with a $22.50 floor.
  • Reinspection of building, fire or plumbing work at a home: $50.
  • Accessory dwelling unit approval: $500, or $1,000 where a violation already exists, plus a $50 biannual accessory apartment inspection.

Residential work done without a permit carries a surcharge of $100 to $500, scaled to the cost of construction. If you added a deck, an apartment or a finished basement and never pulled a permit, sort it out before a buyer's search turns it up. Buyers' attorneys tend to ask for the certificate of occupancy early, so it helps to order the search as soon as you decide to sell.
