Running the house as a short-term rental

The town allows short-term rentals within limits. Chapter 168A of its code covers them, and the fee schedule prices hosted and unhosted stays separately.

  • Hosted, with the primary resident there overnight: $300 for one bedroom plus $50 for each added bedroom.
  • Unhosted in a primary residence: $600 for one bedroom plus $300 for each added bedroom.
  • Unhosted and not a primary residence: $2,000 plus $500 per extra bedroom, and the Town Board must approve it.

A buyer who wants to keep the house as a vacation rental will ask where that stands. If you ran one, tell the buyer's attorney, then ask the town whether the approval stays with the owner or has to be filed again after the sale.

Zoning letters that can speed a closing

Some houses have an odd layout or an addition nobody can document. Three town letters can settle a buyer's questions, and each has a fixed price.

  • Zoning compliance letter: $200 for a residential property, with $25 more for each additional dwelling.
  • Rebuild letter for a single-family home: $200.
  • Determination of legal nonconformity by the Zoning Administrator: $200, or $500 if the application goes to the Zoning Board of Appeals.

The schedule also lists a $75 fence permit and a $300 area variance for a single-family home, rising to $500 when the work already exists. When an attorney spots a nonconforming garage apartment or an oversized shed, a letter in hand cuts down the back and forth. A lot line revision starts at $100 plus a Planning Board fee per meeting, which rarely suits a quick sale.

How property taxes are billed

The town and county bill goes out from the Receiver of Taxes in late January, and the last day of February is the penalty-free deadline. You can pay in three installments. Payments made after that add 2% from March 1 to May 31 and 4% from June 1 to August 31.

School tax arrives separately. It is billed in September after Labor Day and is payable without penalty within 30 days, though each district sets its own due date. With four districts in the town, two neighbors can owe different school bills.

For questions about exemptions and relief programs, the Receiver sends people to the Assessor's Office. Ask the Receiver for a memo bill, listed at $5 on the fee schedule, so your closing attorney can prorate taxes correctly.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Poughkeepsie houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Filing the deed in Dutchess County

The Dutchess County Clerk accepts the deed. Its fee schedule lists $45 for recording, $5 for every page, $0.50 per cross reference and $5 for the TP-584 capital gains affidavit. The RP-5217 transfer report costs $125 where boxes 7a, 7b or 7e apply and $250 in other cases. Since March 11, 2020, a $10 residential deed notification fee has also applied under Real Property Law section 291.

Before any contract is signed, New York requires you to hand the buyer a property condition disclosure form. It asks about the water source, the sewage system and any certificate of occupancy, so pull those answers from your town file ahead of time.

What to gather before you list

A little preparation shortens the path from accepted offer to closing, whether the buyer uses a mortgage or pays cash.

  1. Find out which village or school district appears on your bills, and confirm the town is the right municipality.
  2. Order the municipal violation search and certificate of occupancy request.
  3. Collect permits and final sign-offs for decks, basements and apartments.
  4. Ask the Receiver of Taxes for a memo bill so the attorney can prorate.
  5. Have the deed, the TP-584 and the RP-5217 ready for the county clerk.

A cash buyer skips the appraisal and lender underwriting, so open items on the property are weighed in the price rather than holding up a loan. A traditional sale reaches more buyers, but repairs, inspections and mortgage approval stretch the timeline.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Town of Poughkeepsie the same as the City of Poughkeepsie?

No. They are separate municipalities, and the town wraps around the city. Check your tax bill to see which one bills your property.

How much is a municipal violation search?

The town charges $175 for a one or two family dwelling. A certificate of occupancy for an existing building, requested through that search, adds $25 for residential property.

What is the deadline for the town and county bill?

The bill arrives in late January and carries no penalty through the end of February. School taxes are billed after Labor Day, with 30 days to pay.

Where is a town deed filed?

With the Dutchess County Clerk. Bring the deed, the TP-584, the RP-5217 and the recording fees, which start at $45 plus $5 per page.

Does my Poughkeepsie house need a zoning letter to sell?

Not automatically. A buyer's attorney may ask for one if a use or addition looks irregular, and the town charges $200 for a residential letter.

Selling a West Seneca house: the basics

West Seneca is a built-out Buffalo suburb, so the condition of the house and its paperwork set the timeline more than land does. Central Erie County is home to the town, bordered by Buffalo and Lackawanna on the west, Cheektowaga on the north, Orchard Park on the south, and Elma and Lancaster on the east. It spans 21.4 square miles and has held steady near 45,000 residents since 2000, with 45,500 counted in 2020.

Areas buyers ask about

Gardenville and New Ebenezer lie in the north, East Seneca follows Route 16, and Ebenezer is in the center. Cazenovia Creek and Buffalo Creek cross the town.

Roads matter to buyers here. The New York State Thruway (I-90) crosses the western part of town and meets NY 400, the Aurora Expressway, and U.S. 219 reaches the southwest corner. NY 16 (Seneca Street and Center Road) and NY 354 (Clinton Street) run east and west, while NY 240, NY 277 (Union Road) and Transit Road (NY 78) run north and south.

  • Northern streets near Gardenville: close to Cheektowaga and Buffalo.
  • Central Ebenezer and Union Road: near Town Hall.
  • Along Route 16 and NY 400: quick access to the expressway.
  • Southern streets near Orchard Park: edges of the Orchard Park school district.

School district for your address

Public schools come from three districts. West Seneca Central is the largest and serves most addresses, while some parcels fall in Orchard Park Central or the Cheektowaga-Sloan Union Free School District. Find out which one applies before advertising, as it also determines the separate school tax bill. Buyers who ask about schools will expect a straight answer, and having one ready makes the listing look careful.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your West Seneca house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax on a West Seneca sale

On top of the state charge, Erie County levies its own transfer tax. Together they come to $4.50 per $500 of price: $2.00 to the state and $2.50 to the county. Prices are rounded up to the next $500. The seller owes it, and it is paid at the clerk's counter when the deed is submitted.

Sellers aged 62 or older who have owned and lived in a single-family or two-family house for at least a year can claim the lower $2.00 rate with an affidavit filed at the clerk's office. Separately, the buyer owes a 1 percent mansion tax once a residential price reaches $1 million.

Erie County Clerk recording fees

The clerk's list is brief. Accepted payment includes cash, check, money order, cashier's check, Visa, MasterCard and Discover.

Erie County Clerk charges to record a residential deed

RP-5217 for other property$250.00

Transfer tax is billed in addition to everything in this table.

Property tax dates and exemptions

Assessments are handled in Room 211 of Town Hall at 1250 Union Road, and the Town Clerk collects taxes as Receiver from Room 212 down the hall. Town and county bills arrive in mid-January with a February 15 due date, after which a penalty applies. School bills arrive in mid-September with an October 15 due date. The town hands unpaid town and county taxes to Erie County on July 1 and unpaid school taxes on December 1.

Partial payments are accepted in the office. Credit card payments carry a convenience fee of 2.45 percent, and e-checks carry a $1.75 fee. The town discourages bank bill pay because those mailings lack a U.S. postmark. Check the current bill, since due dates and fees are set each year.

Exemption applications for the 2027 roll are due by March 1, 2027. The exemptions on offer include:

  • Senior citizens: a cut of 5 to 50 percent in assessment for homeowners aged 65 and up whose combined income is under $37,400.
  • Persons with disabilities and limited income: the same 5 to 50 percent range, with income under $32,400.
  • Military service: 15 percent of assessed value up to $18,000, with added amounts for combat service and disability.

The state now runs the STAR program directly, and the town no longer accepts STAR applications.

Permits and rental registration before closing

Building, plumbing and electrical permits and their inspections come from the Code Enforcement Office. An inspection is not scheduled without a house number and a permit, and a certificate of code compliance follows only once the required inspections pass. A deck, finished basement or addition built without paperwork is something to raise with the office now, asking how to close it out.

A landlord must also register each rental with the Town Clerk's Office by filing a Rental Housing Business License Application. If the house has had tenants, make sure that registration is current and tell the buyer. The Code Enforcement Office can answer questions at 716-558-3242.

What happens between offer and closing

Several offices handle pieces of a West Seneca sale. Town Hall at 1250 Union Road holds the assessment in Room 211 and the tax collection in Room 212. The Code Enforcement Office has the permit file. The Erie County Clerk records the deed and collects the transfer tax at the counter.

Start by checking the current tax bill. Town and county taxes are due February 15 and school taxes October 15, so the timing of your closing decides who owes which installment. Any balance the town hands to Erie County on July 1 or December 1 has to be cleared with the county before title can move. Ask your attorney to confirm the figures in writing, and remember that the buyer's attorney will ask for the same numbers.

When a cash buyer fits

Cash makes sense for a house with open permits, a rental history or deferred repairs, because there is no appraisal to fail. Compare offers by the amount you keep after transfer tax, payoff and tax adjustments.

Ahead of the first showing, gather the deed, current tax bills, permit records and any rental registration. Request a payoff letter from your lender and confirm that everyone on title will sign. Fewer loose ends for the buyer and the title company means a faster close.

Frequently asked questions

How much transfer tax does a West Seneca seller owe?

It is $4.50 per $500 of the price, made up of $2.00 for New York State and $2.50 for Erie County. The seller pays at recording, and the price is rounded up to the next $500.

Do West Seneca seniors get a lower transfer tax rate?

Yes. A seller aged 62 or older who owned and lived in a single-family or two-family house for at least a year can pay $2.00 per $500 instead of $4.50. The Erie County Clerk provides the affidavit at no charge.

Which dates matter on a West Seneca tax bill?

February 15 for town and county taxes, with bills mailed in mid-January, and October 15 for school taxes. Town and county balances move to Erie County on July 1, and school balances move on December 1.

Must a rental house be registered with the town before it is sold?

The town requires rental property owners to register with the Town Clerk's Office through a Rental Housing Business License Application. If the house has been rented, confirm the registration is current before you sell.

Where do West Seneca owners apply for tax exemptions?

At the Assessor's Office, 1250 Union Road, Room 211. Applications for the 2027 roll are due March 1, 2027, and STAR is now run by the state, so contact the New York State Tax Department for that program.

Fast sale options in Mount Pleasant

Two routes move quickly here. One is a listing priced and staged to draw offers within a few weeks. The other is an as-is sale to a cash buyer, which gives up some price but removes repairs, open houses and the financing contingency.

Homes in Mount Pleasant sit at a high price point. A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $788,900, and a roof, a service panel or a permit clean-up at that level can cost tens of thousands. Some owners would rather hand that project to a buyer who wants it.

Either way, start the same folder: your deed, a recent Receiver of Taxes bill, the mortgage payoff letter, and permits or occupancy certificates for any work done on the property.

Who buys in Mount Pleasant

The town is growing and well off. Population is 45,444, up 2.2 percent on the 2020 base, and owners live in 70.5 percent of homes. There are 15,312 households with a middle income of $142,857, and rent runs around $1,941.

Buyers at this price borrow heavily, and their lenders insist on clean paperwork. Open permits and missing certificates are what most often stall a mortgage closing in town.

Villages and hamlets inside the town

Mount Pleasant holds several villages and hamlets, and your address decides which offices you deal with. Sleepy Hollow and Pleasantville are villages, Thornwood lies just south of Pleasantville, and Valhalla, home to Town Hall, is in the southeast. Hawthorne, Pocantico Hills, Scarborough and Archville are hamlets, and part of Briarcliff Manor is inside the town.

Eight school districts reach into the town, so your tax bill is the best proof of which one serves your lot. Tell buyers early.

Tax due dates and late charges

The Receiver of Taxes collects for the county, the town and every school district. Your bill shows which district covers your lot.

Mount Pleasant tax calendar and late charges
BillDueLate charge
County and townApril 302% in May, climbing to 12% January through April
School, first halfSeptember 302% in October, 5% in November, 7% December to January
School, second halfJanuary 3110% in February and March, 12% in April

The Receiver cannot waive a penalty once a deadline passes, and parcels left unpaid for 21 months go to foreclosure. You can pay at Town Hall in Valhalla on weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, by mail with a U.S. postmark, or online. A card carries a 2.25 percent fee online, and an electronic check carries none.

If your sale closes after the September payment, the January half still comes due. The town tells sellers to alert the buyer, so write who pays it into the contract.

Assessments and exemptions

Valuation, transfer records and exemptions all run through the Town Assessor. Grievance Day is the third Tuesday of June, and exemption applications close June 1.

  • Informal review requests go in writing by the last business day of March, ahead of the June 1 tentative roll, and none are handled between April 1 and August 1.
  • Exemptions cover STAR, seniors, military service, people with disabilities, and volunteer firefighters or ambulance workers.
  • Dividing assessed value by the residential assessment ratio gives the office's market value estimate.
  • Send plans, a description of the work and a cost estimate, and the office will say in writing how a renovation might move your assessment.

Buyers should phone the Receiver so bills reach them. Sellers can ask the Assessor which exemptions sit on the parcel before the deed is signed. Forms are posted on the town's Assessor page.

Building department steps before closing

The Building Department issues a certificate of occupancy or compliance once the permit, fees, final inspection and a notarized Affidavit of Final Cost are done. Electrical work also needs its own certificate.

This matters most for an aging deck, a finished basement or a new roof. Permits are needed for additions, boilers, central air, decks, fences, hot tubs, interior alterations, permanent generators, pools, retaining walls, roofs, solar panels, sheds, storage tanks and stair changes. Unpermitted work blocks the certificate and can bring a stop-work order and fines.

Permit review can take four to six weeks. Filings go through the Online Service Center without paper, and plans must cite the 2025 building code. Removing an oil tank takes building and plumbing permits plus inspections, and tanks of 1,100 gallons or more must be registered with the Westchester County Department of Health. Villages sit inside the town, so ask whether your address answers to the town building office or a village office.

A buyer paying cash for the house as-is can accept open items, which may spare you the clean-up.

Variances and unapproved space

Owners with an unapproved basement apartment or an addition that breaks a setback may need a variance. Accessory apartments, site plans and variances go through Planning and Zoning, a division of the Building Department.

A variance applicant submits surveys and plans, publishes the public notice in the Journal News, mails notice to neighboring owners and files at least 15 days before a Zoning Board meeting. That is a long road to take just to sell, so weigh it against a buyer who accepts the house unchanged.

Recording the deed and transfer tax

Deeds go to the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division. Its fee schedule starts with a $45 statutory fee, and because Mount Pleasant spans several municipalities, a $0.50 charge for each extra town named can apply to a parcel on a boundary. The clerk's own example, a three-page residential deed in one municipality, comes to $190 in fees.

State transfer tax is figured on the price rounded up to a multiple of $500 and is due when the deed is presented. Sales at $1 million or more add a buyer-paid one percent, the so-called mansion tax. Your closing attorney will handle the filings, but ask for the totals ahead of time so nothing surprises you at the table.

Steps from first call to closing

A sale here follows a predictable order. First, collect the deed, tax bills and any permit paperwork. Second, ask the Building Department whether any permits for past work are still open, since those are the items that surprise sellers late. Third, get your payoff letter from the lender. Then compare offers on what you actually keep, counting repairs a buyer will ask for against the discount a cash buyer wants.

At the closing you sign the deed, the transfer tax return and the closing statement. Keep your own copies. If the Receiver of Taxes still shows a balance on the parcel, it should be paid from your proceeds at the table, and a call to that office a few days before closing will tell you the exact amount.

Frequently asked questions

What are the property tax due dates in Mount Pleasant?

April 30 for town and county tax, then September 30 and January 31 for the two school halves. Penalties start the next month and the Receiver cannot forgive them.

What is the typical home value in Mount Pleasant?

About $788,900 for owner-occupied homes, set against a middle household income of $142,857 and rent near $1,941.

Does the town require a certificate of occupancy before a sale?

The town issues it when permitted work clears final inspection, and unpermitted work stops it. Mortgage lenders may ask to see it, though a cash purchaser can take the house as it is.

How much do recording fees run in Westchester?

The clerk's example of a three-page residential deed is $190, with extra pages billed separately and transfer tax added.

Who owes the mansion tax in Mount Pleasant?

The buyer, at one percent of a $1 million or higher price on a residence. Sellers are liable only when the buyer fails to pay.

How fast can a Webster house close?

Weeks, not months, when the title is clean and no lender has to approve the buyer. The local checkpoints are the town's building file, the tax bills and the deed filing in Rochester. Webster has water on two sides, so a few questions are specific to shoreline parcels, but the paperwork is plain once you know which office holds which piece.

The Town of Webster occupies the northeastern corner of Monroe County, with Lake Ontario to the north, Irondequoit Bay to the west, Penfield to the south and Wayne County to the east. It had 45,327 residents in 2020, up from 42,641 in 2010. A village of the same name sits at the center of the town, and the whole area is part of the Rochester metro.

Webster neighborhoods and housing

Webster grew quickly in the second half of the 20th century, from 7,174 residents in 1950 to 16,434 in 1960 and 24,739 in 1970, so much of the housing is mid-century or later.

  • Lake Ontario side: Lake Road (also called Fieldcrest), Forest Lawn and the streets near Webster Park, which covers 550 acres along the waterfront.
  • Irondequoit Bay side: Glen Edith on the west edge of town.
  • Village of Webster: the center of the town.
  • Oakmonte: a large south-central neighborhood of private homes, apartments and town homes.

Other areas include Parkwood off Klem Road and the hamlets of West Webster and Union Hill. If your parcel fronts Lake Ontario or Irondequoit Bay, ask the town's Building Department what is on file for it, and keep copies of any permits for the buyer.

School and fire districts

The Webster Central School District teaches kindergarten through grade 12 in town, with middle schools Spry and Willink and high schools Thomas and Schroeder. The Assessment Office lists both the Webster and Wayne central school districts among the jurisdictions that tax off its roll, so confirm your district on your tax bill.

Fire protection splits in two. The West Webster Fire District covers the west side, and the North East Joint Fire District covers the east side, including the village. Both are all-volunteer departments.

Tax bills, exemptions and payment

The Webster Assessment Office keeps the roll that Monroe County, the town, the Webster and Wayne central school districts, special districts and the Village of Webster all use to set taxes. The roll holds each property's valuation and exemptions. Exemption applications and renewals are due March 1 each year, and a late application may count for the next tax year.

Town and county bills are mailed on or about December 31. The Receiver of Taxes at 1000 Ridge Road collects them from January 1 through May 31. School tax runs September 1 through October 31 for Webster, Walworth and Ontario residents in the Webster school district. If your taxes are escrowed, the bill goes straight to your lender.

Town Hall takes no credit or debit cards, though Monroe County's online portal does, for a fee. The town discourages online bank bill pay because those payments can arrive after the due date and pick up interest. Before closing, ask the Receiver's office for a balance statement, and pull the property record through the Beacon search the Assessment Office links to.

Permits the Building Department cares about

The Building Department at 1000 Ridge Road enforces the New York State Uniform Code and local zoning. Before listing, check whether any of the following exist at your house and whether a certificate was issued.

  • Decks, additions, accessory buildings and utility sheds.
  • Fences, swimming pools and hot tubs.
  • Roof replacement and interior remodeling that changes electrical, plumbing or structure.
  • Roof or ground-mounted solar panels and standby generators.

Painting, flooring, cabinets, appliances, like-for-like window and door replacement, patios under 12 inches above grade, and swing sets need no permit. When a project does need one, the town issues a certificate that must be in hand before the structure is used or occupied. For work that needs an electrical inspection, the town points owners to three inspection agencies. Staff will tell you by phone on weekdays whether a given project required a permit.

Monroe County Clerk deed charges

Deeds for Webster property are filed with the Monroe County Clerk at 39 West Main Street in Rochester. Get in line before 4:30 in the afternoon if you want same-day recording. A deed needs a completed TP-584 and RP-5217, and the clerk's charges are below.

From contract to closing in Webster

Once a buyer signs, the work moves between three places. Town Hall at 1000 Ridge Road holds your tax payment record and your building file. The Assessment Office confirms exemptions and the school district. The Monroe County Clerk in Rochester records the deed after closing.

Ask the Receiver of Taxes for a balance statement early, because town and county tax can be paid through May 31 and a buyer's attorney will want to know what remains. If the house has a deck, pool, shed or finished space, find out whether a certificate was issued, and call the Building Department if you are unsure. Staff can answer by phone on weekdays whether a project needed a permit.

On filing day, the deed travels with the TP-584 and the RP-5217. Anyone who wants same-day recording should be in line at the clerk before 4:30 in the afternoon, so tell your attorney or title company if timing is tight.

Is a cash buyer right for a Webster property?

A cash buyer suits owners who need a fixed closing day, would rather skip staging and open houses, or hold a property whose repairs would trouble a lender's appraiser. It trades some price for certainty. Listing is the better path when the house is in strong condition and nobody is hurrying you.

Either way, assemble the same folder: recent tax bills, permits and certificates for any work done, the mortgage payoff letter, and for an inherited house, proof of who may sign. Buyers and title companies work faster from a complete file.

Frequently asked questions

Who collects property taxes in Webster, NY?

The Receiver of Taxes at Webster Town Hall, 1000 Ridge Road. Town and county taxes are collected from January 1 through May 31, and school taxes from September 1 through October 31. The town and county bills are mailed on or about December 31.

Can a Webster owner pay property tax by card?

Only online. Town Hall does not take credit or debit cards, but Monroe County's property tax portal accepts a card or an electronic check, with a fee added.

What does filing a deed with Monroe County cost?

A one-page deed is $50, plus $5 for each added page. Expect $5 for the TP-584, $125 or $250 for the RP-5217 depending on the property, a $10 residential deed fee, and transfer tax of $4 per thousand of the price.

By what date must Webster exemption forms be filed?

March 1 each year. Forms received afterward may be considered for the following tax year, and you may need to refile with updated information.

Does painting or replacing windows in Webster require a permit?

Usually not. The town treats painting, flooring, cabinets and like-for-like window and door replacement as work without a permit. Roof replacement, decks, pools, fences and sheds do require one.

Three ways to sell a Lancaster house

Homeowners here choose between an agent, a self-found buyer and a cash purchase. Timing and the building's condition drive the choice. If you have a neat ranch and no deadline, listing makes sense. If the roof is failing, a probate is pending or a tenant is refusing to leave, a fast as-is buyer is the likelier fit.

  • Owner-handled sale: you decide price and terms while your attorney writes the contract and deed.
  • Cash purchase: the buyer accepts the property as it stands, so there are no repair requests and no mortgage contingency.

Whichever you pick, the sale ends with a notarized deed, transfer tax forms filed with the Erie County Clerk, and any back tax on the parcel paid off.

Lancaster town and villages

Lancaster sits in Erie County, roughly 11 miles east of downtown Buffalo, on about 37 square miles. Two villages lie inside it, Lancaster and Depew. Population is 45,075, close to the 45,106 counted in 2020.

Five school districts bill Lancaster addresses: Lancaster Central, Depew Union Free, Alden Central, Clarence Central and Iroquois Central. Lancaster Central covers most of the town, though buyers should hear the district named on your own tax bill. Driving is simple: the Thruway (I-90) runs across the north end, US 20 follows Broadway through the center, and NY 78 (Transit Road) marks the western side.

Owners near Broadway in the village should ask the village what historic review applies before promising a buyer a facade or window project. The Building Department's page carries a Village of Lancaster historic preservation application.

Home values and household figures

Owner-occupants hold about four in five homes, and the middle one is worth $277,600. No midpoint prices a specific house, so pull recent sales from your own area before picking a figure.

Gross rent is $1,079 at the midpoint and household income $89,080. The town counts 19,722 households, and 22.1% of its residents are 65 or older. A 20-minute average commute is one of the quieter selling points for a house here.

Building Department and past renovations

Earlier renovations sometimes surface during a sale. The Building Department enforces the state building and fire code, zoning, stormwater practices and flood plain rules across both the town and the village, and nobody may build, alter, move or demolish a structure without a permit.

The office posts applications for decks, fences, pools and hot tubs, sheds, signs, demolition and one- and two-family dwellings, along with a handout on as-built survey requirements. If a deck, an addition or a finished basement went in before you bought, ask whether the project is on file and was signed off. A clear answer saves negotiating time later.

  • Inspections tied to a permit are booked by phone with the office, which keeps weekday hours.
  • The department also links resources on vacant and "zombie" properties, handy for an inherited house that has sat empty.
  • Truck routes and yard sale permits are separate matters handled through the town and its Highway Department.

Before listing, ask the office for the permit file on your address and read it once. Knowing what is recorded lets you answer a buyer's attorney the same day.

Tax deadlines and late payments

Pay Town and County tax by February 15 and school tax by October 15. A weekend or holiday pushes either date to the next day. The tax office inside the Town Clerk's office collects both. For mailed checks the postmark must show the due date or earlier. The office allows no exceptions.

Lancaster late-payment rules

The town office takes Town and County payments through June 30 and school payments through November 30. Past those dates, payments and payoff questions go to Erie County Real Property Tax Services in Buffalo. Because interest changes the payoff monthly, get the county's number before choosing a closing date.

If you cannot pay before the school deadline, the unpaid amount moves to the county after November 30 and costs more every month. Selling a house with that balance is workable: the payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, and the buyer's attorney will want the county's written figure.

Erie County deed charges and transfer tax

Sellers here pay two layers of transfer tax, the state's $2.00 and the county's $2.50, which makes $4.50 per $500 of price. The Clerk rounds the price up to the next $500.

Recording costs a $45 statutory fee plus $5 a page. Filing the TP-584 is $10, and the RP-5217 report is $125 for residential property. The deed must carry original signatures, a notary's acknowledgment, a full legal description and street addresses for every party, since P.O. boxes are rejected.

  • Owners 62 or older who have lived a year or more in a one- or two-family house may qualify for a reduced $2.00-per-$500 rate.
  • Buyers of residential property at $1 million or above owe an extra 1% mansion tax.
  • The Clerk also asks for a Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership on residential property.

File the TP-584 and pay within 15 days of delivering the deed. After closing, end your STAR registration so the next owner can sign up for the credit.

Sorting out a damaged or inherited house

Storm or fire damage does not stop a sale. Offer the house as-is to investors, list it at a repair-adjusted price, or accept cash from a buyer who skips the repair list. Ask the Building Department about open permits first.

Cash buyers do not need an appraisal or a loan approval, so nothing there delays you. The sequence runs from a written offer to a title search, then signing the deed and transfer forms, then payment on closing day. Bring your latest tax bills, permit paperwork and, for an estate, whatever proves who is authorized to sign. Get payoff figures from the tax office and the county, and your closing attorney can settle any unpaid tax from the proceeds. That payoff step is easy to forget and can hold up the closing if the figure arrives late.

Frequently asked questions

Which office collects tax on a Lancaster property?

Pay at the tax office in the Town Clerk's office for Town, County and school bills. After June 30 (Town and County) or November 30 (school), the payment goes to Erie County Real Property Tax Services in Buffalo.

Does Lancaster belong to one school district?

No. Lancaster Central covers most of it, yet Depew Union Free, Alden Central, Clarence Central and Iroquois Central also bill Lancaster addresses. Read your own tax bill to see which one applies.

Who covers transfer tax on a Lancaster sale?

The seller pays both the state and Erie County portions when the deed goes to the County Clerk, $4.50 per $500 in all. Owners 62 and older who qualify may pay a reduced $2.00 rate.

Must I get a permit before listing my Lancaster house?

A plain sale is not among the permit triggers. The rule covers building, altering, moving and demolishing, so call the Building Department to confirm that earlier decks, pools or additions were permitted and closed out.

Is a damaged Lancaster house still sellable?

Yes. Sell it as-is, list it with the repairs priced in, or take cash from a buyer who wants no repair list. Check open permits with the Building Department before saying yes to any offer.

Selling quickly in Freeport

A Freeport seller can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept cash from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. Each route runs through the same village offices, Nassau County recording and New York State transfer tax rules.

With a median owner-occupied home value of $505,900, closing costs, flood questions and unpermitted work can each move the final number. Settling those items before a buyer's attorney finds them is usually the fastest way to a closing date.

Freeport housing figures

Freeport is a village inside the Town of Hempstead on Long Island's South Shore, with larger households than most of New York. Home values run well above upstate cities, and rents are high too. Sunrise Highway (Route 27) crosses the village west to east, and the Meadowbrook State Parkway marks its eastern edge. The Long Island Rail Road reaches Manhattan in roughly 45 minutes, and Freeport Public Schools runs eight schools with one high school.

Many sellers and buyers here work in Spanish as well as English, so make sure disclosures and contracts are explained in a language you read comfortably. Canals such as the Woodcleft Canal, home of the Nautical Mile restaurant strip, reach the Great South Bay and give many homes a marine setting, along with a flood obligation.

Flood zone status

For a large share of homes in the southern part of the village, flood zone status is part of the sale. A premises may lie in or beside a FEMA special flood hazard area, and a regular homeowners policy does not cover flood damage. A mortgage holder in a flood zone must carry a separate flood policy.

Freeport takes part in the National Flood Insurance Program and reports a 10% discount on flood premiums. Its Building Department keeps elevation certificates on file and has a certified floodplain manager on staff.

  • Ask the Building Department whether an elevation certificate exists for your address.
  • Look up the flood zone and base flood elevation on FEMA's site or through the village.
  • Remember the substantial improvement rule: if repairs or additions cost 50% or more of a building's market value, the building has to meet new construction standards.

Permits and code checks before listing

The village Building Department administers building, plumbing, electrical and housing codes, and it also regulates multiple residences and unsafe buildings. Permit filings go through the village's OpenGov portal, and structural applications need signed and sealed plans.

A buyer's attorney can ask for proof that finished basements, extensions or extra kitchens were permitted. If something was built without a permit, resolve it before listing so the question does not surface mid-contract.

  • Pull your permit history from the Building Department at 46 N Ocean Avenue.
  • Confirm that any converted space has the proper approvals.
  • Check the village zoning map if the house holds more than one unit.

Village services and exemptions

The village runs more of its own services than most Long Island communities. Its departments include the Assessor, Building, Electric, Water, Public Works, Fire, Police and Recreation, and the Treasurer oversees both the Treasurer's Office and the Tax Office. The Village Clerk handles licenses, permits and village records and works with the Planning Board and Zoning Board.

  • Electric: Freeport operates its own electric department, which has supplied power since 1898, and rates are posted on the village electric site.
  • Water and sewer: the Water Department publishes rates and fees, a conservation and regulations page and an annual water quality report.
  • Sanitation: Public Works posts a pickup schedule by area, so the collection day depends on the street.
  • Emergency alerts: Emergency Management lists hurricane evacuation routes and a CivicReady alert sign-up.

Exemptions handled by the Assessor include senior citizens, limited income disability, clergy, home improvement, non-profit, business development and volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers, plus the STAR program. Ask the Assessor how a change of ownership affects any exemption you hold, and tell the buyer which services are billed separately.

Village tax dates and deed recording

Freeport residents pay a village tax separate from Town of Hempstead, county and school levies. Nassau County runs a different assessment calendar, so call the county for its dates.

  • January 1: village final assessment roll published; the first village bill is due between March 1 and March 31.
  • September 1 to 30: second-half village bills are payable without penalty.
  • October 1: deadline for exemption applications and the taxable status date, by 4:30 p.m. in person.
  • November 1 to the third Tuesday in November: grievance window, closing at 8 p.m.

The Nassau County Clerk records the deed, keeps the official index of real property ownership and offers online land record search. New York's transfer tax is $2 per $500 of price, paid by the seller on a standard sale and reported on Form TP-584 filed with the recording office.

Houses with more than one unit

The Building Department regulates multiple residences, so a house with an extra kitchen or a second unit gets closer attention. Before listing, confirm the zoning map allows the unit count you advertise, and gather the approvals for any conversion. A buyer's attorney will ask, and a gap found late can push back a closing date.

Tell the buyer plainly how the house is used today. A cash buyer may still purchase a property with open questions, but the offer will reflect them, and a clean permit file protects your price. If a flood policy is required, share the zone letter early so the buyer can request quotes.

What to have ready for a cash buyer

Bring your permit history, any elevation certificate, your latest village, county and school tax bills, and a list of exemptions you hold. A buyer who sees those papers up front can quote a price without a long inspection period, and your attorney can answer lender questions faster when the file is already organized.

Then ask the village Treasurer and the county for payoff figures. At closing the payoffs come out of your proceeds, the deed is delivered, and the seller or the attorney files the TP-584 return with the recording office.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Freeport seller pay the New York transfer tax?

Yes, on an ordinary sale the seller pays $2 for each $500 of the price, and the TP-584 form goes to the county clerk with the deed. The separate 1% tax on residences of $1 million or more lands on the buyer.

Will flood zone status delay my Freeport closing?

It can if the buyer's lender wants flood insurance quotes first. Collect your flood zone, elevation certificate and any claim history early so the buyer can price a policy without waiting.

Where do I get a permit record for my Freeport house?

Ask the village Building Department, which handles permits and keeps elevation certificates. Its office is at 46 N Ocean Avenue, and permit filings run through the village OpenGov system.

When must I file a grievance on a Freeport assessment?

The village window runs from November 1 until 8 p.m. on the third Tuesday in November, and the application has to be physically in the Assessor's Office by then. A postmark does not count.

Is Freeport its own tax collector?

Partly. The village bills its own tax, and Town of Hempstead, Nassau County and school district taxes arrive separately. Ask the village Treasurer and the county for payoff figures before you close.

Your options for selling in Cortlandt

Cortlandt homeowners generally choose among a broker listing, a handshake sale with a known buyer, and a straight cash purchase. Cash earns its place when repairs are piling up, mortgage or tax payments have slipped, an estate needs closing out, or the calendar leaves no room for delay.

Fixing a house up for market costs money and time before anyone walks through. A cash buyer skips that step, buys the place flaws and all, and lowers the number to match. Compare every offer with what you still owe the lender, any tax balance and your closing costs.

  • Broker listing: best for a house in good shape when you can wait for the right buyer.
  • Private sale: works if you trust the buyer and can handle a contract.
  • Cash sale: built for deferred maintenance, inherited homes, tenant trouble or a tax penalty about to grow.

Cortlandt housing at a glance

Cortlandt is a Westchester County town of about 42,413 people, up the Hudson from the city. It includes the villages of Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson and hamlets such as Cortlandt Manor, Montrose, Crugers and Verplanck. Metro-North stops at the Cortlandt and Croton-Harmon stations, and the mean commute is 37.8 minutes, which buyers weigh when they price a house here. Commuters often ask about train access first, so mention the nearest station in your sale description. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $579,500, a useful yardstick when you weigh offers.

School districts and village taxes

The Tax Receiver collects for five school districts: Croton-Harmon, Hendrick Hudson, Lakeland, Putnam Valley and Yorktown. School taxes can differ sharply between houses only a few miles apart, so say which district the property is in whenever you share details with a buyer.

Village lines add another bill. Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson levy their own village taxes, billed separately from the Town and County bill. For a house within village limits, call the village office for that bill and its schedule. The Tax Receiver's office page links to both villages.

Due dates and penalties

Westchester towns act as collection agents, so the Cortlandt Tax Receiver bills Town, County and school taxes. The Town and County bill goes out by April 1 and is due April 30. The school bill goes out by September 1 and can be paid in full by September 30 or in two halves, the first by September 30 and the second by January 31.

  • Town and County penalty: 2% in May, 5% in June and July, 7% in August and September, 10% from October to December and 12% from January to April.
  • School first half: 2% in October, 5% in November, 7% in December and January, 10% in February and March, 12% in April.
  • No Town employee can waive a penalty.
  • Prior-year taxes unpaid by June 30 become a lien on July 1, and a property with taxes unpaid after 21 months can be foreclosed.

The Receiver's office is at 1 Heady Street in Cortlandt Manor, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. and on the last Saturday of April and September from 9 a.m. to noon. More than 15,000 parcels are billed from there. After hours, a courtyard drop box accepts payments, but not cash. Online payment adds a $1.00 fee for e-check or a 1.81% third-party fee for cards. Mailed payments need a United States postmark on or before the due date, since postage meter marks do not count.

Assessments, exemptions and grievances

Cortlandt runs on its own calendar. May 1 is tax status day, which is also the deadline for exemptions and tax map changes. The tentative roll is published June 1, Grievance Day is the third Tuesday in June, and the final roll appears September 15. The 2027 Grievance Day falls on Tuesday, June 15.

The prior year's final roll sets the current year's taxes. A grievance disputes the assessed value, not the bill itself. Before filing, ask yourself honestly whether the house would really sell for the full market value on the roll. Form RP-524 must be filed with the Assessment Office even if you plan to appear before the Board, and a mailed copy must arrive by 8 p.m. on Grievance Day.

Senior citizen and disability exemptions with limited income renew every year. The Assessor mails renewal forms in February and wants them back with supporting papers by May 1. Selling a house that has one? Let the buyer know the break stays with you as the owner, and a new owner must apply on their own. Enhanced STAR has no application, because the state verifies income yearly.

Deeds and transfer taxes

The Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk files deeds, mortgages and satisfactions and accepts them electronically. Cover pages, Form TP-584 transfer tax returns and RP-5217 reports are created through the clerk's PREP portal. Deeds go back to 1680 in its online search.

The state transfer tax runs $2 per $500 of consideration. Sellers usually cover it, and the return plus payment must reach the state within 15 days of delivering the deed. A sale at $1 million or above adds a 1% tax charged to the buyer. For permits and open violations, start with the Town and, for village addresses, the village hall.

Selling with taxes owed or work undone

Owe something on the house? Phone the Tax Receiver before agreeing to a price and request the exact amount owed with penalties added. Whatever it is gets taken from the sale proceeds, so get the number in writing early. Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson owners should ask their village for the same.

Going cash removes repair lists, open houses and a lender's appraisal. It leaves in place the title work, the deed, the transfer return and any lien payoffs. Pull together your loan statement, newest tax bill, exemption letters and permit notes, and offers can be weighed quickly.

Closing timeline for a cash sale

Step one is the paper trail. Step two is a walk-through followed by an offer. After a contract is signed, the title company searches records and surfaces any lien or tax balance. Those payoffs are subtracted from what you receive when the sale closes.

Once the deed is signed, Form TP-584 carries the transfer tax return, and the cover page and RP-5217 come out of the PREP portal before the County Clerk records the deed. Have your attorney or title company say who files what, so no piece lingers beyond 15 days.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Cortlandt house need repairs before it can be sold for cash?

Not usually. Cash purchasers buy as-is and subtract the repair cost from their price, so your number will sit under a fixed-up listing. Check for open permits or violations beforehand.

When is the next Grievance Day in Cortlandt?

It lands on Tuesday, June 15, 2027, the third Tuesday of June. Exemption applications are separate and due May 1.

Who collects property taxes in Cortlandt?

The Tax Receiver at 1 Heady Street handles Town, County and school bills. Village taxes in Buchanan and Croton-on-Hudson come from the villages.

What happens if I miss the April 30 Town and County tax date?

The bill picks up 2% in May and 5% in June and July. Nobody at the Town can waive it, so pay quickly.

Where is a Cortlandt deed recorded?

With the Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk, in White Plains. Attach Form TP-584 and create the cover page in the PREP portal.

The fastest ways to sell in Haverstraw

Selling fastest in the Town of Haverstraw usually means a cash purchaser who takes the property as it stands. Listing with an agent or selling privately both depend on showings, financing and appraisals. If your house is in good order and nothing is pressing, a listing may still get you a better price.

The town sits in Rockland County along the Hudson River. It includes the Village of Haverstraw and hamlets such as Garnerville, Johnsontown, Ladentown, Mount Ivy and Samsondale. A seller deals with the town assessor, the town Receiver of Taxes, the town Building Department, and the Rockland County Clerk for the deed.

  • Agent listing: the usual path when the property is in good order.
  • Owner sale: keeps the fee, but you handle disclosure and contract work.
  • Cash sale: built for probate homes, houses needing work, or owners facing tax penalties.

Haverstraw housing and layout

Haverstraw had 40,462 residents in 2025, up from 39,087 in 2020, in 12,366 households averaging 3.11 people. Owners occupy 64.8% of homes, with a median value of $387,500. Median rent is $1,906, household income is $89,107 and the commute averages 30.1 minutes.

The town stretches from the Hudson River to the western county line across the northern part of Rockland County. The village of Haverstraw holds the historic downtown, and part of Harriman State Park, including Lake Sebago, Lake Welch and Lake Kanawauke, lies in the west. About a fifth of the town's area is water, so a lot beside the river or a lake should be checked for drainage and flood history before you set a price.

  • Roads: the Palisades Interstate Parkway, US 9W, US 202 and NY 45.
  • Ferry: the Haverstraw to Ossining crossing of the Hudson, tied to Metro-North.
  • Bus: Short Line buses run along US 9W into Manhattan.

School tax installments

Parcels in the Haverstraw-Stony Point Central School District, named on the town's tax collection notice, may pay school tax in installments. The first installment, at least half, is due by September 30. A second, at least half of what is left, follows in October, and the rest is due before early November. Your bill shows the district and the installment option, and buyers will want to see both.

Assessment dates

Every parcel, vacant or built on, residential or commercial, gets a dollar value from the Town Assessor, and town, county and school tax all start from it. Exemption applications and STAR are handled in the same office, which also supports grievances, small claims assessment review and certiorari cases.

Haverstraw assessment calendar
DateAssessment step
July 1, prior yearValuation day
March 1Taxable status day
May 1Tentative roll filed

July 1Final roll goes public

The filing window opens in May and shuts within a few weeks. Miss it and you wait for next year's tentative roll. The office provides a printable grievance application and a questionnaire for proposed assessments. Gather them before May.

Late payment penalties

January 1 through January 31 is the penalty-free period for town and county tax. Haverstraw, a town of the first class, adds 1% in February and 2% in March. On April 1, unpaid tax goes to Rockland County Finance.

  • Installments: bills above $50 may be paid in four parts, with a 5% service charge and the first part due by January 31.
  • Later parts: due April 15, July 15 and October 15, and paid in Pomona to the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance.
  • March payments: once March 15 passes, only bank or certified checks work, and they must be in the office when it closes on March 31. A postmark won't count.
  • Cards: taken, with a 2.45% convenience fee added by the card provider.

Owner-occupants who are elderly or disabled, in homes of up to three families, can ask the Receiver of Taxes to notify a third party using form RP-923. If you close partway through the year, have the closing attorney find out which installments are paid so the proration is right.

Permits and Certificates of Occupancy

Building permits and Certificates of Occupancy come from the town Building Department, and section 84-4 of the Town Code spells out which repairs and construction require them. Those documents show that a house meets the codes for structural soundness and fire safety.

Look at every addition, finished basement and converted space before you list, and make sure a permit and a Certificate of Occupancy are on file for each. The department also takes questions about fire permits, burning permits, fire inspections and sprinkler systems. Expect a buyer's attorney to ask for a certificate on any addition or conversion. If a record is missing, raise it with the department early.

Deed recording and transfer tax

The Rockland County Clerk records Haverstraw deeds and wants originals that are recordable, legible, signed and notarized. New York charges $2 on each $500 of price, rounded up, which the seller normally pays.

The return and payment are due within 15 days of delivering the deed, and the clerk collects them when it records. On a residence of $1 million or more, the buyer owes an additional 1%. Downloadable forms for the common filings are posted on the clerk's land records page.

Selling a probate or inherited house

With an inherited house, every step raises the same question: who can sign. Before accepting an offer, collect the papers showing who may convey the property, because the deed must be signed and notarized in recordable form before it is filed. Also pull the latest town and county bill, the school installment record and any penalty notices, because unpaid tax keeps growing while an estate is settled. The Receiver of Taxes adds 1% in February and 2% in March, and on April 1 the balance moves to Rockland County Finance, so timing the sale around those dates can save money.

Estates often suit cash buyers, who accept the condition and work to the schedule probate allows. Still, have the buyer write down the closing date and who pays each cost.

Closing a cash sale in Haverstraw

Cash deals take only a few steps. You accept an offer, attorneys exchange the contract, title is searched, and the deed is filed. A mortgage buyer would add an appraisal and a lender's calendar. Because the cash buyer takes the house as is, the open items are permits, tax installments and any lien, which must all be settled before title passes. Ask for proof of funds and a firm date on paper, and weigh the net against what listing would leave once commission and repairs are paid.

Frequently asked questions

What happens to unpaid Haverstraw taxes after March?

Rockland County Finance takes over collection of unpaid bills on April 1. Until then the Receiver of Taxes adds 1% in February and 2% in March, and late-March checks must be certified or bank checks.

When can I grieve a Haverstraw assessment?

Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday in May every year, and filing starts May 1 and closes within weeks. In spring, call the Assessor's Office for the exact last day.

Can I pay Haverstraw taxes in installments if I am selling?

Yes, if the bill is over $50, with a 5% service charge and the first part due by January 31. Later parts fall on April 15, July 15 and October 15, so ask your attorney which have been paid before closing.

Which authority records a Haverstraw deed?

That is the Rockland County Clerk, which takes only original documents that are legible, signed and notarized. File the transfer tax return within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

Will a buyer ask for a Certificate of Occupancy in Haverstraw?

They come from the town Building Department as proof a building meets code, and an attorney for the buyer may request one for an addition or conversion. Section 84-4 of the Town Code lists the work that needs permits.

How fast can a Valley Stream house sell?

Anywhere from a few weeks to several months, and the route you choose decides which. Nassau County village owners generally compare three paths: hiring an agent, selling alone, or accepting a cash offer on the house in its current condition.

With homes averaging above $600,000, most buyers borrow, and the lender's appraisal and underwriting dictate when closing can happen. A cash buyer needs neither. Any path involves village, county and state paperwork, covered below.

Valley Stream housing at a glance

Valley Stream is a village of homeowners, with some of the higher housing costs on Long Island's western edge. Nearly four in five homes are owner-occupied.

Valley Stream housing and population
MeasureValley Stream
Residents, 2025 estimate40,379
Households12,340

A building boom that began in 1922 took the village from 11,790 residents in 1930 to more than 38,000 by 1960, so many houses are old and have been renovated more than once. That makes permit history matter later in a sale.

Which school district serves your address

The answer changes by street. Valley Stream elementary districts 13, 24 and 30 cover most of the village and feed the Valley Stream Central High School District. A few southern blocks go to the Hewlett-Woodmere Union Free School District instead.

Schools are usually a buyer's first question, so check your address and name the district in the ad. That choice also determines the school tax bill the buyer inherits, and school taxes go to the Town of Hempstead, not the village.

Building permits before a sale

The village Building Department reviews construction plans, issues permits, and applies the state building and fire codes alongside the village code. Permits are required for:

  • Finished basements and cellars, interior alterations, additions and dormers.
  • New or replacement windows, siding, exterior painting, driveways, steps and patios.
  • All plumbing and electrical work, including direct replacement of fixtures.
  • Pools, hot tubs, fences, solar panels and changes in use or occupancy.

A building permit expires 12 months after issue. An unpermitted basement left by a prior owner tends to surface in the buyer's attorney review, so call the department and learn what records exist for your parcel before listing. Buyers of older homes may also ask about the village Private Sewer Lateral Repair Program.

Parking and trash rules buyers ask about

Buyers new to the village tend to ask about parking and trash. The village answers both.

  • No parking on village streets overnight between 3:30 a.m. and 5:30 a.m.; the Clerk's Department issues temporary permits for overnight guests.
  • Garbage can be set out after 6 p.m. the evening before pickup; the weekly cap is 250 pounds and pails may not exceed 32 gallons.
  • Recycling takes #1 and #2 plastics and plain brown corrugated cardboard.
  • Construction debris can go to the village sanitation yard for $120 a ton, payable by check.

A full house cleanout will blow past 250 pounds quickly, so plan on the sanitation yard or a hauler.

Village tax due dates and penalties

The village taxes about 11,000 parcels and runs its own Tax Department. Village tax comes due June 1, with no penalty through July 1. Later payment brings 5 percent for the first month and another 1 percent each month after. Partial payments are refused, and balances still unpaid go to the annual lien sale on the first Tuesday in May.

On a sale, whatever village tax is still owed gets paid out of closing proceeds. Request a written payoff from the Tax Department so your attorney has an exact figure.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Valley Stream houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Assessment appeals and exemptions

The village reports an equalization rate of .87 and a residential assessment ratio of .90. Its assessment roll is final on April 1. The grievance period opens February 1 and closes the third Tuesday of February, which is Grievance Night, held 4 to 8 p.m. A denied complaint can go to a Small Claims petition, for which the Nassau County case number is obtained from April 1 through May 1.

  • Seniors 65 and over with household income under $28,900 can apply for a village exemption.
  • Military service earns 15 percent for wartime service plus 10 percent for combat-zone service, and Cold War service earns 10 percent.
  • Firefighters with more than five years of service receive 10 percent.

The senior, disability and firefighter filing window is September 1 through December 31 every year, so it is open now. STAR goes through the Nassau County Department of Assessment.

Recording the deed in Nassau County

The Nassau County Clerk in Mineola records every Valley Stream deed. Submit the TP-584 transfer tax form and the RP-5217 transfer report along with it, plus the IT-2663 estimated income tax form if the seller lives out of state. Transfer and mortgage tax must be paid by certified check.

Deeds get bounced here for small errors. Put the section, block and lot on page one, use a street address rather than a post office box, and sign everything in original ink. Delivery to the clerk should happen an hour or more ahead of closing, or use an approved e-recording company.

State transfer tax is $2 per $500 of price. The 1 percent buyer's tax applies to residences of $1 million or more, which is well above the village median. After closing, the new owner must send the village Tax Department a written request with the deed and the section, block and lot to change the owner and mailing address.

What a cash sale skips

With a cash purchase there is no appraisal, no underwriting and no mortgage contingency, so closing is not held up waiting on a bank. The house is bought in its current condition, which spares you permit chases, repairs and a cleanout.

Government paperwork does not go away. Tax payoffs, deed forms and county recording all still apply, so pull together your latest village tax bill, permit records and current deed early. Your attorney can then order the payoff and fill out the TP-584 and RP-5217 right away.

A simple order of work: confirm your school district, ask the Building Department about permits, request the tax payoff, then hand the deed details to your attorney. Doing the first two before you accept an offer keeps surprises out of the contract period. Keep copies of everything you send, since the village and the county each keep their own files.

Frequently asked questions

Do village taxes in Valley Stream have to be paid at closing?

Any unpaid village tax is normally settled at closing. Ask the village Tax Department for a payoff, since the village bills once a year on June 1 and accepts no partial payments.

How expensive are homes in Valley Stream?

The typical owner-occupied home is $616,100. About 78.7 percent of homes are owner-occupied and the median gross rent is $2,124.

When can I challenge my Valley Stream assessment?

File between February 1 and the third Tuesday of February, when Grievance Night runs from 4 to 8 p.m. The village roll is final on April 1, and denied complaints can move to a Small Claims petition.

Does Valley Stream require a permit for a finished basement?

Yes. The Building Department lists finished basements and cellars among the projects that need a permit. Ask what is on file for your address before you list, because missing permits surface during a buyer's inspection.

Where do I record the deed for a Valley Stream sale?

The Nassau County Clerk records it. The clerk requires the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms, certified checks for transfer tax, and the section, block and lot on the first page.

Which office covers your Ossining house?

Ossining is a Hudson River town containing two incorporated villages, the Village of Ossining and part of Briarcliff Manor, and an unincorporated area outside both. The town's Building Department answers only for that unincorporated area. If your lot sits within a village, permits and occupancy questions belong to the village, so confirm your location first.

The town covers 15.74 square miles, with the Hudson on its west edge and the Croton River on the north. Ossining Union Free School District serves the town. Put the district on every document, since the state seller form asks for it.

Housing and prices

Ossining town had 39,964 residents in 13,711 households as of July 2025. About 62.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied, with a typical value of $552,900, while the median rent is $2,203. Households with a mortgage carry a median monthly cost of $3,774, and the median household income is $125,539. Low turnover (89.5 percent stayed put over the past year) means a tidy house with complete records tends to draw notice.

The 2025 reappraisal and your assessment

The 2025 assessment roll followed a town reappraisal, so a buyer who compares your figure with a neighbor's is looking at fairly fresh numbers. Tyler Technologies helped with the project, and data collectors visited properties in yellow vests with ID badges. The town updates its assessment records every year.

Stop by the Assessor's Office at 16 Croton Avenue, 3rd Floor, or phone, before you list. Look over your property record for mistakes like a wrong bedroom count or an addition that was never recorded. Staff will talk through an assessment with you at any time. Weekday hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. From July 1 through September 1, expect every town office but the Town Clerk to close at 3:15 pm on Fridays.

Watch for scam callers posing as the Building Department and asking for more application money. Any message that pushes you to pay should be checked by calling the department at the number on the town website.

Contesting an assessment

The Board of Assessment Review hears complaints, and its meeting falls on the third Tuesday in June, the date the state gives for Westchester town boards. Sessions are held late afternoon into evening, so working owners can attend.

Ossining assessment calendar
Ossining calendar itemWhen
Valuation dateJuly 1 of the prior year
Taxable status day and exemption filing deadlineMay 1
Tentative assessment roll publishedJune 1
Grievance DayThird Tuesday in June
Final assessment roll publishedSeptember 15

Submit the state complaint form with a grievance questionnaire and evidence of market value: what you paid recently, comparable sales or an appraisal. Pleas based on what you can afford, or on how little you use public services, do not count. You will hear back by September 15. If the result disappoints you and you live in your one, two or three family home, a Small Claims Assessment Review is the next step, and you can handle it without a lawyer.

Deed fees and transfer tax

Filing a deed with the Westchester County Clerk starts at a $45 statutory fee. Add $5 for every written side of a page, $5 for the residential TP-584 and $125 for the RP-5217 transfer report. The clerk's own sample, a three-page residential deed in a single municipality, totals $190.

State transfer tax is two dollars on each $500 of the sale price, and a leftover partial $500 is rounded up. It falls on the seller by default. Buyers of a $1 million or higher residence pay an added 1 percent mansion tax.

  • The county's Property Records Electronic Portal calculates the fees for each submission.
  • Transfer tax can be paid by ACH, certified check, bank check, attorney escrow check or approved vendor check.
  • Credit cards cover ordinary fees up to $500 but never taxes.

Your title company or attorney will probably do the filing. Ask who is submitting the deed and on what day.

What must an Ossining seller reveal about flooding and condition?

Under Real Property Law 462, a seller of a house with up to four units must fill in the state's form and hand it over ahead of the buyer's signature on the contract. Two rivers bound this town, so read the flood questions closely.

The form asks about FEMA floodplain status, flood insurance, any flood claim you filed, and whether water ever entered the building through heavy rain, storm surge, tidal inundation or river overflow. It also covers shared or leased areas, septic or public sewer, a sump pump, the roof and any radon testing. An owner who later learns something that makes an earlier answer wrong owes the buyer a corrected form. An as-is sale is still legal, but the form must be delivered either way.

Do you have a deck, shed or finished basement built without a permit? Ask the Building Department, or your village, whether the permit can still be closed. Certificates of occupancy come up on the form too.

Steps from decision to closing

Most sales follow the same order. First, learn whether your lot is in the town or a village. Check your assessment record for errors. Answer the state seller form, closing out any open permit questions with the right office. Choose an attorney or title company, who will prepare the deed, Form TP-584 and the RP-5217 transfer report. At closing the transfer tax is paid, the deed is filed with the Westchester County Clerk, and any loan payoff comes out of your proceeds.

Skipping an early step usually costs time later, because the title company cannot record a deed with missing forms.

Selling for cash

Cash works best for a house with problems that a retail buyer's inspector would flag. With no lender underwriting, timing rests on title, payoff letters and the recording steps described above. After an owner's death, an attorney can say which estate papers the title company needs prior to signing a deed.

Get offers in writing, find out who covers transfer tax and recording, and confirm the buyer can truly close when promised. For questions about your own assessment or exemptions, the Assessor's Office is the right place, not a buyer.

Before talking price, line up your deed, current tax bill, permits for earlier projects, and payoff letters on any loan or lien. A buyer can then start title work immediately, which protects the closing date. Also decide ahead of time which rooms and systems you will disclose as needing repair, so the seller form and the contract say the same thing.

Frequently asked questions

Does the Town Building Department cover a house in the Village of Ossining?

No. The department has jurisdiction only in the unincorporated area outside the village limits. For a house in the Village of Ossining or the Briarcliff Manor part of the town, ask that village about permits and certificates.

What is the deadline for an Ossining assessment complaint?

Grievance Day, the third Tuesday in June. The tentative roll comes out June 1, and the Board of Assessment Review is the first stop before any other remedy.

Who pays transfer tax on an Ossining sale?

Usually the seller, at two dollars per $500 of price with partial amounts rounded up, unless the contract shifts it. The buyer owes the extra 1 percent mansion tax only on residences of $1 million or more.

Do I owe a buyer the state's seller disclosure form in Ossining?

Yes, for a house of up to four units. Get the signed form to the buyer or the buyer's agent before the contract is signed. Condo and co-op apartments are outside the rule.

Who records the deed for an Ossining house?

The Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division. A deed costs $45 plus $5 per page, and cover pages and transfer forms are prepared in the county's online portal. For fee questions call (914) 995-3094.
