Ways to sell a Penfield house

Penfield owners choose between a broker, a sale with no agent, and a cash buyer. Condition, timing and the people who must sign all affect that choice. The town is a suburb in eastern Monroe County, and sale paperwork passes through Town Hall offices and the Monroe County Clerk in Rochester.

A cash offer fits a house with put-off repairs, a project that never got its final inspection, or an estate being settled. Unfinished permit work can slow any sale, so open your permit file first.

Penfield at a glance

The town covers 37.88 square miles on the eastern side of Monroe County, with Webster to the north and Perinton and Pittsford to the south. Six hamlets carry names today: East Penfield, Lloyd's Corners, Panorama, Penfield, Penfield Center and Roseland. Most students attend Penfield or Webster central schools, though small parts of town fall in the East Rochester, Pittsford and Wayne districts. Check which one covers your address before you write the listing.

The population was 39,438 in 2020 and about 39,139 as of July 1, 2025. Owners occupy 80.8 percent of housing, with a median home value of $291,500. Rent has a median of $1,473, and median household income is $119,154 for 15,699 households.

Long-time owners are common here, so downsizing and inherited houses account for many sales. Such sellers tend to want a dependable closing date more than polished showings.

Assessment calendar

Assessments follow market value. From June through March 1 the Assessor's Office checks for new construction, additions and demolitions, and what exists on March 1 goes onto the next roll.

Penfield assessment dates
DateWhat happens
March 1Taxable status date. Exemption forms are due.
About May 1Assessment change notices are mailed and the tentative roll is filed.
Fourth Tuesday of MayGrievance Day at Town Hall. The next one is May 25, 2027.
Before July 1Owners learn the Board's decision.
July 1Final roll filed. A 30 day window for court review begins.

That final roll is what the September school bill and the next January's town and county bill are built on.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Penfield house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

Hand in form RP-524 to the Board of Assessment Review before it meets. The board holds its hearings in the Town Hall Auditorium at 3100 Atlantic Avenue and decides on the evidence you present, for example three or more recent sales of comparable houses. For a ten-minute appointment, bring the original form and exhibits plus five copies. Without an appointment, the original alone is enough. A form sent by email or fax does not count.

If the board says no, a resident of a one-, two- or three-family home can petition for Small Claims Assessment Review at the Monroe County Clerk, within 30 days of the final roll. Everyone else can file a tax certiorari case in State Supreme Court, on that same 30 day clock, ideally after speaking with a lawyer. Remember that the board takes assessment complaints only, not disputes over the bill.

Exemptions and a change of owner

Exemptions apply to a primary home only, and filing is due March 1. The Assessor's Office handles these:

  • STAR, Basic and Enhanced.
  • Limited Income Senior Citizen.
  • Persons with Disabilities and Limited Income.
  • Alternative Veteran and Cold War Veteran.
  • Agricultural Assessment.
  • Volunteer Firefighters and Ambulance Workers.

Take forms to Room 203 at 3100 Atlantic Avenue, where staff will copy your supporting papers on the spot. Renewal notices arrive each fall. If a buyer closes late in the year, the new owner should apply before the following March 1.

Permits and final sign-offs

Before you build, enlarge, alter, repair, move or tear down a structure, or work on electrical or plumbing systems, get a building permit. Sheds, barns and gazebos all require one, as do decks, hard-surface patios, finished basements and permanent standby generators. Residential fences skip the permit but face Town Code height limits: 6 feet, dropping to 3 feet within 20 feet of the front line.

Every project should close with a final inspection and a Certificate of Occupancy or Compliance. The Building Department, at (585) 340-8636, can tell you what is on record for your address. Landmarks and historic districts carry extra rules, and demolishing a landmark requires a certificate of appropriateness plus a 120 day wait.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Penfield houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How does a Penfield deed get recorded in Monroe County?

The Monroe County Clerk takes deeds at 39 West Main Street, Room 105, in Rochester. A one-page deed is $50, and each extra page adds $5. You also file the TP-584 ($5) and the RP-5217 ($125 for most residences, $250 for others), and residential deeds pay a further $10. The clerk quotes transfer tax at $4 per $1,000, the same as the state's $2 per $500. For same-day recording, be in line by 4:30 p.m.

Unpaid taxes can end in the county's in rem foreclosure and a public auction of the parcel. An owner behind on taxes can ask the County Treasury at 585-753-1200 what is owed, and should do so before listing.

From offer to closing

Once you accept an offer, the work shifts to the title company and attorney. They order a title search, prepare the deed, and fill out the TP-584 and RP-5217. Any balance on your tax bills and any mortgage payoff is taken from your proceeds at closing. If you have an exemption, tell the buyer what changes after transfer, since the new owner must apply on their own by the next March 1.

Keep the closing date realistic. A cash buyer can often close sooner than a financed one, but only if your permits, payoff figures and signatures are in order. Ask each buyer to put the timeline in writing. If the house has an open permit, ask the Building Department what inspection is still needed and book it early, because that single step is what most often pushes a closing back.

What a Penfield seller should gather first

A short folder saves days near closing:

  • Deed and any survey of the lot.
  • Permit records and the Certificate of Occupancy for decks, finished basements and additions.
  • Latest school and town and county tax bills, also viewable on the Monroe County Real Property Portal.
  • Proof of any exemption, so the buyer knows what changes after transfer.
  • Payoff figures for each mortgage or lien.

With the folder complete you can compare a broker sale, a private sale and a cash offer on equal terms. A cash buyer then has little left to check except title, so the closing date you agree on is more likely to hold.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Penfield house with permits still open?

Yes, though questions will follow. The Building Department wants permitted work finished with a final inspection and a certificate, and gaps can slow a sale. A cash buyer may accept the property in its current state, but the open permit remains attached to the address.

What date is Grievance Day in Penfield?

The fourth Tuesday of May, which is May 25 in 2027. The Assessor's Office accepts applications from May 1.

What does a typical Penfield home cost?

The median for owner-occupied homes is $291,500, and median household income is $119,154.

Does a Penfield fence need a building permit?

No, but Town Code caps fences at 6 feet, and at 3 feet within 20 feet of the front property line. If one side looks better, it should face the neighbors.

Who answers Penfield assessment questions?

The Town Assessor's Office at 3100 Atlantic Avenue, reachable at (585) 340-8610 on weekdays. It sets assessments, while school, town and county tax rates come from those taxing bodies.

Selling in Guilderland

Guilderland sits in Albany County just west of the city of Albany, so its houses compete with the capital's other suburbs. Inside the town are the Village of Altamont and hamlets including Guilderland, Guilderland Center, McKownville, Westmere, Meadowdale, Fort Hunter and Hartmans Corners. Buyers shop by hamlet, so name yours when you describe the house. Westmere is in the east on Route 20, McKownville is near the Albany line, and Meadowdale is by the southern town line. Mail can arrive under ZIP codes such as 12084, 12085, 12009 for Altamont, 12159 for Slingerlands or 12186 for Voorheesville.

The 2025 population was 38,216, up 3.5% from the 2020 base, across 14,697 households. Owners occupy 65.3% of homes, so about a third are rented, and that mix can bring in buyers who plan to rent the house out. The median home value is $357,400, median owner cost with a mortgage is $2,283 a month, rent is $1,564, and household income is $112,273.

Most of the town belongs to the Guilderland Central School District. A few parcels fall in Voorheesville Central, Schalmont Central or Mohonasen Central. Check the district on your tax bill, because the disclosure form has a line for it.

Building permits and how long they take

Most construction, renovation and structural work needs a permit. The Building / Zoning Department's FAQ covers the rules that matter to a seller fixing up a house.

  • A complete application can take four to six weeks to approve, and longer in summer.
  • Every fence needs a permit, with a fee that depends on length. A survey is recommended first, and no permit is issued over a utility easement without that agency's permission.
  • Every shed needs a permit whatever its size or foundation, and sheds go in rear yards only.
  • Permanent signs need a permit. For sale signs are on the list of temporary signs that don't.

Because the review is slow, start permit questions before you list. Ask the department what is on file for your lot, and get a survey if a fence or shed sits near a boundary or an easement. Plan around the four to six week window. If a buyer's inspection turns up unpermitted work and you start the paperwork late, the review may outlast the contract's closing date. Cash buyers who accept a house as is usually just take over the open items.

Property tax dates and penalties

Guilderland tax bills and where unpaid balances go
BillPenalty-free collectionIf left unpaid
Town and countyJanuaryHandled after the collection period ends, so call the Tax Office
SchoolSeptember 1 to September 302 percent penalty into early November, then payable only to the Albany County Division of Finance

The Tax Office is in Town Hall on Western Turnpike. It collects property and school taxes on about 12,500 parcels and takes water bill payments for the Guilderland Water District. If the house you are selling has an open school tax balance in November or later, call the county before closing.

  • You can pay in person, by mail, in the 24 hour drop box beside the Town Hall front doors, or online. Online fees are $2.00 for an e-check, $4.00 for a debit card and 2.5 percent for a credit card.
  • Only a U.S. Postal Service postmark proves timely mailing.
  • The Receiver can't waive penalties set by Real Property Tax Law section 924.
  • A returned check carries a $20 fee.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Guilderland house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Assessments and exemptions

The Assessor's office maintains assessments on more than 13,000 parcels and processes more than 1,000 deeds a year. It receives copies of building permits from the Town and from the Village of Altamont and inspects the work to decide whether the assessment or property inventory should change. A permitted finished basement or addition will therefore be reviewed.

  • Informal review: submit the form and proof of value by April 1 each year.
  • Formal grievance: the town's assessment contest page lists May 25, 2027 as the last filing date for the next cycle, before 8 p.m., with an original signed RP-524 and two copies of supporting documents.
  • Exemptions: new and renewal applications are due March 1, except senior partial exemption renewals, which are due by grievance day.

Seniors and people with a physical disability may qualify for partial exemptions. If you hold one, tell your closing attorney.

How a deed reaches the town records

Your attorney files the deed with the Albany County Clerk, the office that receives, indexes, stores and retrieves documents on real property ownership. The county then uploads each deed and sends it to the town, and the assessor's office receives these uploads two to four times a month. A new owner's name can therefore take a few weeks to show up in town records.

Recording charges change, so ask the Albany County Clerk for the current fee schedule. State transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of price, and your attorney can total the amount.

Selling when taxes are owed

An open balance won't stop a sale, but it has to be handled before the deed changes hands. Begin with the Tax Office at Town Hall and ask what is owed on the January town and county bill, the September school bill and the water bill. If the school balance has already moved to the county, call the Albany County Division of Finance instead, since the Tax Office can't take it.

Penalties are set by state law and the Receiver has no power to waive them, so there is nothing to negotiate on that side. Your closing attorney adds the payoff to the closing statement and pays it from your proceeds. For a seller who is behind on several bills and can't afford repairs, a direct purchase by a cash buyer can clear the balance at the table. Compare that net figure against a listing after commission, permit costs and the weeks of waiting.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Guilderland houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to gather before listing or accepting a cash offer

  • Your signed property condition disclosure statement under Real Property Law section 462, given to the buyer before any binding contract is signed.
  • Permit and certificate paperwork for any addition, deck, fence or shed.
  • The January town and county bill and the September school bill, plus the water bill from the Guilderland Water District.
  • Payoff statements, and any county tax balance.
  • A realistic closing date, since inspections and permit reviews can each take weeks.

A cash sale lets you skip showings and most repair requests, but the title search, payoff and recording still follow the same order. Ask each buyer for the offer in writing with a closing date and proof of funds, and have your attorney read the contract before you sign.

Frequently asked questions

Is Guilderland the same as the city of Albany?

No. Guilderland is a separate town in Albany County, west of the city. It has its own assessor, building department and tax office, and its own school district.

How long does a Guilderland building permit take?

A complete application can take four to six weeks, and review can run longer in summer. Emergency repairs and demolitions may be handled sooner.

What happens to unpaid Guilderland school taxes in November?

After the early November cutoff, unpaid school taxes are payable only to the Albany County Division of Finance. Call the county for the amount due, including penalties, before the closing.

Do I need a permit for a for sale sign in Guilderland?

No. For sale signs are listed among the temporary signs that need no sign permit. Permanent signs and temporary banners do.

When are Guilderland assessment grievances due?

The town lists May 25, 2027 as the last date to file, before 8 p.m., using an original RP-524 form. Informal reviews with the Assessor are due by April 1.

Listing or cash sale in Clifton Park

A Clifton Park seller can hire an agent, handle the sale personally, or sign with a buyer who pays cash and accepts the property in its current state. Condition, timing and your tolerance for hassle decide it.

A listing puts your house beside every updated kitchen and fresh roof on the market, so a tired interior or an aging roof can leave a listing sitting. A cash buyer prices those flaws in and skips the open houses. You give up some of the top-end price in exchange for speed and certainty, so compare what each path leaves in your pocket after the mortgage payoff and the closing costs.

  • List when the house shows well and your dates can move.
  • A private sale fits an owner who has a buyer lined up and is comfortable with the contract and deed work.
  • A cash sale fits an estate house, a tired rental, a property with code issues or a job transfer that will not wait.

Clifton Park housing

Clifton Park is a suburban town in the southern part of Saratoga County, about 12 miles north of Albany, 7 miles northeast of Schenectady and 10 miles south of Saratoga Springs. The Mohawk River forms its southern boundary. The Adirondack Northway (I-87) and US Route 9 run through the eastern part, and NY Route 146 crosses the middle of town. Growth came fast once the Northway opened in the early 1960s. The 2020 count was 38,029 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 37,775.

Clifton Park housing and income, 2020 to 2024

With a median home value of $395,400, a delayed sale has a real carrying cost: another round of mortgage, Town and County tax and school tax. For an estate, those months of holding costs can eat into what the heirs receive. Setting a closing date early avoids that.

With more than four in five homes owner-occupied, a rental or a vacant inherited house stands out on its street.

School districts and neighborhoods

Most of the town, roughly its eastern two-thirds, belongs to the Shenendehowa Central School District, while corners of the northwest and southwest fall under Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake and Niskayuna. Buyers tend to ask for the district before they ask for the square footage.

Named places inside the town include the hamlets of Rexford, Vischer Ferry, Jonesville, Elnora, Grooms Corners and Clifton Park Center, plus the neighborhoods of Clifton Knolls-Mill Creek, Clifton Gardens and Country Knolls. The town has a 15-mile trail network, the Clifton Common sports complex and, on the river, the Vischer Ferry Nature and Historic Preserve with a stretch of the original Erie Canal towpath. Mention those amenities to any buyer.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Clifton Park house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

No general town tax

The Town of Clifton Park has no general town tax. The January bill therefore carries County and special district charges, and school tax comes separately from whichever district serves the parcel.

A buyer comparing Saratoga County towns may care about that. Still, the total bill depends on the school district and the assessment, so hand a buyer a real bill rather than a talking point. Special districts also appear: the Receiver's office collects for the Old Nott Farm and Rivercrest Sewer Districts. School taxes are never paid at Town Hall. Shenendehowa, Niskayuna and Burnt Hills-Ballston Lake each collect their own.

Tax bills and penalties

Town and County bills are mailed December 31 and are due in January. Anyone who has not received a bill by January 7 should call the Receiver.

  • January: pay the exact amount on the bill with no penalty.
  • February: 1% is added.
  • March: 2% is added, plus a $2 late fee.
  • After March 31: the Receiver stops taking payment, and the Saratoga County Treasurer collects instead.

The office takes payment in person at One Town Hall Plaza, by mail to a bank lockbox in Albany, or online by card or e-check, where fees apply. The bill prints from the Assessor's records, and all changes of owner or mailing address go through the Assessor. If you sell in the fall, send the buyer's attorney your latest paid receipt so the proration at closing is clean. Escrow lenders sometimes pay the bill directly, so confirm whether yours did.

Assessment dates and exemptions

The Assessor's year starts at the March 1 taxable status date, which is also the last day to file an exemption. The tentative roll follows on May 1 and the final roll on July 1. School bills are dated September 1 and Town and County bills January 1. Grievance Day lands on the fourth Tuesday of May, May 25 in 2027.

The Town works to reach residents who may qualify for the senior citizen, disability and limited income, or military service exemptions. The assessor's office, on the second floor at 1 Town Hall Plaza, also collects data on improvements in the field and photographs them, so recent improvements may already be on record. If you added a deck or finished a basement, expect it to be reflected in the assessment.

Local rules, deeds and recording

Local Law No. 14 of 2026 amends sections 73-33 and 208-7 of the Town Code to define and regulate short-term rentals. If a buyer plans to run a short-term rental, have them read the text at the Town Clerk's office first.

Deeds are filed with the Saratoga County Clerk at 40 McMaster Street in Ballston Spa, which accepts land recordings until 4:15 in the afternoon. The seller ordinarily pays the state transfer tax, $2 for each $500 of price, and files Form TP-584 with the clerk within 15 days after the deed changes hands. Recording fees are set by the clerk, so phone ahead.

What a cash sale skips is the lender's side: no appraisal, no underwriting queue and no loan commitment that can lapse. What it does not skip is the title search, so any old mortgage that was never discharged, an unpaid bill or a lien has to be cleared first. Ask your attorney to order the search at the start so surprises show up while there is still time.

In practice, the closing attorney or title company handles the filing. Before the closing date, collect the deed, your latest Town and County bill and school bill, and a mortgage payoff statement, and ask the Assessor about any exemption you hold so the buyer is not surprised by a change in the next bill.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Clifton Park house if it needs work?

Yes. A cash buyer takes houses that need updates or repairs, and the offer reflects the cost. Compare it with a listing price minus fixes, commission and carrying costs.

Who do I pay Clifton Park property taxes to?

Town and County taxes go to the Clifton Park Receiver of Taxes in January, with penalties of 1% in February and 2% plus a $2 fee in March. School taxes go to the school district, not Town Hall.

When is Grievance Day in Clifton Park?

Clifton Park holds it on the fourth Tuesday of May (May 25 in 2027). Exemption paperwork is due the March 1 before.

Does Clifton Park have its own Town tax?

No. The Town has no general town tax. County charges, special districts and school taxes still apply.

Which office files the deed after a Clifton Park closing?

The Saratoga County Clerk in Ballston Spa records it. Form TP-584 goes in with the deed. Ask the clerk what the current fees are.

Brighton housing at a glance

Brighton lies just southeast of Rochester in Monroe County. A sale involves two offices: Building and Planning for zoning paperwork, and the county clerk for recording the deed. The 2025 estimate is 36,695 residents, slightly below the 37,137 counted in 2020.

Among 15,988 households, 56.4% own their homes. Median value is $282,100 and median gross rent is $1,350, while owners spend a median of $2,055 monthly with a mortgage or $935 with none. An owner of many years may find that a buyer prices in updates, so check what neighbors' houses sold for, and in what shape, before you set a number.

Neighborhoods and nearby features

Brighton has no central village. Rochester annexed the old village of Brighton, around East Avenue and Winton Road, in 1905. The commercial hub is Twelve Corners, where Winton Road, Monroe Avenue and Elmwood Avenue cross, and Brighton High School and Twelve Corners Middle School stand there.

  • The Erie Canal runs through town, along with the Erie Canal Heritage Trail.
  • Lynch Woods Nature Park gives access to the Lehigh Valley Trail.
  • The Brickyard Trail park, built on a former clay-mining site, opened in 2017.

Name the trails and parks in your listing. Buyers like to know what is within walking distance.

Do you need a certificate of occupancy to sell?

Not at a sale. Building and Planning issues no Certificate of Occupancy when ownership transfers. What it offers instead is a Zoning Verification Letter, which buyers and lenders ask for at a sale or refinance.

The letter names the property's legal use and its zoning district, and lists any violations the office knows of. Either you or the buyer's attorney can order it with the form on the town website.

Working with the Building and Planning office

  • The department is part of Public Works. It enforces the state's Uniform Fire Prevention and Building Code, and the town adds its own sprinkler rules.
  • Planning staff also support the Planning Board, Zoning Board of Appeals, Conservation Board, Architectural Review Board and Historic Preservation Commission.
  • Certificate of Compliance requests count as land use applications, and permits are filed online in the town's OpenGov portal.
  • Payments are taken in person, by phone or by mailed check. Online payment is not offered.

Town Hall at 2300 Elmwood Avenue closed for renovation in November 2024, and town offices have been working from 680 Westfall Road. Call the town to confirm the current office location before you drop anything off, and ask which window handles the request you are making.

Property tax bills and help for owners in trouble

One tax office in town handles both the town and county bill and the school tax bill. The town website has forms to request a bill, a past receipt, or a change to the mailing address and mortgage information. The first installment of town and county tax is due February 10, and the tax clerk suggests treating January 31 as the real date.

Seller and buyer divide the tax bill at closing. Before signing a contract, ask for the current bill and a receipt for payments made. Receipts for earlier years come through the same page.

Owners behind on a mortgage can call the HOPP hotline, 1-855-466-3456, listed on the town's tax page, or visit homeownerhelpny.com for a referral to a legal services or housing counseling organization. It exists so that no New York family loses a home for lack of a lawyer or counselor.

Monroe County deed recording costs

Brighton deeds are recorded by the Monroe County Clerk at 39 West Main Street in Rochester. To get same-day recording, be in line by 4:30 pm. Later drop-offs are handled the next day. A deed needs an original signature, a notary acknowledgment, a full legal description, and the new tax number.

Sellers normally cover the transfer tax, and buyers of residences at $1 million or more add a 1% extra tax. A free Restrictive Covenant Modification form has been available since June 3, 2026, for removing unlawful discriminatory covenants from recorded documents. Ask your title company whether anything of that kind sits on your deed.

Steps from decision to closing

  1. Request a Zoning Verification Letter through the town website so the legal use and zoning district are on paper.
  2. Request your current tax bill and proof of payment from the tax office, with earlier years' receipts if a buyer wants them.
  3. Get a payoff figure from your lender. Behind on payments? Phone the HOPP hotline before anything else.
  4. Sign a contract. The deed is drawn up with your original signature, a notary acknowledgment, the full legal description and the new tax number.
  5. Take the deed, the TP-584 and the RP-5217 downtown to the Monroe County Clerk with the fees listed above.

With a financed buyer, expect an appraisal and inspection requests before the contract is final. A cash buyer uses the same papers without waiting on a lender, so your own schedule can set the closing once title is clear.

What to tell a buyer about your house

Buyers and their attorneys ask the same questions in Brighton. What is the legal use, and is the zoning district right for the way the house is lived in? Are any violations on record? Were permits filed for work done on the house, and were they closed out? Is the tax bill current, and what was paid in prior years?

You can answer most of these with documents from town offices: the Zoning Verification Letter, a permit history from Building and Planning, and a tax receipt from the tax office. Collect them before you list or ask for a cash offer. A buyer who gets clear paper has less reason to discount the price, and your closing is less likely to stall over a question nobody can answer.

If the house has been in the family for years, add any survey or older deed copies you have. Title companies can often find them, but a seller who holds a copy saves a few days.

Ways to sell a Brighton house

You can list, sell privately or accept a cash purchase. Tidy houses are easy to market. Homes needing work, rentals with tenants and inherited properties often go faster to a cash buyer who accepts them as is.

Compare any cash offer with your likely net from listing, after repairs, agent fees and the taxes and utilities you would carry for months. Either way, keep the Zoning Verification Letter and a current tax bill in your paperwork, because every buyer asks about legal use and tax status.

Does Brighton issue a certificate of occupancy when a house sells?

Not at a sale. Building and Planning hands out Zoning Verification Letters instead, which give legal use, zoning district and known violations.

Which office files a Brighton deed?

The Monroe County Clerk in downtown Rochester. Recording costs $50 for a single page and $5 for each page added, and the TP-584 and RP-5217 go in with it. Get there by 4:30 pm to finish the same day.

When is the first installment of Brighton town and county tax due?

February 10, though the tax clerk advises paying by January 31. School tax comes on a separate bill, and the town website offers forms to request bills and past receipts.

How much transfer tax will I pay in Brighton?

Monroe County charges $4 for every $1,000 of price, usually paid by the seller. A further 1% applies to residences at $1 million or more, and the buyer pays that.

The hamlet your address falls in sets the school, library and fire districts that show up on the tax bill. Population was 35,902 in 2020 and is estimated at 36,394 for July 2025.

Who sells here, and what homes cost

A typical Riverhead house is valued at $486,600, and owners occupy 79.8 percent of homes. Tenants pay $1,974 a month, and the household in the middle of the income range takes in $94,249.

  • 14,202 households averaging 2.48 people.
  • Owner cost per month: $2,944 with a mortgage, $1,364 without one.

Many owners are past 65 and few move, so a lot of houses have been held for decades. The sellers who want a fast, simple close tend to be heirs and owners downsizing. Because the area is long settled, paperwork behind the house can decide a sale: certificates of occupancy, addition permits and septic records. Pull them together before you answer any offer.

Flood, water and the disclosure form

So much of the town is shoreline that water questions come up often. The town has Long Island Sound to the north, the Peconic River and bays, and four beaches that stay open all year. Basements, roofs and sump pumps all get tested by weather.

Real Property Law section 462 prints the disclosure form, and its questions to a seller cover floodplains, flood insurance, past flood claims, water in the basement, fuel tanks and septic age. Hand it over late, after the buyer has signed, and the buyer gets a $500 credit against the price. Answer only from what you know, and attach whatever radon, septic or mold reports you hold.

Rental permit rules for a house with tenants

Town Code Chapter 263 requires an owner to get a rental permit before renting out a dwelling, and the permit does not pass to a new owner. The Code Enforcement Division at 4 West Second Street handles applications, and the town now runs them through an online portal.

  • A permit applies to the whole premises, and a multi-family house needs one for each rented unit.
  • Stays of 29 days or fewer count as transient rentals, which the code bans.
  • Whoever buys must register the property inside 30 days after title closes.
  • First offenses carry fines of $250 to $1,000, and each additional week can count as a separate violation.

The town's summary of Chapter 263 shows a $300 fee for a two-year permit. Call Code Enforcement for the current fee. If your tenant moves out before closing, a lapsed permit is one more item a buyer's attorney may raise, so ask the office what it would take to put the file in order.

Property tax due dates and penalties

Riverhead's Receiver of Taxes mails one bill in mid-December and splits it into two halves, due about January 10 and May 31. A weekend due date slides to Monday, which is why recent halves landed on January 12 and June 1. The receiver collects town, county, school, fire and special district taxes together.

Riverhead late-payment penalties on the first half
Payment datePenalty
December 1 to January 12None
After January 121%
After February 102%
After March 103%
After April 104%
After May 115%

After June 1 the unpaid balance is owed to the Suffolk County Comptroller, and parcels still behind move to the county tax lien sale in November or December. The tax year runs December 1 to November 30. Report the sale to the receiver's office afterward, since a bill may carry the old owner's name for as long as six months. If the buyer cannot claim your exemptions, a pro-rata charge appears, and the closing attorney should prorate with that in mind.

Recording the deed with the Suffolk County Clerk

Deeds for Riverhead properties are recorded with the Suffolk County Clerk. The deed schedule lists a base cost of $245 plus $5 for each page, and the filing must include the state transfer tax form TP-584 and the real property transfer report.

State transfer tax is charged on any conveyance above $500, at two dollars for each $500 of the price, with part of a $500 block counted as a whole one. The mansion tax also applies to residential sales of $1,000,000 or more, paid by cash or certified check. For the tax map number, ask the Town Assessor. Most sellers leave this to the closing attorney, though recording happens separately from the signing.

Picking a sale route when time is short

You can list with an agent, run the sale yourself, or take an offer from a cash buyer. Let the repair list and your calendar decide.

  • A listing puts the house in front of the widest crowd, but showings, repair requests and a buyer's mortgage approval each add weeks.
  • Going it alone keeps the commission in your pocket, yet you price the house, fill in the disclosure form and handle the contract.
  • A cash offer fits a house with deferred repairs, rental permit trouble, an inherited title or a firm deadline. Get the number in writing and set it beside what a listing would leave you after fix-ups and closing charges.

Before any of the three, put the rental permit, current tax bill, disclosure statement and septic or oil tank records in one folder.

What happens between an accepted offer and closing

After the contract is signed, the buyer's attorney will usually ask for the latest tax bill, septic or oil tank records and, if the house was ever rented, the permit. Your attorney requests a payoff figure from the Receiver of Taxes, or from the county Comptroller once the bill has moved there.

You sign the deed and transfer forms at the table. Filing comes afterward as a separate step, when the county clerk takes the transfer tax and per-page charges. With cash there is no appraisal and no loan approval, so the schedule hangs on title, the permit file and how fast the receiver sends figures. Mention anything unusual, like an unpermitted unit or a flood claim, at the start.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Riverhead house if it was rented without a permit?

Yes, but expect questions. Chapter 263 makes renting without a permit a violation, and the permit is not transferable, so a buyer must register within 30 days of closing. Ask Code Enforcement what it would take to get the file in order before you list.

Who do I pay Riverhead property taxes to?

Until June 1, pay the Town of Riverhead Receiver of Taxes at 4 West Second Street. Later payments of an unpaid balance go to the county Comptroller, 330 Center Drive in Riverhead.

How do I find my Riverhead school district?

The hamlet decides. Four districts bill through the receiver here: Riverhead, Shoreham-Wading River, Mattituck-Cutchogue and Eastport South Manor, and the name is on your tax bill.

Does the seller or the buyer pay New York transfer tax?

The county clerk collects the tax with the deed, at two dollars per $500 on sales above $500. Your contract decides who pays, so have your attorney check that clause before you sign.

Where do I record the deed after closing in Riverhead?

The Suffolk County Clerk records it and takes the fees and taxes in the same visit. Call (631) 852-2000 with questions.

How quickly can a Yorktown house change hands?

Local sellers choose among a broker, a private sale and a cash buyer who accepts the house unchanged. Yorktown sits on the northern edge of Westchester County, about 38 miles from midtown Manhattan. It is a town, so you deal with the receiver of taxes, the assessor and the building inspector in place of a city hall.

The town is made up of five business hamlets, and no train runs inside its borders. Buyers weigh commute time, school district and the age of the mechanical systems, which makes the records you can hand over early the main factor in closing speed.

Yorktown housing and income

Most Yorktown households own, and incomes run high. The July 1, 2025 estimate of 35,944 people is 1.7 percent under the 2020 base of 36,562.

About 95 percent of residents did not move in the past year, which points to long ownership. Rail commuters drive to Katonah on the Harlem Line or Peekskill on the Hudson Line.

Hamlets and boundaries

Yorktown is bordered by Putnam Valley in Putnam County to the north, Somers to the east, New Castle to the south and Cortlandt to the west, and the Croton River crosses its south end.

  • Yorktown Heights, the mailing address of Town Hall.
  • Jefferson Valley, site of the Jefferson Valley Mall.
  • Shrub Oak, Mohegan Lake and Crompond, part of which lies in Cortlandt.

Franklin D. Roosevelt State Park and the North County Trailway, built on the old New York and Putnam rail bed, are the best known open spaces and worth naming in a listing.

School districts

School levy depends on which of four districts your parcel is in. Yorktown Central covers a large part of town, and the rest goes to Lakeland Central, Croton-Harmon Union Free or Ossining Union Free.

The town receiver collects school tax on behalf of all four but has no say over their budgets. Confirm the district before you list, and tell buyers which one applies.

Older houses and the systems buyers check

Winters here are hard on a house, so inspectors look first at the roof, the driveway and the heating plant. A recent furnace and roof, backed by receipts, make a better first impression than the same house without paperwork.

Tax bills and penalties

Fire, parks, sewer and water district charges are billed by the town's Receiver of Taxes, who also collects county and school tax. Tax is still owed when a bill goes missing.

  • School tax covers July 1 to June 30. A single bill goes out September 1 with two stubs, the first payable September 30 and the second January 31. When a due date lands on a weekend it moves to the next business day, so the 2027 second half is due February 1.
  • A late first school half starts at 2 percent in October and rises in steps to 12 percent, which then holds until the property is sold.
  • Town and county tax goes out April 1 and is due April 30. A late payment starts at 2 percent in May, reaches 5 percent for June and July, and tops out at 12 percent after December.

Nothing extra is charged on the second school half through January, but 10 percent applies in February and March. No reminder goes out in January, and the town has no power to waive penalties. A mailed check needs a genuine post office postmark on or before the due date. Because machine postmarks show the day mail is first processed at a regional facility, put the envelope in the mail days ahead. Pay in person at the Tax Office, 363 Underhill Avenue, any weekday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., or use the green drop box behind Town Hall.

Grieving a Yorktown assessment

The filing window opens June 1 and closes on Grievance Day, the third Tuesday of June. For the 2027 roll that is 8 p.m. on June 15, 2027, and the Board of Assessment Review meets at Town Hall from 4 to 8 p.m. that evening. There is no filing fee and no need for an attorney.

Back up the complaint with sales of comparable houses in your neighborhood and school district within a year of the July 1, 2026 valuation date, or with an appraisal. Emailed filings are refused. You can deliver by hand, mail, FedEx, UPS or the drop box at the rear entrance of Town Hall, and the board mails its determination on September 15, 2027.

Each property transfer is reviewed by the assessor, who records the buyer, seller and price. Senior citizens, STAR, military service and agricultural exemptions are the common ones. The assessor can be reached at 914-962-5722, extension 2.

Building Department and permits

The Building Inspector enforces the town's zoning ordinance and the State building codes, issues permits and certificates of occupancy, and may order unsafe buildings condemned. Applications filed on or after December 31, 2025 are measured against the 2025 editions of the State codes. Hours are weekdays 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. at Town Hall.

The town warns that it never tells anyone to wire a development fee. Fees are paid by check to the Town of Yorktown under the master fee schedule.

Records to hand over early

Buyers here worry about the age of the house, so show them proof. Get permits and certificates of occupancy from the Building Department, find the receipts for the roof and furnace, and print the newest school and town bills. The Tax Office will tell you what is paid, and the assessor will tell you which exemptions sit on the parcel.

With cash there is no lender appraisal, and the house is taken as is, so you skip repairs. Payoff, transfer forms and county recording are unchanged. Your attorney can prepare them in parallel with your gathering of documents.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Sorting out a sale with a closing attorney

Two clocks govern the closing. One is the tax calendar, which settles who owes which bill, and the other is the county clerk's document list, which sets how soon the deed can be filed. If the school tax second half falls due soon after your closing date, ask the attorney to work out the split and to show the payoff in writing.

If the title has more than one name on it, make sure every owner is available to sign. An estate or a divorce can add weeks, and a cash buyer cannot shorten that part. Put the question to your attorney on day one so there are no surprises later.

Recording a Yorktown deed

Every Yorktown deed is filed through the Land Records Division of the Westchester County Clerk. Bring four documents from the clerk's PREP portal: recording cover page, TP-584, RP-5217 and payment cover page.

New York's transfer tax is $2 for every $500 of the price, rounded up to the next $500, due when the deed is presented. The seller usually pays, though the contract can say otherwise. Once a home reaches $1 million, the buyer owes an extra 1 percent.

Frequently asked questions

When is the second half of Yorktown school tax due?

January 31. A weekend date moves to the next business day, so the 2027 second half is due Monday, February 1.

What penalty applies to Yorktown town and county tax paid in June?

The penalty is 5 percent. The bill is due April 30, adds 2 percent in May and 5 percent in June and July, and the town says it cannot waive any of it.

How do I contest my Yorktown assessment?

File with the Assessment Office between June 1 and Grievance Day, which is June 15, 2027, attaching comparable sales or an appraisal. The office takes no email filings.

Which Yorktown office issues certificates of occupancy?

The Building Department at Town Hall, 363 Underhill Avenue, headed by the Building Inspector, who also issues permits and enforces zoning and State codes.

Who pays state transfer tax on a Yorktown sale?

The seller pays unless the contract shifts it to the buyer. The tax is $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500.

Bethlehem housing at a glance

Town Hall in Delmar holds assessments and building records, and the Albany County Clerk takes the deed. The 2025 estimate is 35,684 residents in 14,722 households, and 73.0% of those households own.

The typical owned home is valued at $370,400. Monthly owner costs are about $2,300 with a mortgage and $959 without, against a median rent of $1,721. Longtime owners tend to hold a lot of equity in a house that still has its original systems. A house needing a roof, kitchen or heating system can still sell on the open market, though showings and repair talks come first. A cash buyer skips those steps and prices in the work.

Hamlets inside the town

Bethlehem covers 49.03 square miles on the Hudson River side of the county, and U.S. Route 9W passes through it. Its communities are organized as hamlets.

  • Delmar: the most populous hamlet. Delaware Avenue holds the town hall, police station, justice court and public library, and the Four Corners intersection of Delaware and Kenwood avenues is the traditional center.
  • Elsmere: home to Delaware Plaza, a shopping plaza built in the 1950s with a large supermarket.
  • Slingerlands, Glenmont, Selkirk, South Bethlehem and North Bethlehem: the other hamlets, with ZIP codes of their own for most of them.

The Albany County Helderberg-Hudson Rail Trail, a paved path toward Albany, follows the old rail line through Delmar. Elm Avenue Park, the town's largest park, has pools, courts and winter skating, with swimming limited to residents and their guests. Parks and trails belong in a listing, because buyers ask what is nearby.

How to check your assessment before selling

Start online. Use the Town of Bethlehem's Beacon portal. It shows property data kept by the Assessor's Office, including structure details, exemptions, sale history, tax bill and payment information, and it lets you run comparable assessment and sales searches. The portal carries the 2026 final assessments.

Spot an error in the inventory, say the bedroom count or square footage? Send the portal's feedback form so the Assessor can fix it. A tidy record helps the buyer's appraisal and heads off closing surprises.

To contest an assessment, get the grievance form from the New York State tax department site or the Assessor's Office. Homeowners may file directly with the Assessor at any time before or on Grievance Day. Call the Assessor's Office for the date, since it follows the assessment calendar. Write the date down and give it to the buyer, because a challenge filed in time can lower the bill they inherit.

Permits and certificates

The Building Division, part of the Department of Economic Development and Planning, handles permits and zoning information. It sits in Room 214 of Town Hall at 445 Delaware Avenue in Delmar. Before a sale, ask that office whether any permit on your house is still open.

  • A permit is required for additions, alterations and demolition, and also for decks, fences, hot tubs, pools, porches, ramps, roofing, sheds, generators and signs.
  • Residential permits typically take 7 to 10 business days, and work should not start until the permit is issued. Commercial permits average 14 to 21 business days.
  • Inspections must be requested at least 24 hours ahead.
  • Zoning rules sit in Chapter 128 of the Town Code, and specific zoning requests such as legal uses should be made in writing.

For a project you finished years ago, ask whether the final inspection was ever signed off. Fixing that now takes a phone call and an inspection request made at least 24 hours ahead, while fixing it after a buyer's attorney spots it can hold up a closing. The division's records are public. Open permits show up there, so close out old ones before listing.

Selling a house with an accessory apartment

An accessory apartment needs a Special Use Permit from the Planning Board under Section 128-73 of the Zoning Law, except in Rural Districts. If your house has a second unit, confirm it was approved before you list, because a buyer's attorney will ask. Ask the Planning Department for your permit record, and tell any buyer, including a cash buyer, what the approval covers.

Deeds and the transfer tax

Deeds for Bethlehem property are filed with the Albany County Clerk on Russell Road in Albany, indexed by liber and page number. Deeds and mortgages filed after 1980 can be searched through the clerk's website. Surveys are kept there too, filed by the map and drawer numbers printed on the deed.

The seller covers the state transfer tax of $2 per $500 of price. A buyer purchasing a residence at $1 million or more adds an extra 1%. Hand Form TP-584 to the county clerk along with the deed, and pay within 15 days of delivery. If one side skips its share, the other is exposed, so confirm both at closing.

Preparing your paperwork

Build a short folder before you talk to any buyer or sign a listing agreement. Print your Beacon record and mark errors. Ask the Building Division about open permits. Locate the deed, noting its liber and page, plus the survey's map and drawer numbers. Add your lender payoff letter and newest tax bill.

Your title company will ask for the same papers, so having them ready saves days. A second unit adds its Special Use Permit to the pile. Cash buyers appreciate the folder too, and a clean one speeds up the offer: it lets them price the house accurately instead of padding for unknowns.

Your options if you want out of a Bethlehem house

You can hire an agent, sell it yourself or take a cash purchase. A listing tends to show the biggest number on paper but brings showings, inspection requests and a closing that depends on the buyer's lender.

Cash fits an inherited Slingerlands house nobody wants to clear out, a Selkirk rental with tenants, or a Delmar home with more repairs than its owner wants to handle. The buyer takes it as is and the closing follows your calendar. Weigh each offer against your net after repairs, agent costs and carrying costs, and test it against Beacon sale history for nearby parcels.

Frequently asked questions

Is a certificate of occupancy required when my Bethlehem house sells?

Ask the Building Division before you list, since it keeps the permit records. It can say whether a project such as a deck or finished basement has an open permit or a missing sign-off.

Where is a Bethlehem deed recorded?

The county, not the town. Albany County Clerk files deeds by liber and page, and deeds and mortgages after 1980 can be viewed online. The TP-584 goes in with the deed.

How do I challenge my Bethlehem assessment?

Submit the state grievance form to the Town Assessor's Office by Grievance Day. Compare similar properties and sales on the Beacon portal first. Hiring someone is optional.

Which side owes the state transfer tax in a Bethlehem closing?

The base tax of $2 per $500 falls on the seller. The extra 1% on residences at $1 million or more falls on the buyer.

Can I sell a Bethlehem house that has an accessory apartment?

Yes, as long as the apartment was approved. Outside Rural Districts the Planning Board must have granted a Special Use Permit, and the Planning Department can show you the record.

Ways to sell on the barrier island

Owners in Long Beach can go to market with an agent, sell privately, or accept a cash purchase that comes with no repair requests. The barrier-island setting colors each choice, since Hurricane Sandy flooded the city in 2012, and condition and documentation carry real weight.

Neighborhoods and housing types

Long Beach is a dense oceanfront city on a barrier island, with the Atlantic to the south and Reynolds Channel to the north. It covers 2.22 square miles of land, less than a mile wide and about 3.5 miles long. Fewer than 40% of its homes are detached houses, so apartments, condos and attached homes make up much of the housing.

Neighborhoods vary a lot in feel and housing type:

  • West End: small bungalows and a few large houses on narrow streets that run from beach to bay.
  • East End: wider land between ocean and bay, with larger family houses.
  • The Canals and The Walks: canal-front streets and a network of narrow walkways between houses.
  • Central District and North Park: the area around City Hall and the Long Island Rail Road terminal.

Your neighborhood decides who is likely to buy. A West End bungalow, a canal-front house and an East End family home attract different buyers and different questions, so ask an agent for recent sales in your own neighborhood instead of a citywide number. The long commute fits the city's role as a commuter community. The Long Beach branch of the Long Island Rail Road ends at a terminal at Park Place and Park Avenue, and the city runs its own 24-hour bus service.

Monthly cost matters to buyers too. Mortgaged owners pay $3,519 a month at the midpoint, which limits what a buyer can spend on a house that needs a new roof or bulkhead.

Permits a buyer will ask about

Home work of many kinds needs a Building Department permit, and an unpermitted job in the house's past can slow a sale. The list covers roofs, siding, fences, driveways and curb cuts, central heating and air conditioning, sidewalks, bulkheads and docks, decks and porches, pools, hot tubs and saunas, fireplaces and chimneys, and all plumbing. Electrical work must be done by an electrician who holds a license, and a dumpster or roll-off container placed on the street needs a permit as well.

Additions, alterations and new structures also need approval, as does cutting a wall, removing a beam or changing a stairway or required exit. The department sits on the third floor of City Hall. Permit prices change, so ask the office for the current fee before you start work. If you did a bulkhead, deck or roof after Sandy, pull your permit and final inspection records now and keep them with your closing file.

Before you list, find out from the Building Department what it has on your address. A missing final inspection is cheaper to finish now than to explain once a buyer's attorney finds it.

How Long Beach taxes are billed and paid

One city office, the Tax Department, sends the bill for city real estate tax and residential sanitation and also collects the current-year Nassau County tax, so start there with most questions. You can pay on the third floor of City Hall with cash or a check, send payment to the City of Long Beach Treasurer at 1 West Chester Street, or pay online.

The City Charter lets properties with annual city taxes under $8,000 pay in two installments, while a bill of $8,000 or more is due in one payment in July. If your bill sits near that line, call the Tax Department to confirm whether you pay once or twice.

Escrow customers should watch for one trap: after a property moves into the single-payment group, a lender may keep collecting as though two installments still apply. Have your servicer review the escrow before closing, and request a written balance from the Tax Department for your attorney's closing adjustment.

Grieving a Long Beach assessment

If the City of Long Beach assesses your property, you appeal to the city's Board of Assessment Review. A filing with Nassau County's Assessment Review Commission does not preserve your rights there. The county's own filing window for its tentative roll runs from January 4 to March 1, 2027, with no fee and no extension, and it applies to county-assessed properties.

The commission can lower an assessment or leave it unchanged, nothing more. Ask the City of Long Beach assessor for the grievance dates and forms that apply to your parcel.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Long Beach houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Transfer costs

The state charges $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up, and sellers owe it unless the contract says otherwise. A residential price of $1 million or more brings a 1% mansion tax for the buyer. The TP-584 return and payment reach the county clerk within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

The Nassau County Clerk records deeds and lists recording fees on its real estate records pages. Ask your attorney or title company for the exact recording charge on your closing statement. After the sale, close your STAR registration.

With cash there is no buyer's lender or appraisal, the usual place a barrier-island deal stalls over flood insurance. A cash buyer still wants the survey, elevation certificate, claim history and permits. Weigh any offer against the net from a listing after commission, repairs and carrying costs, and let a New York attorney read the contract.

Frequently asked questions

Does Nassau County assess my Long Beach house?

Not always. If the City of Long Beach assesses your property, you appeal to the city's own review board, and a filing with Nassau County's Assessment Review Commission does not cover that city assessment.

Who bills property tax in Long Beach?

The city's Tax Department bills City of Long Beach real estate tax and residential sanitation and also bills the current-year Nassau County tax. You can pay at City Hall, by mail to the City Treasurer or online.

Is my Long Beach city tax paid in one payment or two?

Properties with annual city taxes under $8,000 may pay in two installments, and $8,000 or more is due in one payment in July. Call the Tax Department if your bill is close to the line.

Do I need a permit for work on my Long Beach house?

Yes for most structural, mechanical and exterior work. Roofs, siding, fences, driveways, decks, pools, heating and cooling, plumbing and electrical work, and street dumpsters all need one.

Who pays transfer tax on a Long Beach sale?

The seller owes New York State's $2 per $500 transfer tax unless the contract shifts it, and the buyer owes the 1% mansion tax when a residential price is $1 million or more.

Spring Valley layout and location

Spring Valley is a dense village in Rockland County, about 22 miles north of Manhattan and 5 miles north of the New Jersey line. Most of it lies in the Town of Ramapo, with a small western slice in the Town of Clarkstown. Neighbors include Chestnut Ridge to the south, Airmont and Monsey to the west, Hillcrest to the north and Nanuet to the east.

The village sits next to the New York State Thruway (Interstate 87), and the Spring Valley Transit Center is the terminus of New Jersey Transit's Pascack Valley Line. That access to rail and highway is a selling point for commuters. Downtown revitalization has meant demolishing abandoned buildings on Main Street and putting mixed-use buildings in their place.

Because the village straddles two towns, the town part of your tax bill depends on the side of the line your parcel is on. Your deed, tax bill and the county's property search will show it.

Housing in Spring Valley

Spring Valley is crowded and rent-heavy. The village has 2.01 square miles of land and 16,442.6 residents per square mile, with 34,482 people as of July 1, 2025, up 4.3% from 2020. Only 25.0% of homes are owner-occupied, and households average 3.63 people.

Spring Valley village housing figures, 2020-2024
Housing measureSpring Valley village
Households9,082
Owner-occupied rate25.0%
Typical owner-occupied value$381,800
Typical gross rent$1,695
Monthly cost, owners with a mortgage$2,947
Typical household income$57,196

The population is young and multilingual: 36.0% of residents are under 18 and 75.6% of those age five and up speak a language other than English at home. Marketing in more than one language may reach more of the buyers and tenants here.

With three-quarters of homes rented, a lot of sellers own two-family and multi-family buildings with tenants in place. If yours is one of them, gather leases, rent rolls and any inspection records before you talk to buyers.

Permits and certificates of occupancy

The Village of Spring Valley Building Department, at 200 North Main Street, administers the New York State Building Code, Fire Prevention Code, Housing Code and Energy Code along with the village's planning and zoning rules. It issues building permits, certificates of occupancy and water meters, schedules construction inspections and takes complaints. Its inspectors also carry out fire code and housing inspections.

That mix of housing inspections and certificate work makes the department the first call if your house has an unfinished project, an extra apartment or an open complaint. Village Hall answers at (845) 352-1100. The village website links to the Rockland County property search and an interactive county map, which help you confirm lot lines and the correct town.

  • Ask whether every unit in your building has a certificate of occupancy.
  • Ask whether any housing or fire inspection is open.
  • Ask whether the village requires any registration or certificate when a house with tenants changes owners.

How property taxes are billed

A Spring Valley owner usually receives three kinds of tax bill, and they come from different offices. Village taxes are billed and collected by the village itself, and the Town of Ramapo does not collect taxes for the villages. The Village Treasurer's Office at Village Hall takes payments and posts due dates on the bill and in the village's tax portal.

Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes collects the County and Town bill, with the first payment due on or before January 31 and penalties starting in February. School tax penalties start in October. If your bill is over $50 you may pay the County and Town tax in four installments, with a 5% service charge collected by the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance. School taxes arrive on a separate bill.

If you plan to sell, skip the installment plan. It can cause confusion at closing, and the service fee is 5% of the total. At closing you receive credit for the unused portion of the taxes. Under state law an owner stays responsible for taxes even if a bill never arrives, and the town cannot waive statutory penalties.

Recording a deed in Rockland County

Deeds are recorded by the Rockland County Clerk at 1 South Main Street in New City. The clerk does not supply deed forms and cannot help prepare one. The deed has to be signed and notarized, include the names and addresses of all sellers and buyers, and carry a Schedule A property description, which you can copy from the current deed of record.

  • Form TP-584 must be signed by all parties, and Form RP-5217 needs at least one grantor and one grantee, with a buyer contact name and a valid phone number.
  • The base recording fee is $45, plus $5 per page, a $6 TP-584 fee and a $10 notification fee.
  • The RP-5217 filing fee is $125 or $250, depending on the property class code and the sale type on the form.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope must come with a mailed submission, or the recorded original is not returned.

The state transfer tax is $2 per $500, or $4 per $1,000 of price. The 1% mansion tax applies only when the taxable consideration is $1 million or more.

What to line up before contract

Start with the parcel: confirm the town, the school district and the village tax account from your bills. Then collect permit records and certificates of occupancy from the Building Department, and ask for the tax status of the village, County and Town, and school bills. A closing attorney can then prepare the deed, Schedule A and transfer forms.

Ramapo's tax office handles school and property taxes for about 30,000 parcels, keeps the tax roll open for public inspection and helps residents, realtors, lenders and title companies who need tax information. A Third Party Request Form is available on its page.

If the building has tenants, add leases, rent ledgers and any inspection notices to the file. Buyers of multi-family buildings in a village where only a quarter of homes are owner-occupied will want to know exactly who lives in each unit and what each pays.

If you would rather not run that gauntlet, a cash buyer can take the building with tenants in place and close on your date, without a lender waiting on inspection notices.

Closing day in Spring Valley

By closing, your attorney should have the signed and notarized deed, the Schedule A description and both transfer forms ready for the Rockland County Clerk in New City. The tax credit for the unused part of the year is worked out at the table, so bring your latest bills from the village, the County and Town, and the school district.

Landlords should also hand over rent ledgers and keys for every unit, and tell tenants in writing who the new owner is. Skipping that step is a common source of confusion after a sale.

Frequently asked questions

Does the Town of Ramapo collect my village taxes?

No. Each village bills and collects its own taxes. In Spring Valley that means the Village Treasurer's Office at 200 North Main Street.

Should I choose installments if I plan to sell?

No. Ramapo's Receiver of Taxes advises against it because of closing confusion and the 5% service fee. At closing you are credited for the unused part of the taxes.

Which county office records a Spring Valley deed?

The Rockland County Clerk in New City records it. The deed must be signed and notarized, and Forms TP-584 and RP-5217 go with it.

What does recording a deed cost in Rockland County?

The base fee is $45, with $5 per page, a $6 TP-584 fee and a $10 notification fee, plus transfer tax and the RP-5217 fee of $125 or $250.

Who inspects houses and issues certificates of occupancy?

The village Building Department at 200 North Main Street. It enforces the state building, fire, housing and energy codes and handles permits and certificates.

Selling a house in Carmel, NY

Carmel is the Putnam County town that borders Westchester County on the south, and it is also the county seat. A Carmel owner has three paths: an agent listing, a private sale, or an offer from a direct buyer such as our company. Home values are high enough that waiting on a buyer's mortgage approval, and the chance of that approval falling through, is a real cost. A direct sale removes that wait.

Putnam County is a commuter area, and the 41.2 minute average drive to work shapes who buys here. Households tend to be long-term: 85.4% of homes are lived in by their owners, so many listings come from people who have been in the house a long time and have equity built up. Some of those sellers are handling an inherited house or a move out of state, and a quick closing helps them.

The rest of this page covers the local offices you will deal with, the paperwork a sale triggers and the steps to take if money is owed on the property.

Carmel housing costs

Carmel's population was estimated at 34,442 in mid-2025, up 2.5% from 33,592 in April 2020. Housing costs run well above national figures: the median owner's home is valued at $495,100, against $332,700 nationally. About 93.0% of residents stayed in the same house over the past year, and the average commute is 41.2 minutes, compared with 26.4 minutes nationally.

A typical mortgaged owner pays $3,335 a month, so a missed payment or two adds up fast. If you are behind, or you owe close to what the house is worth, ask your lender for a payoff letter before you compare offers.

Hamlets, Town Hall and ZIP codes

Carmel sits on the southern edge of Putnam County, about 50 miles north of New York City and 10 miles west of Danbury, Connecticut. The southern town line is the Westchester County border, next to Somers and Yorktown.

The town has no incorporated villages. It has hamlets instead, and the two largest, Carmel and Mahopac, are big enough to pass for villages. Baldwin Place and Carmel Hills are others. Town Hall is at 60 McAlpin Avenue in Mahopac, while the county seat sits in the Carmel hamlet in the northeastern corner of the town. ZIP codes 10512 and 10541 both apply. Copy the address from your deed and tax bill onto every form.

Wells, septic and school districts

If your house relies on a well or a septic system, the county's Public Access Portal already holds records for those systems. Check what is on file before an inspector visits.

Two school districts cover most of the town, and the parcel decides which one a buyer's children attend: Carmel Central and Mahopac Central. Smaller slices fall in the Lakeland, North Salem and Brewster districts. Families will ask early, so check your parcel's district first.

Before you list: Town of Carmel checks

Visit or call the Town of Carmel Building Department at Town Hall, 60 McAlpin Avenue. Find out if any permit on the house was never closed and whether additions, decks, finished basements and garages have certificates of occupancy. Open permits usually turn up once a buyer's attorney orders the municipal search. A cash buyer can take the house with those items still open, which a mortgage lender often will not allow.

The assessor can tell you the current assessed value and which exemptions sit on the parcel. Pull together your deed, the latest tax bills, any permits and a mortgage payoff letter if there is a loan, and the first attorney meeting will go faster.

Putnam County Clerk and deed recording

The Putnam County Clerk's Office is at 40 Gleneida Avenue in Carmel and sees customers by appointment only. The number is 845-808-1142. Hours are 9am to 5pm Monday through Friday, with summer hours of 8am to 4pm from mid-June through mid-September. Land recordings can go in the dropbox outside the County Office Building, or you can e-record through one of the clerk's partners. The office offers a Land Records Search and a fillable RP-5217 transfer report form.

The clerk's free Fraud Alert service sends an email each time a document is recorded in your name. Owners of a vacant house, such as an inherited one, can sign up through the clerk's page.

New York's state transfer tax is $2.00 per $500 of price, reported on the TP-584 filing. Ask the clerk's office for the exact amount before you sign, and expect your attorney to handle the filing.

Assessments and tax relief

The Carmel Assessor's Office is at 60 McAlpin Avenue in Mahopac, phone 845-628-1500. The county's Real Property Tax Service Agency at 40 Gleneida Avenue, phone 845-808-1030, runs the Beacon property search and publishes tax rolls and rates.

These exemptions exist under the Real Property Tax Law:

  • Senior citizens aged 65 and over (section 467)
  • Persons with disabilities (section 459-c)
  • Alternative and Cold War military service exemptions (sections 458-a and 458-b)
  • Volunteer firefighters and ambulance workers (section 466-a)
  • Forest land (section 480-a) and agricultural land (section 305)

If you think the assessment is too high, take it first to the local Board of Assessment Review. After a denial, a resident owner of residential property can file a Small Claims Assessment Review petition. File within 30 days after the final roll, and file it online, since paper SCAR petitions are not accepted. Remember that a successful challenge lowers future bills, so it matters most to a seller who plans to stay for a while longer.

What a direct sale skips

Timeline for a typical direct sale: you request an offer, the buyer looks at the house, you agree on a price and a closing date, an attorney or title company clears the title, and you sign. If a mortgage or a tax balance exists, it is paid from the proceeds and the remainder goes to you.

With a conventional listing you prepare the house, host showings, negotiate repairs after the inspection and wait for the buyer's bank. A direct sale replaces that with one offer on the house as it stands. You still sign a contract and a deed, the closing attorney still pays off any loan or tax balance from the proceeds, and the county still records the transfer. What drops out is the repair list and the financing contingency.

Frequently asked questions

Is Carmel a town or a village?

Carmel is a town, and it has no incorporated villages. Carmel and Mahopac are hamlets inside it, and Town Hall sits at 60 McAlpin Avenue in Mahopac.

Where is a Carmel deed recorded?

The Putnam County Clerk's Office, 40 Gleneida Avenue in Carmel, takes recordings. Visits are by appointment, and land documents can be left in the dropbox or e-recorded through a partner.

Which office handles my Carmel assessment?

The Carmel Assessor's Office, at 60 McAlpin Avenue in Mahopac, phone 845-628-1500. The county's Real Property Tax Service Agency, 845-808-1030, helps with tax rolls and exemption questions.

Can I contest my Carmel assessment before selling?

Only owners who live in the house. The first stop is the local Board of Assessment Review, and after a denial you may file a Small Claims Assessment Review petition, electronically, within 30 days after the final roll.

Which school district covers my Carmel house?

Most of the town falls in Carmel Central or Mahopac Central, and smaller areas in Lakeland, North Salem and Brewster. Because the line follows the parcel, verify it with the district before quoting it to a buyer.

Selling in Eastchester?

Ways to sell in Eastchester

A homeowner in Eastchester may go through a broker, sell without one, or take cash. Cash tends to be quickest for a house that needs repairs or a seller who must close on a fixed day, though you should expect a figure under full market value.

First, get your tax status from the Receiver of Taxes, look up permits at the Building Department, and pin down the school district and village for the address. Price and timing both depend on those answers.

Eastchester and its villages

Eastchester is a town in southern Westchester County, roughly 5 miles south of White Plains and 20 miles north of New York City. It has about 4.87 square miles of land and 34,015 residents. Scarsdale lies to the north, New Rochelle to the east, Yonkers to the west and Mount Vernon to the south.

Two incorporated villages, Bronxville and Tuckahoe, sit inside the town boundaries. The rest is the unincorporated area also called Eastchester, with neighborhoods such as Lake Isle, Twin Lakes, California Ridge, Hickory Hills, Huntley Estates, Chester Heights, Garth Road and Waverly Heights. Whether a house is in a village or in the unincorporated part decides which local offices serve it, so confirm that first. Most town offices share Town Hall at 40 Mill Road.

About 72.3 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, the typical home value is $806,300, typical household income is $155,726 and typical monthly rent is $2,302. The average trip to work is 35.9 minutes.

Trains, parkways and school districts

Metro-North's Harlem Line stops at Crestwood, Tuckahoe and Bronxville, and the town sits between the Hutchinson River and Bronx River Parkways, with Route 22 running through the middle. Rail and parkway access is easy to verify, so give a buyer the walking distance to a station instead of a general claim.

Three school systems cover the town: the Eastchester Union Free School District, the Tuckahoe School District and the Bronxville Schools. The town's Receiver of Taxes collects the Eastchester and Tuckahoe district taxes. For a Bronxville Schools address, ask that district how its taxes are billed. Name the district in any listing.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Eastchester house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Tax due dates and penalties

County and town taxes are paid once a year and are due without penalty by April 30. School taxes follow a July 1 to June 30 fiscal year and are paid in two halves. The Receiver of Taxes also handles notices of tax lien sales and gives callers information on apportioning taxes in a real estate sale.

Eastchester tax payment calendar
BillLast day without penaltyPenalty after that
County and townApril 302 percent in May, rising to 14 percent by the following June
School, first halfSeptember 302 percent in October, rising to 14 percent by June
School, second halfJanuary 3110 percent in February and March, rising to 14 percent by June

For county and town bills the cost steps up month by month: 5 percent in June and July, 7 percent in August and September, and 10 percent in the final quarter of the year.

What the Assessor can tell a seller

The Assessor estimates market value by comparing recent sales, by replacement cost, or, for rental property, by income. The first of those compares a property with similar homes that sold recently, and state law calls for every property in a town to be assessed at the same percentage of value.

Owners planning an addition or renovation can ask for a written estimate of how it would change the assessment. The request must be in writing, with drawings that mark what exists and what is new, a square footage breakdown, a narrative description and a cost estimate at market prices, even if the owner will do some of the work personally. Estimates usually arrive within a week.

Applications for senior, STAR and disability exemptions are due to the Assessor by June 1, and applicants must show Eastchester residency, so ask the office at Town Hall, 40 Mill Road, for its forms.

Permits and zoning approvals

The Zoning Law requires many development applications to win Planning Board approval before a building permit can even be requested. Some also need review by the Architectural Review Board, the Zoning Board of Appeals if a variance or special permit is involved, or the Sign Review Board. The Planning Department staffs all four and works from Town Hall at 40 Mill Road, Room 216.

  • Comments on a hearing item must reach the Secretary to the Land Use Boards by 4:00 pm on the business day before the meeting, or be handed to the board at the hearing.
  • The Building Department, also in Room 216, takes building permit applications.
  • Town Hall is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

Before listing, find out whether any past addition or sign went through the right board, because a buyer's attorney may ask to see those approvals.
