State transfer tax

New York State charges $2 for every $500 of consideration on a conveyance, and the TP-584 return is filed with the county clerk where the property lies. Residences priced at $1 million or more also trigger a 1 percent charge that the buyer pays.

If you owe taxes when you sell

Taxes that are late carry the penalties shown in the table, and the Receiver of Taxes also handles notices of tax lien sales. Phone that office before you accept an offer and ask what is owed today, penalties included. The amount is paid out of your proceeds at closing, so it belongs in your math from the start. Write the figure down with the date you called.

A seller who is behind on the April 30 bill is usually better off selling quickly than waiting, since the monthly steps keep climbing toward 14 percent. A cash buyer will factor the balance into the offer, and your attorney will make sure it is cleared at the table.

Preparing for a quick closing

Bring four documents to the first buyer conversation: the current tax bills, your mortgage statement, any written Assessor estimate for past work, and the approvals for additions. With those in hand a cash buyer can quote a price without a long inspection period.

The Receiver of Taxes can explain how taxes are apportioned between buyer and seller at the closing, which matters most when a sale lands between the April 30 and September 30 dates. The apportionment shows up as a line on the closing statement, so ask your attorney to walk you through it before you sign. Are Bronxville and Tuckahoe part of Eastchester?

Yes, both are incorporated villages located inside the Town of Eastchester. The town also includes an unincorporated area also called Eastchester.

When are school taxes due in Eastchester?

September 30 is the cutoff for the first half and January 31 for the second, both without penalty. The town's Receiver of Taxes collects for both the Eastchester and Tuckahoe districts.

What happens if Eastchester county and town taxes are paid late?

The cost rises with each month. May adds 2 percent, June and July 5 percent, August and September 7 percent, and the final quarter of the year 10 percent, with no charge through April 30.

Which office takes Eastchester exemption forms?

The Assessor's Office at Town Hall, 40 Mill Road. Exemption applications are due June 1, and applicants must show Eastchester residency.

Owners, renters and who buys in Ithaca

Renters outnumber owners in this university city, and only 29.6% of homes are owner-occupied. So the first thing to settle before a sale is whether your house has ever been a rental. That answer shapes who will bid and what the city will want to see.

Ithaca sits at the south end of Cayuga Lake in Tompkins County. The Town of Ithaca around it is a separate municipality, so confirm which one covers your address. The city has 33,632 residents, up 4.8% from the 2020 base of 32,085, in 14,167 households of about 1.71 people. Just 54.2% of residents were in the same house a year earlier, which tells you how often homes change hands here. Decide early whether your likely buyer lives in the house, wants rental income, or pays cash and takes the place as is.

  • Owner-occupied houses on East Hill, West Hill and South Hill tend to sell to people planning to live in them.
  • Houses near Collegetown, or with accessory apartments, attract investors who will ask about the rental certificate.
  • Houses needing work or holding tenants often move fastest to a cash buyer.

Prices and rents

The middle value of an owned home in the city is $342,700, and gross rent is $1,447 at the midpoint. Owners with a mortgage pay $2,368 a month, and those without one pay $994. Household income is $48,784 at the midpoint.

The city covers only 5.39 square miles of land, so housing is tight and a modest house can draw several showings in a good season. Buyers pay attention to walkable addresses, since the average commute is just 18.7 minutes and Cornell and Ithaca College supply most of the jobs. The hills matter too: East Hill, West Hill and South Hill each have their own feel, so ask an agent for sales on your own hillside.

If the house has accessory apartments or past student tenants, say so when you talk to buyers. Investors will price the rental paperwork into their offer, and owner-occupants will want to know what they are inheriting.

Rental certificates and short-term rentals

The city requires a housing inspection and a Certificate of Compliance for residential rentals, and a buyer who plans to rent will check that yours is current. The rule reaches one- and two-family dwellings, multiple dwellings, dormitories, fraternities, sororities, mixed-use buildings with apartments and accessory apartments in single-family homes.

Fees depend on building type. The Building Division bills the owner after the inspection, and payment is due within 30 days. Each property gets one 30-day extension to prepare for inspection or fix violations without added violation charges.

City of Ithaca Certificate of Compliance fees
Inspection itemFee

Two-family dwelling, initial inspection$175

Short-term rentals need a permit in addition to the certificate. It lasts one year, the permit number goes in every listing, a local contact must answer within 60 minutes, and hosts collect a 5% Tompkins County occupancy tax and a 5% City of Ithaca one. If your buyer wants to run the house as a short-term rental, ask the Building Division at 108 E. Green Street whether the permit transfers or must be reissued. Recording a deed in Tompkins County

The Tompkins County Clerk records deeds for Ithaca. The first page costs $50 and each added page $5. Residential deeds carry a $10 deed notice, and the TP-584 transfer tax return costs $5. Transfer tax is $6 per $1,000.

The RP-5217 real property transfer report costs $125 for residential property and $250 otherwise. A seller who lives out of state files form IT-2663, which the state revises every year, so use the current version. The clerk's counter takes cash or check.

Land record searches by clerk staff run $5 per name for records back to 1968, and copies are $0.65 a page with a $1.30 minimum. Your closing attorney or title company normally handles all of this. Just know that these Tompkins County amounts will not match a settlement statement from a sale elsewhere in New York.

Before closing, collect what the attorney will ask for: a copy of your deed, the current rental certificate if the house is a rental, any open violation notices, and your out-of-state form if it applies. Having these ready keeps the closing date from slipping while someone hunts for a document.

Winter and the hillside homes

Snow averages about 67 inches a year, so buyer inspectors look closely at roofs, gutters, foundations and heating systems. Expect questions about the furnace's age, whether pipes in exterior walls have ever frozen and how water leaves the lot after spring melt. A house without air conditioning still sells, but it may draw a lower offer.

  • Gather heating, roof and foundation records before the first showing.
  • Photograph the house in dry weather if the basement ever took on water.
  • Clear gutters and walkways before an inspection in cold months.

Is a cash offer a good fit for an Ithaca house?

Cash fits houses with rental violations, deferred repairs or tenants in place, because those problems slow a financed sale. A clean owner-occupied house in a sought-after neighborhood may do better on the open market.

Get any offer in writing. Ask how the buyer handles an expired Certificate of Compliance or open violations, and have a New York real estate attorney review the contract. Compare the price with what you would net after commission, repairs and several months of carrying costs. A student rental adds a timing question, so ask the buyer up front how existing leases would be handled.

The steps for a cash sale are short. You accept a written offer, the attorney and title company order a title search, you sign the deed and transfer forms, and the buyer pays at closing. Because no lender is involved, there is no loan approval or appraisal to wait on. If the house has an expired certificate, you and the buyer decide in the contract who schedules the inspection and who pays the fees listed above.

Frequently asked questions

Does Ithaca require a certificate before I sell a rental house?

The city requires a Certificate of Compliance for residential rentals, issued after a Building Division housing inspection. A buyer who will keep renting usually wants it current, so schedule the inspection early. Applications can be made online.

How much is a Certificate of Compliance for a one-family house in Ithaca?

The initial inspection is $100 for a one-family dwelling and $175 for a two-family. Each violation found adds $10 and each one still uncorrected at re-inspection costs $50. A return trip is $75 per hour with a $75 minimum.

What does it cost to record a deed in Tompkins County?

The first page is $50 and each added page $5. Add a $10 deed notice, a $5 TP-584 filing and the $125 RP-5217 fee for residential property. Transfer tax is $6 per $1,000.

Which municipality covers my Ithaca address?

The City of Ithaca and the surrounding Town of Ithaca are separate municipalities. Check your tax bill or ask the city Building Division before you start city paperwork such as a rental certificate.

Can I sell my Ithaca house if it has an Airbnb permit?

Yes. Ask the Building Division whether a new owner must apply for a fresh permit. The permit lasts one year, depends on a current Certificate of Compliance, and hosts collect separate 5% city and county occupancy taxes.

Selling a house in Clarence

Clarence is in the northeastern part of Erie County, northeast of Buffalo, and it has no incorporated villages. The town covers 53.63 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 32,950 residents, a 7.4 percent increase over 2010. Tonawanda Creek forms the northern boundary with Niagara County, and Amherst, Lancaster and Newstead are the neighbors to the west, south and east.

In Clarence you can hire an agent, sell it yourself, or accept an offer from a direct buyer such as our company. The right choice turns on the house's condition, your timeline and whether past work was permitted.

A useful first step is a walk around the house with the permit list above in mind. Decks, sheds, pools, generators and a reroof are the projects that most often turn out to lack paperwork, and a Clarence buyer's attorney will look for exactly those. Knowing the answer before you call a direct buyer keeps the price from shifting later.

Hamlets, schools and ZIP codes

Clarence is a collection of hamlets rather than one downtown. Clarence Hollow is the main district in the southeast, Clarence Center sits near the middle of town around Goodrich Road and Clarence Center Road, and Harris Hill occupies the southwest corner. Swormville, Millersport and East Amherst lie along the western and northern borders and extend into neighboring towns. Spaulding Lake is an upscale housing project built around a former quarry north of Main Street, and Rock Oak Estates is a 55-plus community on Main Street.

Most of the town is in the Clarence Central School District. Part of the town falls in Williamsville Central instead, which makes the parcel the thing to verify.

  • The ZIP codes in town are 14031, 14032, 14051 and 14221.
  • New York Route 5 (Main Street) crosses the southern half of the town.
  • Transit Road (Route 78) marks the west line, and Sheridan Drive (Route 324) ends at Main Street.

How to challenge a Clarence assessment

Clarence assesses property at 100 percent of full market value and gives owners a three-step path to contest the number. The informal review accepts applications from January 1 to March 28. Bring reasonable evidence based on market sales, and compare like with like: a five-year-old house is not a fair match for a fifty-year-old one, and neither is a house in a different neighborhood.

Step two is a hearing before the Board of Assessment Review on Grievance Day, held the fourth Tuesday in May (May 25 in 2027). Use form RP-524 for that board only, not for the informal review. Owners who still disagree can ask for a small claims assessment review, and the town posts SCAR instructions and an assessment timetable on its assessment cycle page.

The town also runs an online Property Record Online System for looking up parcel data and the informal review worksheets, which become available after January 1. Check your record there for errors before you list.

Tax due dates and penalties

The Town Clerk's office collects property tax in Clarence, from the Town Hall at One Town Place. Town and county bills go out by mid-January and are due on or about February 15. School bills go out by mid-September and are due on or about October 15. If your taxes are in escrow, you receive a receipt after the bank pays rather than a bill.

Town and county payment windowPenalty
February 16 to 281.5%
March 1 to 153.0%
March 16 to 314.5%
April 1 to 156.0%
April 16 to 307.5%

On May 1 a 7.5 percent penalty joins the levy, and 1.5 percent interest accrues monthly until unpaid taxes are sold in November, at which point the total reaches 18.78 percent. After June 30, unpaid town and county taxes move to Erie County Finance. School taxes carry a 7.5 percent penalty from October 16 to 31 and 9 percent in November, and unpaid school balances are re-levied onto the next town and county bill. The Clerk will take a partial payment in any amount.

If you sold a parcel, forward the bill to the new owner or call the Clerk so the office can locate them. Behind on taxes? The balance and any penalties are taken from your proceeds at closing, so ask the Clerk for the exact amount first.

Permits before you list

Clarence requires permits for new construction, additions, conversions, pools, decks, sheds, walls, reroofing, and for plumbing, heating, cooling and electrical changes, including generators. Fence and sign permits come from Planning and Zoning, and driveway permits come from the County, State or Town Highway Department. The Building Department is at 6221 Goodrich Road, and the Town Clerk collects permit fees.

Work done without a required permit may hold up the sale of your property and may affect an insurance claim, and the town can issue a stop work order. Every permitted project needs inspections and a certificate of occupancy or compliance before the space is used.

  • Plumbers working in town need a license from the Town.
  • The town keeps records of permitted projects, and copies are available through a Freedom of Information request.
  • Planning and Zoning answers variance questions.

Ask the Building Department for the file on your address early. It shows which permits were closed, which are still open and whether a certificate of occupancy exists. If your file has gaps, request the records before you accept an offer, so a buyer can compare your paperwork to the house as it stands.

Recording a Clarence deed at the Erie County Clerk

The Erie County Clerk records deeds for Clarence parcels. Submit an original deed, signed and notarized, that carries a legal description and a street address for every party. P.O. boxes are not accepted. A TP-584 tax affidavit goes in duplicate, and an RP-5217 transfer report is prepared on the state's site because its barcode cannot be reused from another transaction.

Fees are a $45 statutory recording fee, $5 per page, $10 to file the TP-584, and $125 for the RP-5217 on residential or farm property ($250 for other property). The seller pays New York State and Erie County transfer tax at filing. The two shares add up to $4.50 per $500 of price.

An affidavit drops the rate to $2.00 per $500 for sellers aged 62 or older who have lived in and owned their one or two-family house for at least a year. A one percent mansion tax is added at $1 million or more. Residential transfers also need a Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form delivered to the Clerk at the time of transfer, and the finished original deed is mailed back to you after indexing.

How many people live in Clarence, NY?

The 2020 census counted 32,950 residents, a 7.4 percent increase over the 2010 count of 30,673. Clarence has no incorporated villages.

When is Grievance Day in Clarence?

The fourth Tuesday of May, so May 25 in 2027. File form RP-524 for the Board of Assessment Review, or go through the earlier informal review if you just want the Assessor to take a second look.

Where do I pay Clarence property taxes?

Pay the Town Clerk at One Town Place, Clarence, NY 14031, by check, cash, mail or online. After June 30 unpaid town and county taxes move to Erie County Finance.

Do unpermitted repairs affect selling a Clarence house?

They can. A missing permit can stall a sale, complicate an insurance claim and bring a stop work order. Ask the Building Department what a project needs to be closed out.

How much is transfer tax in Erie County?

The combined State and Erie County rate is $4.50 per $500 of price, paid by the seller at filing. Eligible senior owners aged 62 or older can reduce it to $2.00 per $500.

Selling quickly in the Town of Manlius

You can hire an agent, sell on your own, or take a cash offer from someone who buys the house as-is. Only the cash route lets you pick the closing date and skip repairs.

East of Syracuse, Manlius competes with neighboring suburbs, and shoppers compare school district, lot size and drive time. An unfinished deck, a lapsed permit or a worn kitchen costs a house in that comparison. A cash buyer prices what is in front of them, which means no repair negotiation and no lender appraisal.

Start with four documents: the deed, your latest tax bill, permits for work done since you bought, and your lender's payoff letter. How fast you close depends on having them in hand.

Local market snapshot

Manlius leans toward homeowners and higher incomes. Population stands at 32,864, a 2.5 percent drop from 2020, and 81.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

A typical home value of $253,600 sits beside household income above $113,000. Buyers can afford to pay up for a house that is ready to move into. One that is not gets an inspection report listing every deferred item, then a lower bid.

Not sure what your house is worth? Have a local agent pull nearby sales and measure any cash bid against them before replying.

Villages, hamlets and school districts

Inside the town are three villages, Manlius, Fayetteville and Minoa, plus hamlets such as Eagle Village, Fillmore Corners, Kirkville, Mycenae, Fremont Heights and Fremont Hills. Your location within that map sets both price and the likely buyer.

  • Manlius village is near the southern boundary, where NY 92 meets NY 173.
  • Fayetteville is on the western edge at NY 257 and NY 5, close to the Fayetteville Towne Center plaza.
  • Minoa is in the north, and the Thruway cuts across that end of town.
  • Green Lakes State Park and the Old Erie Canal State Historic Park are outdoor features that often show up in listings.

The town splits among the Fayetteville-Manlius, East Syracuse-Minoa and Chittenango school districts, so tell buyers which one serves your lot. The district is printed on your tax bill. Many houses here went up during the suburban boom of the 1950s, so expect buyers to ask about the age of the roof, furnace and wiring.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Manlius house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Code rules that can come up in a sale

Work covered by the state Uniform Code requires a building permit from the Town Code Enforcement Officer. When a permitted job is finished or a building's use changes, the file closes with a certificate of occupancy or compliance. If you built a deck, finished a basement or put on a new roof, a buyer will want to see those records.

The town's Planning and Development page spells out these everyday rules:

  • A deck needs a permit whether it is attached or freestanding, though sealing it or replacing rotted treads does not.
  • A shed smaller than 144 square feet needs no building permit, but zoning setbacks still apply.
  • Inspections require 24 hours' notice and must be booked with town staff.
  • The zoning code lets you keep one unlicensed, working vehicle in the open and no inoperative vehicles.
  • FEMA flood maps are kept at Town Hall, and a flood-zone lot carries added building conditions.

Under Chapter 59 of the town code, a violation can draw a fine of up to $1,000 per day until it is fixed. An inherited house with unpermitted work is a case for a call to the Code Enforcement Officer, who can explain what closing the file takes. Many cash buyers will accept open items, which is why owners in that spot often look at this route.

Property taxes and exemptions

Two bills a year reach Manlius owners: school tax in September, then county and town tax in January. Both go to the Receiver of Taxes, and unpaid balances move on to the Onondaga County Finance Department.

The assessment year opens March 1, the taxable status date and last day for exemption filings. The tentative roll comes out May 1, Grievance Day lands on the fourth Tuesday in May, and the final roll is July 1. A grievance on form RP-524 must be in the town's hands by 8:00 PM that day. The exemptions on offer include senior, disability, veteran and firefighter or EMS exemptions, and STAR questions are handled by the state.

  • Onondaga County's Beacon system shows each parcel's inventory and sale history.
  • The Receiver accepts up to four partial payments on town and county tax and three on school tax.
  • Ownership changes reach the town slowly, so a new owner should tell the tax office where the bill goes.

Before listing or signing, find out whether any installment is still open and set the split with the buyer in the contract. Call the Assessor or the Receiver of Taxes for the current dates.

A bill you have not paid gets settled from your proceeds at closing, so get the exact balance from the Receiver of Taxes shortly before the date.

Recording the deed and paying transfer tax

The Onondaga County Clerk records Manlius deeds and also accepts the state transfer return, Form TP-584. Sellers carry the base tax of $2 per $500 of price.

Filing must happen within 15 days after the deed changes hands. A $1 million house brings the buyer an extra one percent. The clerk can quote the current recording fee before closing.

The lawyer or title agent on your file normally lodges these forms at closing. Check that the net sheet lists the transfer tax before you sign.

When is a cash sale the better move?

Cash works for sellers pinned down by a deadline or by the condition of the house. Around Manlius that tends to mean a parent's estate, open permit questions, a rental still occupied by a tenant, or a job move with no time to list.

Compare offers by what lands in your account, not by the headline number. Listing brings agent commission, repair demands after the inspection, months of mortgage and utility bills and the risk of a buyer's loan falling through. A direct sale generally gives up some price in return for certainty. Request a written closing date, proof of funds, and a line stating who covers the transfer tax.

An attorney should read the contract, and you should hold written confirmation that no repairs or credits are owed after you sign.

With an estate, the attorney will want the papers showing who may sign before any closing date is set. With a tenant in place, decide in advance whether the buyer takes over the lease or you hand over the house empty.

Frequently asked questions

How quickly can a Manlius house close for cash?

Often within a few weeks when title is clean. The payoff letter, the title search and any probate paperwork set the pace, and estates or houses with title defects run longer.

Is a certificate of occupancy needed to sell a Manlius house?

The code requires one for permitted work and for a change of use. When a permit was never closed out, talk to the Code Enforcement Officer. Lenders may insist on the certificate, and as-is buyers often do not.

What is the seller's transfer tax in Manlius?

It is $2 for each $500 of the price, reported on Form TP-584 at the Onondaga County Clerk.

When do I have to file a Manlius assessment grievance?

The RP-524 form must arrive by 8:00 PM on the fourth Tuesday in May. Exemption applications run on a separate March 1 deadline.

Which school district is my Manlius address in?

It is one of Fayetteville-Manlius, East Syracuse-Minoa or Chittenango. Your tax bill shows the district, and buyers will want it stated up front.

Where Salina is, and who buys homes there

Salina is a big suburban town just north of the city of Syracuse, on the shore of Onondaga Lake. It takes in Liverpool, Mattydale, Lyncourt, Galeville and a part of North Syracuse, and also includes areas such as Hinsdale, Long Branch and Pitcher Hill. Mid-2025 population is 32,375, a 2.6% dip from 2020, over 13.65 square miles of land.

Interstate 81 and the Thruway meet inside the town, NY 370 follows the lake, and US 11 crosses the east side. Commuters and airport-area workers shop here, and a piece of Syracuse Hancock International Airport sits in the northeast corner. A house inside the Village of Liverpool may also have village offices to deal with.

How quickly can I turn a Salina house into cash?

You can trade time for price in three common ways.

  • Hire a Realtor: expect staging, photos, open houses and a lender's appraisal. The listing may reach a higher number when the house shows well and you can wait.
  • Go it alone: advertise, screen buyers and write the contract with help from an attorney. You keep the fee but take on the work.
  • Accept a cash bid: there is no appraisal gap or loan approval, so you can pick the closing date. Houses with tenants, code issues or piled-up repairs usually fit.

The town keeps a vacant and foreclosure property registry with a registration fee, so an empty or distressed house costs more than taxes and upkeep. A faster exit trims those costs if the house is sitting idle.

Homes have a midpoint value of $160,500, and owners live in 68.7% of them. Around 20% of residents are 65 or older, and 87.4% stayed in the same house for the past year, so many buyers already have ties to the Syracuse area.

Tax bills and assessment challenges

The Tax Receiver collects on about 13,527 parcels. School taxes come due in September and October, for the three school districts that reach into the town. Town and county taxes come due between January and March.

Dates from the assessor's office:

  • March 1: deadline for every exemption application and renewal, and taxable status date.
  • May 1: tentative assessment roll filed.
  • Fourth Tuesday in May: Grievance Day, with the Board of Assessment Review in session.
  • July 1: final roll filed, and work on next year's roll begins July 2.

Payment choices: the county's online portal (3% convenience fee, $3 minimum), the mail, in person, or the outdoor drop box, where cash does not belong. Mail goes to the Town of Salina Receiver of Taxes at 201 School Road, Liverpool. A payment made outside the collection window is sent to the Chief Fiscal Officer, PO Box 1004, Syracuse, NY 13201-1004.

The assessor's office also offers informal reviews before the formal grievance, and it processes exemptions for seniors and volunteers.

Permits and registrations

Building and code enforcement sit under Planning and Development, which applies New York's building and residential codes. Pools, sheds, fences, decks, porches, generators, plumbing and heating changes and demolitions all need permits, and the permit application asks for a property survey, a form and a drawing. Projects over $20,000 need plans sealed by a New York engineer or architect.

For a seller, three checks come first:

  • Check any earlier deck or shed for a missing final inspection or certificate.
  • See whether the house is covered by the Vacant and Foreclosure Property Registry. The town runs it through Hera Property Registry, and owners, mortgagees or trustees register online and pay a fee.
  • Study the zoning map when the lot is close to a commercial corridor like US 11 in Mattydale.

Inspections must be requested at least one business day ahead, so schedule any open sign-offs before you list.

Clearing out a Salina house

Before you leave furniture at the curb, look at the town's news page for the Large Item Pick Up Schedule for 2026 and for yard waste notices. Stormwater notices are posted there as well, useful when you are clearing a yard or basement.

The Receiver of Taxes is at 201 School Road in Liverpool, which is also the town court's address, so one trip can cover a tax question and a court errand. Call the Tax Receiver at (315) 457-2710 for questions about bills; office hours and other phone numbers are on the town's department pages.

Deed and transfer tax in Salina

A Salina deed is recorded with the Onondaga County Clerk, which holds the county's real property records. Form TP-584, the state transfer tax return, goes to the same office, and the tax is due by the 15th day after the deed is delivered.

The tax is $2 for every $500 of price, counting any leftover part as a full $500, and it falls on the seller unless the contract says otherwise. A 1% buyer tax applies from $1 million, which rarely touches a Salina sale.

Steps to a smooth closing

Start with the town and school tax bills, then ask Planning and Development about earlier work that never got a final inspection. A vacant house also needs its registry status and fee confirmed. After that, pick a route: listing, sale by owner or cash bid. In every case the closing attorney needs a payoff from the Tax Receiver, the deed details and a completed TP-584 for the county clerk.

With cash, the closing date can follow your schedule since no lender must approve anything. The registry, permit and tax items still decide how soon the deed is recorded, so clearing them first keeps the date firm. If the house has tenants, mention that to the buyer early and ask the attorney how it affects showings.

If you think your assessment is too high

Start early. Once the tentative roll is filed on May 1, compare your value with the house's condition and with what similar houses are bringing. The assessor's office offers an informal review before the formal grievance, which costs nothing and can settle a small error quickly. If that does not work, bring your evidence to the Board of Assessment Review on Grievance Day, the fourth Tuesday in May. Exemptions, whether new or renewed, must reach the assessor by March 1, so a senior or volunteer exemption should be filed well before the roll appears. A buyer will see your assessment too, so a corrected figure can help the sale.

Can I sell a vacant house in Salina that is on the town's registry?

Yes. Registering is the duty of the owner, mortgagee or trustee, and it does not block a sale. A cash buyer can take the vacant house as it is, which also ends your registry cost.

Where do I send a Salina property tax payment?

Send it to the Town of Salina Receiver of Taxes, 201 School Road, Liverpool, NY 13088, or use the county portal, the counter or the drop box. A payment outside the collection season goes to the Chief Fiscal Officer, PO Box 1004, Syracuse.

When is Grievance Day in Salina?

It is the fourth Tuesday in May. The tentative roll is filed May 1 and the final roll July 1, so check your value as soon as the tentative roll appears.

Who pays transfer tax on a Salina sale?

The seller, unless the contract moves it. The rate is $2 per $500 of price, rounded up, and a 1% buyer tax starts at $1 million.

Does Salina require a permit for a deck or fence?

Yes. Fences, decks, porches, sheds and pools all need one. Before you list, ask Planning and Development whether earlier work ever got its final inspection.

Closing a Port Chester sale quickly

Line up the village paperwork first, then choose a buyer who can close on cash. A cash purchase drops the appraisal and loan commitment that often slow a closing, yet the deed, the state tax return and the village records still have to be finished.

Port Chester is a village within the Town of Rye in Westchester County, pressed against the Connecticut line. One sale touches the village hall, the town, the county clerk and a state tax form. The sections below follow the order a seller meets them.

Housing and buyers in Port Chester

The village counted 31,693 people in 2020, and the mid-2025 estimate is 32,303, within a land area of 2.33 square miles. It is densely built, with one and two family houses alongside apartment buildings. Owners live in 46.5 percent of the 11,056 households, so renters slightly outnumber owners. The median owned home is valued at $582,600, median gross rent is $2,028, and median household income is $92,222.

Because rent is high and ownership is under half, many buyers are landlords or owner-occupants of two-family houses who plan to rent one floor. That brings in the village rental registry described next. Trains from the village station reach Grand Central, Stamford and New Haven, and Bee-Line routes 13 and 61 run local buses, so commuters have a clear reason to look here.

Every address belongs to the Port Chester-Rye Union Free School District. Because the Sound is close, roof, gutter and basement condition draw attention during inspections.

Rental registry for two-family houses

Local Law I-5 of 2023 created Chapter 248, a registry for two-family dwellings that are rented and not owner-occupied. If one unit is owner-occupied or the house is vacant, no certificate is required.

  • A rental registry certificate lasts two years, and renewal papers are due 45 days ahead of the expiration date.
  • The certificate cannot be transferred. Anyone buying a rented two-family and keeping the tenants needs a new certificate when title closes.
  • The owner must tell the Department of Code Enforcement right away about a change in status, and an impending sale is one example.
  • The application costs $75, which covers the village inspection. Each re-inspection costs $150.
  • To register, the property needs no open code cases, no pending village enforcement proceedings, and current village taxes and special assessments.

Violations draw a fine of $500 to $5,000, up to 15 days in jail, or both penalties. If you own a tenant-occupied two-family house, ask the village whether your certificate is current before a buyer's attorney asks for it.

What does the Port Chester Building Department handle before closing?

The Building Department issues permits, schedules inspections, resolves notices of violation and handles the Municipal Search Report. Submit the search request form with a check made out to the Village of Port Chester.

The permit counter takes walk-ins on weekdays from 9 am to 1 pm, and phone messages are checked from 9 am to 4 pm. Permit records since February 2021 are digital in the village's Accela portal, while older files require a Freedom of Information request to the village clerk. One question on New York's disclosure form asks whether certificates of occupancy exist for the property, so an owner with an unpermitted porch, finished basement or extra kitchen should learn now what the file shows.

New York has revised its statewide building and energy codes. Work permitted years ago was inspected under older rules, and the department can explain what that means for a permit that is still open.

Village bills at sale: sewer rent

Sewer rent is the one many owners overlook. The village bills it apart from property tax, based on metered water use, with invoices mailed about every three months. A bill must be paid inside 25 days, a 1% penalty follows, and unpaid sewer rent attaches to the parcel as a lien under General Municipal Law section 452.

When a property changes ownership, notify the village and the water billing authority before the title closing, so a final reading can be taken and the new owner recorded. Do this early, since a missing final reading can hold up the payoff figure.

Your annual tax bill also carries a Port Chester Sewer Tax collected for Westchester County's treatment plant, a different charge from the village sewer rent. Get a written payoff from the village or your attorney so each charge shows up in the closing adjustments.

Deed recording and tax

Port Chester deeds are recorded by the Westchester County Clerk. The clerk takes a deed only with a PREP-generated cover page, Form TP-584, Form RP-5217 and a payment cover page showing fees and taxes.

The clerk's own illustration prices a three-page residential deed covering one municipality at $190. The return and payment are due within 15 days of the deed's delivery. A seller living outside New York must also deal with estimated income tax on the gain at filing.

What New York requires a Port Chester seller to disclose

Section 462 of the Real Property Law makes the seller of a house with up to four dwelling units sign a condition disclosure form and put it in the buyer's hands ahead of a binding contract. The same statute permits an "as is" sale, so the form and a discounted price can sit side by side.

For a house close to the water, read the flood questions with care. They ask about FEMA floodplain mapping, any flood insurance policy, and water that reached the basement from heavy rain or tidal flooding. A knowingly false or incomplete answer can expose the seller to claims before or after title passes.

Documents to gather

Before you contact buyers, collect the deed, your latest tax bill, the sewer rent account number and a recent bill, the rental registry certificate if you have tenants in a two-family house, and any permit paperwork for porches, basements or added kitchens. Ask your attorney who will file the deed packet with the county, and when. With those pieces in order, a cash buyer can set a closing date that holds, and you avoid last-minute requests from the title company.

Frequently asked questions

Must a landlord register a two-family house before selling it?

Only if it is rented and not owner-occupied. The certificate cannot be transferred, so the buyer applies for a new one at closing, and code enforcement should hear about the pending sale.

Who bears the state transfer tax in Port Chester?

The seller owes the base tax by default, and a contract can shift it. The buyer owes the 1% mansion tax at $1 million or more.

Which office records a Port Chester deed?

The Westchester County Clerk, through its PREP system. You need the deed, a TP-584, an RP-5217 and payment of the recording fee and taxes.

Will unpaid sewer rent follow the house to the buyer?

It can, because the unpaid amount attaches to the parcel. Ask the village for a final reading and a payoff figure ahead of closing so the adjustments cover it.

Can a house with open repairs still be sold in Port Chester?

Yes. New York allows as-is sales, but you still must hand over the signed disclosure statement before the buyer signs, and any open permits or violations are best sorted with the Building Department.

Ways to sell fast in Harrison

Harrison owners can list with an agent, sell privately, or accept an as-is cash purchase. Only the cash route skips staging, showings and renovation deadlines. Median home values here run above $1 million, so a rushed sale can cost real money. Hold any offer up against what comparable Harrison houses have sold for.

Harrison is a combined town and village in Westchester County, about 27 miles from Grand Central. That setup gives sellers one building department for the whole municipality, a Receiver of Taxes who collects several times a year, and a county clerk who records the deed.

  • Agent listing: works when the house is market-ready and you have time to spare.
  • Private sale: avoids the commission, but negotiation and paperwork fall on you.
  • Cash purchase: for estates, unfinished projects, tenant-occupied homes or a fixed deadline.

Housing and neighborhoods

Harrison had 32,273 residents in 2025, up from 28,218 in the 2020 count, living in 9,222 households of about 2.88 people. Owners occupy 60.5% of homes. The median owner-occupied value is $1,010,700, median rent is $2,616, household income is $164,250 and the commute averages 29.2 minutes. Because the median sits just over $1 million, many Harrison sales reach the level where the state's 1% mansion tax applies. The buyer pays it.

The town is shaped roughly like a figure eight. Downtown Harrison lies in the south, with Purchase and West Harrison to the north. Downtown breaks into Brentwood Plaza, Sunny Ridge, Sterling Ridge/The Trails and the Village part, with Halstead Avenue as its main street. West Harrison, around Lake Street and Silver Lake Park, has few road entrances. Purchase holds Manhattanville University and SUNY Purchase, and Westchester County Airport lies almost entirely within it. Harrison station on Metro-North's New Haven Line is the commuter link, and I-95, I-287, I-684, the Hutchinson River Parkway, NY 120, 120A and 127 cover the roads. The Bee-Line runs buses.

Much of the older housing dates from the 1920s through the 1950s. Sunny Ridge was laid out on a former farm after 1929, and most of its colonial revival and Tudor houses went up from the mid-1940s on. Owners of period homes should keep records of past renovations, since buyers of older houses ask for them.

School zones

The Harrison Central School District runs Harrison High School and Louis M. Klein Middle School, both downtown, plus four elementary schools. Purchase School covers Purchase and the north of West Harrison, Preston covers the Silver Lake area, Parsons covers south downtown, and Harrison Avenue School covers the rest of downtown. Elementary zones follow neighborhoods, so a Sunny Ridge address and a Purchase address feed different schools. Name the zone when you describe the house.

Assessment and tax calendar

The Assessor's Office keeps a record card on each of roughly 7,000 parcels and values them using current sales and cost, then the tax rate is applied to produce each bill. The Receiver of Taxes collects town, village, school, county and state tax from a single office in the Municipal Building.

Bills are mailed before the first of the month and must be paid by the month's last day. Mailing is a courtesy, and a lost bill doesn't excuse a late payment. Report a change of ownership to the tax office in writing.

Permits and certificates of occupancy

Harrison requires a building permit for new buildings, additions, alterations and accessory structures, and the Building Inspector issues the Certificate of Occupancy. A buyer's attorney will look for both on any house with visible improvements.

Most residential construction needs Architectural Board of Review approval. Permits also cover sheds, decks, pools, interior alterations, fences, driveways, tree removal, plumbing and electrical work. After new construction, additions, accessory structures, fences, walls or altered driveways, the department may ask for a final as-built survey. The Assessor learns of finished work from the permit and inspects with the Building Inspector before adjusting the assessment, so an unpermitted addition can show up as a code problem and a higher bill at once.

  • Collect permits and Certificates of Occupancy for each improvement.
  • Find the latest survey; the department wants 36 by 48 inches at standard size.
  • Counter hours run 9am to 5pm, and applications go in person or by mail, not electronically.

Recording a deed in Westchester

Harrison deeds are recorded by the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division. The fee schedule lists a $45 statutory fee, $5 per written page, $5 for the TP-584 form on residential property and $125 for the RP-5217 transfer report. The clerk steers filers to its PREP portal to work out the fees due.

New York's transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up, and the seller normally pays it. The 1% mansion tax at $1 million or more falls on the buyer.

Why records matter on an older house

A good share of Harrison's houses were built decades ago and have been added onto since. Each project leaves a trail: a permit, an inspection and, for larger work, a final survey and a Certificate of Occupancy. When a buyer's attorney sees an addition without that trail, the sale slows while someone sorts it out. The Building Inspector's office is the place to ask what is on file for your address, and it is much easier to ask before you list than during a contract.

Closing steps for a Harrison seller

After you accept an offer, your attorney sends a contract and the buyer's side orders title work. Missing permits or a missing Certificate of Occupancy will surface there, so gather those first. At closing you sign the deed and transfer forms, your lender's payoff comes out of the proceeds, and the deed goes to the county clerk. Cash buyers can often close sooner because there is no mortgage underwriting, but ask for the closing date, proof of funds and a split of costs in writing before you commit.

Tax proration follows the calendar above. A closing in spring or summer means school and town installments may be partly paid, so ask the Receiver of Taxes for a printout of what is open.

Frequently asked questions

Does Harrison have separate town and village taxes?

Harrison is one combined town and village, and the Receiver of Taxes collects both, with payments due in February and June. School tax is billed separately for January and September, and county and state tax in April.

When can a Harrison owner contest an assessment?

The grievance period runs from June 1, when the tentative roll is filed, to the third Tuesday in June. The Assessor sets May 1 as the date exemptions are due, and the final roll is filed September 15.

Is a permit needed for a deck or shed in Harrison?

Yes. Sheds, decks, pools and interior alterations all need permits, and most residential construction also needs Architectural Board of Review approval. The Building Inspector issues the Certificate of Occupancy.

What does the buyer pay on a million-dollar Harrison sale?

A 1% mansion tax applies when a residence sells for $1 million or more, and the buyer pays it. The seller covers New York's base transfer tax of $2 per $500, paid at recording.

Where is a Harrison deed filed?

With the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division. A recording needs the deed, form TP-584, form RP-5217 and the filing fees, which the clerk's PREP portal can calculate.

The Binghamton University campus sits inside the town, and Vestal has long worked as a residential suburb west of Binghamton. Population jumped from 2,848 in 1930 to 26,909 in 1970, so a large share of the housing went up during those decades. Hamlets include Ross Corners, Tracy Creek, Twin Orchards, Vestal Center and Willow Point, and the Vestal Parkway, NY Route 434, is the main retail strip.

Do Vestal landlords have to register rentals?

Yes. Under a local law announced in October 2025, owners of residential and rural rentals must register each one with the Vestal Police Department. Registration is free, and fines escalate for owners who skip it.

The registry names a contact person responsible for the care and upkeep of each rental, and it helps the Code Department pursue neglected properties. A landlord getting ready to sell should find out:

  • if the rental was registered, and under which contact;
  • if a code complaint is pending on the property;
  • and if the tenant has been told of the sale and what the lease allows for showings.

A buyer planning to keep it as a rental will want to know how the registry transfers after a sale, so bring it up early.

Paying Vestal property taxes

The Town Clerk doubles as Receiver of Taxes. Since the Town Board expanded the options in 2025, there are four ways to pay the town, county and school bill:

  • Taxlookup.net accepts e-checks and credit cards at any hour.
  • Checks can go in the secure drop box in the Police Department lobby at Town Hall.
  • Send payment by mail to the Town Clerk.
  • Walk in to the Town Clerk's Office on weekdays, 8:30 to 4:30, and pay with cash or a check.

The online tax lookup also pulls up tax-map details you will need for the deed. Call the Town Assessor for this year's exemption filing date and grievance dates, and get a payoff from the Receiver of Taxes before closing so nothing is left owing.

Documents to gather before closing

  • The latest bills from the town, the county and the school district.
  • A note from the Assessor on which exemptions, such as STAR, sit on the parcel and whether the buyer must file.
  • Permit records, plus your water and sewer account information.
  • The landlord registry status, if the house has been a rental.

With these in a folder before an offer lands, your attorney can go straight to the payoff and the deed forms. Add a copy of the current deed and the names of everyone who owns the house, so the transfer forms are filled out correctly the first time.

Broome County deed recording costs

Every deed for a Vestal parcel goes to the Broome County Clerk. Recording runs $45 plus $5 per page, which makes a two-page deed $55. Add $10 to file the TP-584 transfer tax return. The RP-5217 transfer report carries a charge of $125 on residential property and $250 on vacant land or commercial parcels. For an ordinary two-page residential deed, the clerk's total lands near $190.

The county's transfer tax rate is $5 per $1,000 of price, with $4 of it going to the state and $1 staying with the county. The seller covers all of it. Prices that fall between $500 steps are rounded up first.

  • Buyer and seller names should read identically across the deed, the TP-584 and the RP-5217.
  • Include a complete legal description, and have a notary acknowledge the sellers' signatures.
  • Submit originals only, since photocopies are refused.
  • A seller who lives out of state also files the IT-2663 nonresident estimated tax form.

Owners can sign up for the county's free Fraud Alert, which sends a notice whenever a deed or mortgage is recorded in their name.

Permits, zoning and town services

The town website lists a Code Department with downloadable building and code forms, the Town Codes, a zoning map, a Planning Board and a Zoning Board of Appeals. If you finished a basement, built a deck or changed a use, ask the Code Department which permits and certificates are on file for your address.

The Highway Department runs brush, leaf and holiday tree pickup, and the Water and Sewer office handles water and sewer billing. Buyers of a house on town water will ask who bills them, so keep recent statements handy. Families shopping in town will also look at the Vestal Central School District, so mention it in your listing.

From offer to closing in Vestal

After you accept an offer, the load is shared. Your attorney handles title work and the deed, you provide tax bills and permit records, the Receiver of Taxes issues the payoff figure, and the county files the deed once closing is done.

A mismatched name on the deed or the transfer forms means a return trip to fix it. The clerk also wants original signatures, so schedule signing with delivery of the paper in mind.

For a former or current rental, sort out the registry and the tenant's lease before signing a contract, because any buyer will ask.

What a cash sale skips

When title is clear and all owners agree, cash deals tend to wrap up within weeks. Nobody waits for a bank appraisal, and the buyer takes the house as is, so you skip repairs and staging.

Paperwork is what slows things. Tenants in place, an estate to settle or an open code complaint are the usual culprits.

A tidy folder speeds everything up. Before you talk to a cash buyer, you should know who is on the deed, whether anyone else must sign, which exemptions the Assessor shows on the parcel, and what the latest tax bills say.

The middle value for owner-occupied homes is $193,500. Rent runs about $1,199 a month, and about three in four homes are lived in by owners.

The Broome County Clerk in Binghamton. A deed costs $45 plus $5 a page, with a $10 TP-584 fee and a $125 RP-5217 fee for residential property.

Do I need to register a Vestal rental before selling it?

Yes. The town requires all residential and rural rental owners to register with the Vestal Police Department. Registration is free, but fines escalate for owners who skip it, so confirm yours is on file.

Orange County has two Newburghs. The city of Newburgh is a separate municipality on the river, independent of the town since it was rechartered in 1865. This page covers the town. If your deed or tax bill says Newburgh, confirm which municipality issued it before you look up dates and rules.

About 31,825 people live in the town, in 11,640 households averaging 2.71 people. Nearly four in five homes, 79.8 percent, are owner-occupied. Median home value is $375,700 and median gross rent is $2,159. Turnover is low, since 93.1 percent of residents lived in the same home a year earlier.

Land, lots and older houses

The town covers 43.36 square miles, hilly in the middle and bounded on the east by the Hudson River. Steep bluffs line most of the shoreline, so few houses have easy river access. Named areas include Balmville, Gardnertown, Orange Lake, Fostertown and Algonquin Park, which holds the town's only historic district, built around old gunpowder mills.

On hilly lots, a survey and a look at drainage are worth doing before you list. The housing stock spans farmhouses to 1980s developments, since the town stayed rural into the twentieth century and postwar years turned farmland into subdivisions. If your house is on a private road, find out who plows and repairs it before you list. Most roads are maintained by the town highway department, two are county roads, and the town also has many private roads.

Highways and the airport

Two interstates cross here: I-84 east to west and the New York State Thruway (I-87) north to south, joined by a direct ramp that opened in December 2009. Route 300 is the commercial strip, and Routes 9W, 17K, 32, 52 and 207 also pass through. Stewart International Airport sits partly in the town, though mostly in New Windsor. Commuters value that access, so put it in the listing.

School districts and who collects school tax

Property tax comes from the Receiver of Taxes, though school tax depends on your district. Four districts serve the town: Marlboro, Wallkill, Valley Central and the Newburgh Enlarged City School District. Who collects the school bill depends on the district:

The town has 13,027 taxable parcels. The Receiver does not allow partial payments or installments on property tax, so the January amount is the full bill and penalties start if you pay in February or March.

Four water and sewer bills arrive each year, and a 5 percent penalty applies after 30 days. Whatever stays unpaid is carried onto next year's property tax bill, so clear any water balance by closing.

Exemptions, permits and the deed

Exemptions run through the Assessor: STAR, military service, senior citizen, disability and agricultural. Find out which ones your parcel carries. Its page links the state's Basic and Enhanced STAR credit registration and the forms for the other exemptions. The Code Compliance Department issues building permits and certificates of occupancy for new and existing structures and investigates code complaints.

Recording is done by the Orange County Clerk, who also receives the state transfer tax return, Form TP-584, within 15 days after delivery of the deed. How a sale moves from offer to closing

After you accept an offer, the buyer's attorney requests a contract and a title search is ordered. The search looks for unpaid taxes, water and sewer balances and any lien on the property. A buyer who needs a mortgage adds an appraisal and an inspection, and the lender may ask for repairs or paperwork that stretches the schedule. A cash buyer skips those steps, so the closing depends mainly on title work and your own timing.

Plan for the property tax split. Because the Receiver does not accept installments, the January bill is a single payment, and your closing date decides how much of the year each side covers. Your attorney will work out the proration and put it on the closing statement. Keep the water and sewer receipts, since unpaid amounts roll onto the next tax bill.

Why timing matters on a Newburgh sale

Newburgh's calendar rewards planning. If you list in the spring, the March 1 exemption deadline and the May 1 tentative roll are close behind, and a buyer who closes in summer will want to know what the July 1 final roll shows. A sale closing in the fall lands near the September school tax due date for Marlboro and Valley Central, with a penalty in October. A winter closing falls before the January bill is due in full. Whichever season you choose, ask the Receiver for the current status of every bill and put the split in writing.

Getting a Newburgh house ready to sell

Start the work a month before you want to close. Pull together your deed, a current tax bill, your last school bill, and the water and sewer statement. Ask Code Compliance whether any permit for past work is still open. Because most owners here stay for years, many houses have had additions or finished basements over time, and a buyer's lawyer will ask for the permit record. If repairs look expensive, compare a listing against a cash offer by what you keep after repair costs, carrying costs and taxes. A cash buyer can skip the appraisal and the lender's repair list, so closing can follow your own timeline.

Walk the property with a notebook and list every repair you know about, large or small, so each buyer hears the same story. Before closing, request payoff figures for property tax and for water and sewer, and ask your attorney to confirm who pays each balance and how it is divided by the closing date.

It is for the town, estimated at 31,825 residents in 2025. The city of Newburgh is a separate municipality and is not included in that figure.

When is Grievance Day in the town of Newburgh?

The fourth Tuesday in May. The tentative roll comes out May 1, and the final roll is filed July 1.

Who collects school tax in the town of Newburgh?

It depends on the district. The town's Receiver collects for Marlboro and Valley Central, while Wallkill and the Newburgh Enlarged City School District use their own collectors.

Can I pay Newburgh property tax in installments?

No. Installments and partial payments are not allowed for property tax, so the January amount is the full bill, and penalties start if you pay in February or March.

Do unpaid water bills affect a Newburgh house sale?

Yes. Unpaid water and sewer bills are added to the next year's property tax bill, so settle them at or before closing.

Know your hamlet, your district and your assessment before talking numbers.

The Town of Warwick fills the southwestern tip of Orange County along the New Jersey line. It spans about 105 square miles and counted 32,027 residents in 2020. Inside it are three incorporated villages (Warwick, Florida and Greenwood Lake) and hamlets that include Amity, Bellvale, Edenville, Pine Island, Sterling Forest and Wisner.

Homes and land across the town

Housing ranges from village streets to lake communities to farmland. Land around Pine Island and Hoopstick sits in the Black Dirt region, known for fertile soil, and Greenwood Lake straddles the New York and New Jersey border. The Appalachian Trail passes through town.

Because the lots vary so much, tell buyers exactly what comes with yours: village sewer or septic, lake access, acreage and how far it sits from the village center.

School district and commute

Most of the town lies in the Warwick Valley Central School District. Other parts belong to the Florida Union Free School District, the Greenwood Lake Union Free School District and the Tuxedo Union Free School District. Families usually ask which school their children would attend, so confirm your district before you list instead of guessing from the mailing address.

NY 17A and NY 94 carry most traffic, and Warwick Municipal Airport serves the town. New Jersey Transit buses 196 and 197 run to Manhattan, and a Warwick inter-municipal bus also serves the town.

Warwick's community preservation transfer tax

Warwick charges a transfer tax of three-quarters of one percent on property sales, and the buyer pays it. Voters approved it by referendum in November 2006, and it has applied to conveyances since April 1, 2007, including those inside the villages. The money goes into a fund for open space, farmland, recreation, water resources and historic structures.

The first $100,000 of the price of improved property is exempt, and so is the first $50,000 for unimproved land. The town's own transfer tax form goes to the county clerk with the standard state form, and the deed is not recorded until both are in. Orange County's deed page lists a $5 fee for the Community Preservation Fund form and refers Warwick filers to the town for it.

Because the buyer carries this cost, ask any buyer whether the offer already accounts for it.

Assessments and property tax

The Town Assessor's office in Town Hall, 132 Kings Highway, sets assessments. Warwick's 2026 assessments sit at a uniform level of 7.65 percent of full value as of July 2025, so a low assessed value says nothing about market value. Exemption applications are due March 1 each year, and the office begins taking the next year's applications in July.

An informal review can be requested before the town files its tentative roll on May 1, and the town suggests asking by March 15. Formal complaints go to the Board of Assessment Review on the fourth Tuesday of May.

The Receiver of Taxes collects real property tax from January through March and school tax from September through October. Unpaid taxes go to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance at 255 Main Street in Goshen. Ask for a current bill and a payoff figure before closing.

Building permits and certificates

The Building Department enforces the state and town building codes and issues certificates of occupancy, which the town requires for all building in Warwick. Its office is in Town Hall and is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4:00. A five-member Zoning Board of Appeals hears requests for relief from the zoning laws. Three separate filings meet at closing, and each goes to a different place. The buyer's attorney or title company sends the deed, the TP-584 and the RP-5217 to the Orange County Clerk, the town's own transfer tax form travels with them, and the Receiver of Taxes provides the payoff for any open town bill.

Start with the town form, since the clerk will not record the deed until both the town and state forms are in. Ask the Town Assessor which exemptions sit on the parcel, and check whether the house is inside a village, because the transfer tax applies there too. Put the answers in writing and hand them to your attorney, who can then close without calling you back for each missing item.

Is a cash offer a good fit?

A cash offer fits when speed or condition matters more than the top price. Houses that struggle with a bank appraisal, such as ones with deferred repairs or an estate that has not settled, are the usual candidates. A cash buyer also works without a lender's timetable.

Whichever route you take, gather the deed, the tax bill, permit records and certificate of occupancy before the first showing, so the contract stage is short.

The buyer pays it. Warwick's community preservation tax is three-quarters of one percent of the price, with the first $100,000 of an improved property exempt. The seller still owes the state deed tax of two dollars per five hundred dollars.

A tornado rated EF2 hit the center of the city on July 16, 2024, damaged roofs and brick buildings, and prompted emergency declarations from the city, county and state.   • Price out a cash bid for a home with postponed repairs, storm damage, tenants or a probate matter.

Getting the paperwork ready

Rome's local steps add up, so line them up before an offer arrives. Ask Code Enforcement whether any permit for past work was left open, especially windows, decks, porches or a pool. Find the most recent city, school and county bills, and call the Treasurer's Office if one never arrived. Set aside time for the assessor's stamp on the deed, then file at the Oneida County Clerk.

A cash sale does not wait on a lender's appraisal, so these steps are usually what sets the pace. If the house is in probate or has tenants, say so at the start, since it changes who has to sign and when the house can be shown.

Taxes and water when you sell mid-year

Because Rome's calendar mixes city, school and county taxes, a sale rarely lands neatly between bills. The city tax and the school tax each run in two halves, April 30 and October 31, but the halves are swapped: April 30 carries the city's first half and the school's second half, while October 31 carries the city's second half and the school's first. County tax is due February 28. Metered water and sewer are billed on January 31 and July 31.

Ask your closing attorney to work out in writing which of these are paid and which fall to the buyer. Special assessments and metered water charges can ride on the January 31 bill, so a final water reading is worth requesting before the keys change hands. If any bill is unpaid at closing, it comes out of your proceeds, which is easier to handle when the Treasurer's Office has given you the exact balance beforehand. Keep copies of every payment receipt in the same folder as the bills, because the buyer's attorney may ask to see them.

Does a Rome deed need a stamp from the city assessor?

Yes. The Oneida County Clerk requires deeds for Rome properties to be stamped by the Rome City Assessor before recording. Allow time for that step before closing.

Does the 2024 tornado affect how I sell a Rome house?

It can. An EF2 tornado crossed the city on July 16, 2024, and damaged roofs and brick buildings. Keep repair invoices and permits to show a buyer.

Which school district serves a Rome address?

The Rome City School District covers most of the city and runs Rome Free Academy. Oriskany, Sherrill and Westmoreland districts cover other parts, so look at the tax bill.

Whom do I contact if a Rome tax bill never arrives?

Call the City Treasurer's Office at 315-339-7689 for a duplicate. Checks go to the City of Rome at 198 North Washington Street.

Is a permit required for window replacement in Rome?

Generally yes. New windows are among the work that needs a permit because of energy code and egress rules, and doubled fees apply if work starts first.

One local step comes first. Confirm whether your address is in the unincorporated Town, the Village of Mamaroneck or the Village of Larchmont, because the building and tax offices you deal with depend on it.

If you list, expect buyers at this price level to bring an inspector and to ask for repairs or credits for each deferred item. A private sale saves the commission but puts the screening, the negotiation and the follow-up on you. A cash sale ends at the contract and the closing, with no repair talks in between, though the price is usually lower than a well-prepared listing would reach.

Town, villages and water

The Town of Mamaroneck covers 14.07 square miles in Westchester County, and 7.41 of those are water, which is 52.85% of the total. It contains two villages, Larchmont and the Village of Mamaroneck, though part of the Village of Mamaroneck lies in the neighboring Town of Rye. Most of the town's land is unincorporated, yet most residents live inside the villages.

Much of the unincorporated area receives mail through the Larchmont Post Office, so a Larchmont mailing address does not tell you which municipality governs the lot. The Town Center is at 740 West Boston Post Road.

Because so much of the town is water, ask early whether your lot sits in a flood zone. A buyer's lender will check, and the answer can change the insurance quote and the offer. Gather any elevation certificate, past claim records and receipts for flood protection work before you list, so you can answer the question the same day it is asked.

Assessment calendar and grievances

Grievances run from June 1 to the third Tuesday of June each year. The next window opens June 1, 2027 and ends June 15, 2027, when the Board of Assessment Review sits.

  • May 1: taxable status date, the day ownership and condition are measured and the deadline for exemption applications.
  • June 1: the tentative roll goes online and in the office, and change-of-assessment notices are mailed to all owners, even those with no change.
  • Third Tuesday in June: the office must have every grievance in hand by then, delivered or mailed. A postmark does not rescue a late one, and email does not work.
  • September 15: the final roll appears and filing opens for Small Claims Assessment Review petitions.

The valuation date is July 1 of the prior year, so a roll reflects what a property was worth in mid-summer of the year before. The assessor's office reviews every property transfer for accuracy, using the RP-5217 form signed at closing, and corrects the sale information it records.

If you plan to challenge your assessment before you sell, the timing matters. A grievance filed in June affects the roll the new owner inherits, and the paperwork must be in the office on time. Missing the window means waiting a full year, so decide early whether the possible savings justify the effort, and tell the buyer if a case is pending.

Building permits and flood maps

The Town's Building and Code Enforcement department takes permit applications online through the OpenGov Viewpoint portal, and first-time users must create an account. It issues permits for new construction, additions, alterations, plumbing, signs, erosion control and tree removal. Many jobs need a second approval from Engineering for erosion and sediment control, the Highway Department for work in the road, or the Environmental Planner for trees.

Work must meet the 2025 building standards. The Town also adopted the 2020 NYStretch Energy Code and the 2025 Energy Conservation Construction Code, applying whichever provision is stricter for each component.

With more than half the town's area under water and a recorded elevation of zero feet, flood maps matter here. The department links to the FEMA Flood Map Service Center and to FEMA's guidance on changing a flood zone. Check your parcel on the map before listing, and keep any elevation certificate nearby.

Before listing, ask Building and Code Enforcement whether any open permits show on your address. A closed permit with a final sign-off is the cleanest answer a buyer's attorney can get. If you find an open one, finishing it before you list usually takes less time than negotiating around it after an offer.

Westchester deed fees and transfer tax

The Westchester County Clerk applies the state's $2 per $500 of price. A buyer at a residential price of $1 million or more adds the 1% mansion tax.

A residential deed carries a $45 recording fee, $5 a page, a $5 TP-584 filing and a $125 RP-5217 filing. The clerk asks filers to calculate exact amounts in its Property Records Electronic Portal, and taxes can be paid by ACH, cash, check or money order.

Once the sale closes, end your STAR registration and let the buyer register for their own credit. Your attorney or title company normally handles the filings, so expect to sign the deed and transfer forms and little else.

On closing day the attorney will adjust taxes between you and the buyer, collect the transfer tax from the seller's proceeds, and file the deed. Ask for a written net sheet ahead of time so each charge is listed before you sign.

Preparing for a fast sale

Speed in Mamaroneck depends on paperwork more than anything. Confirm your municipality, pull the permit file for any deck, addition or finished space, and check your parcel on the flood map. Ask your lender for a payoff letter and collect your latest tax statements.

A cash buyer skips the lender and the appraisal, so these papers set the pace. Compare any offer with what a listing would net after commission, repairs and months of carrying costs, and have a New York attorney read the contract before you sign.

Frequently asked questions

Is Mamaroneck a town or a village?

Both exist. The Town of Mamaroneck contains the Village of Larchmont, part of the Village of Mamaroneck and a large unincorporated area. Check which one governs your address before contacting a building or tax office.

When must a Mamaroneck grievance be filed?

By the third Tuesday of June. The next window runs from June 1 to June 15, 2027. The office takes grievances in person or by mail, never by email.

Which dates set a Mamaroneck assessment?

Assessments reflect property condition and ownership on May 1, and values are based on market value on July 1 of the prior year.

Does Mamaroneck require a permit for home work?

Yes for new construction, additions, alterations and plumbing, and the department invites owners to call if unsure. Filing happens in the online permit portal, and some projects also need engineering, highway or tree approvals.

Who pays the transfer taxes on a Mamaroneck sale?

The seller pays the state's $2 per $500 unless the contract moves it. The buyer pays the 1% mansion tax once a residential price reaches $1 million, a figure the town's midpoint home value already exceeds.

School districts and school tax bills

Collection windows differ. Middletown collects from October through February, while Pine Bush, Valley Central, Goshen and Minisink list September and October. Town and county tax due dates

Town and county bills go out around December 30 from the Receiver of Taxes, whose office handles over 10,000 of them. Payment runs in three stages:

  • January 1 to 31: no penalty.
  • February 1 to 28: 1 percent penalty.
  • March 1 to 31: 2 percent penalty.

Partial payments and installments are refused, and by law the office cannot accept anything after March 31. Whatever is unpaid on April 1 is returned to the Orange County Commissioner of Finance in Goshen.

Under Real Property Tax Law section 992, a missing bill does not cancel the tax or the fees that follow. Call the Receiver of Taxes if nothing has arrived by early January. Paying on time in January avoids any penalty at all.

Assessor, exemptions and grievances

The Assessor maintains the roll behind town, county, school, fire district and library taxes and handles exemptions: STAR Basic and Enhanced, military service, low-income senior, disability with limited income, agricultural, clergy, not-for-profit and firefighter. Applications are due March 1. Anyone who bought after 2015 registers for STAR with the state.

Disputing an assessment means filing Form RP-524, the Complaint on Real Property Assessment, between May 1 and Grievance Day, the fourth Tuesday in May. Filing sets your appointment time, and the Board of Assessment Review mails its decisions on July 1.

Owners are responsible for keeping their mailing address, escrow account and property inventory accurate with the Assessor. After closing, send over the new owner's mailing address so the next bill reaches the right person.

Transfer tax is calculated on the total consideration and added.

Cash and checks are the only accepted payments. Personal checks above $250 are refused, and any business, attorney or title company check above $10,000 has to be certified or replaced with a money order.

The clerk's office examines documents for recording requirements but not for legal sufficiency, so have your closing attorney review the deed first.

  • Your STAR registration status, since owners who bought after 2015 register with the state.
  • Permits and certificates of occupancy for renovations.
  • The current deed; the Orange County Clerk can provide a copy.
  • Lease copies for any tenant who will stay past closing.

Once those are in your attorney's hands, the payoff request to the Receiver of Taxes and the TP-584 and RP-5217 can be prepared without further input from you.

If tenants will remain after closing, bring their lease copies to the attorney as well. A buyer who plans to keep them needs the terms, and a buyer who wants the house empty needs to know that early. Either way, tell the tenants about the sale before the first showing, and ask them how much notice they need. Showings go more smoothly that way.

Building permits and certificates

You will find Building and Code Enforcement at Town Hall, where forms are posted, including demolition application documents for 2026. Should a previous owner have added a deck, finished a basement or built an addition, find out which permits and certificates of occupancy exist for the address before pricing the house.

Lenders and buyers' attorneys check whether what was built matches what was permitted. Any difference can slow closing or prompt a lower offer, and resolving it before listing keeps the timeline under your control.

What a cash sale skips

Cash buyers need no lender appraisal or loan approval and take the house as is, so you can drop the repair list and most staging. The legal side is unchanged, because a tax payoff, a deed, transfer forms and county recording are needed in every sale.

A workable order for a Wallkill seller: identify the school district, ask the Assessor about exemptions and STAR, check permits with the Building Department, get a payoff from the Receiver of Taxes, then give the closing attorney the deed details. January 1 to 31 without penalty, with 1 percent added in February and 2 percent in March. The Receiver of Taxes cannot accept payment after March 31.

The fourth Tuesday in May. File the RP-524 complaint form from May 1 through that day, make an appointment, and expect the Board of Assessment Review's decision on July 1.

Population was 31,065 in mid-2025, up 1.8% from 2020, and 91.0% of residents had not moved in the past year, so most neighbors stay put.

Communities include Carman, Cold Brook, Colonial Manor, South Schenectady, Rotterdam Junction and Pattersonville. Colonial Manor was built out in the 1950s and is one of the larger suburban pockets.

Which selling route fits a homeowner on a deadline?

The route that fits depends on whether you value the highest possible price, the lowest effort, or the earliest closing date.

  • Agent listing: makes sense for a tidy house if you can sit through showings, an appraisal and a buyer's loan approval. Request a written net sheet that shows commission and closing costs.
  • For sale by owner: saves the commission, though you take on pricing, inquiries and contract details, usually with an attorney.

Which office bills Rotterdam property tax?
